title: CreateWalls crashes Archicad on a zero-length wall (begCoordinate == endCoordinate)
body:
## Summary

`CreateWalls` with a wall whose `begCoordinate` equals `endCoordinate` (zero-length / degenerate wall) **crashes Archicad** instead of rejecting the input. Observed reproducibly on **Archicad 26 (Win)** during a batched `CreateWalls` call: after a number of valid walls, the first zero-length entry takes Archicad down (process exits, the Python client then fails with a connection reset on the next command).

This is nasty because a single bad coordinate pair in an otherwise-valid batch aborts the whole session and can lose work.

## Environment

- Tapir 1.5.3 (AC26 Win); also relevant for other versions
- Native JSON server → `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` → `TapirCommand.CreateWalls`

## How it happens

Source plans whose corner axes collapse during processing can produce wall segments where `beg == end`. Such entries pass schema validation (both coordinates are present and well-formed) and are handed straight to `ACAPI_Element_Create`, which crashes on the degenerate geometry rather than returning an error.

A batch with even one such wall crashes; the same batch with the zero-length entries removed completes fine.

## Root cause

`CreateWallsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`) reads `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate` and assigns them to `element.wall.begC`/`endC` without checking that they differ. There is no degeneracy guard before `ACAPI_Element_Create`.

## Suggested fix

Reject zero-length walls in the handler so the bad item returns an error (and is skipped) instead of crashing — using the existing `IsSame2DCoordinate` helper:

```cpp
API_Coord begCoordinate = Get2DCoordinateFromObjectState (*parameters.Get ("begCoordinate"));
API_Coord endCoordinate = Get2DCoordinateFromObjectState (*parameters.Get ("endCoordinate"));

if (IsSame2DCoordinate (begCoordinate, endCoordinate)) {
    return CreateErrorResponse (APIERR_BADPARS, "Zero-length wall: 'begCoordinate' and 'endCoordinate' are identical.");
}
```

Because `CreateWalls` is array-in / array-out, the offending wall then yields an `ErrorItem` in its slot and the rest of the batch still succeeds — no crash. I have this change ready and can open a PR if you'd like. (`ModifyWalls` may deserve the same guard for `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate` edits.)
author: weltmaister

title: feat(stories): return per-story height from GetStories
body:
Adds a computed `height` to each story in the `GetStories` response, so callers can read back floor-to-floor storey heights (previously only `level` was returned, and there was no way to verify a storey height set via `SetStories`).

`API_StoryType` does not store a height — the DevKit notes it "should be calculated based on neighboring stories". So `height` is computed as **the next story's level minus this story's level**. The topmost story has no story above, so `height` is omitted there. The `StoryParameters` response schema documents the field.

Built clean on AC28.
author: weltmaister

title: feat(walls): support curved walls via arcAngle in CreateWalls/ModifyWalls
body:
Adds an optional `arcAngle` (radians) to `CreateWalls` and `ModifyWalls` so curved walls can be created/edited — previously only straight walls were possible.

A curved wall in Archicad is an `APIWtyp_Normal` wall with a non-zero `angle` (the `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate` are the chord endpoints). The change writes `element.wall.angle`:
- **CreateWalls** — sets it in `SetTypeSpecificParameters` (wall stays `APIWtyp_Normal`).
- **ModifyWalls** — sets it in `ApplyWallDetails` with the `API_WallType` `angle` mask, next to `begC`/`endC`.

This mirrors the existing `CreateBeams`/`ModifyBeams` `arcAngle` → `curveAngle` convention, and is symmetric with `GetDetailsOfElements`, which already reports a wall's `arcAngle`. `arcAngle` is optional (no breaking change). Built clean on AC28.

title: Add drawIndex repositioning to SetDetailsOfElements
body:
_Since this is a workaround for an Archicad limitation, it may not meet the quality standards we want for Tapir, in which case we may choose not to include it.
I’ve also discovered some pretty surprising limitations related to Archicad (not even a C++ API issue) in this regard. I now understand better why there isn’t a direct command to change the display order. The modified command attempts to work around these limitations._

## What this does

Adds `drawIndex` support to `SetDetailsOfElements`. Setting `drawIndex`
via `ACAPI_Element_Change` is silently ignored by ArchiCAD (confirmed
Graphisoft bug in AC27), so repositioning is implemented via
`ACAPI_Grouping_Tool`.

## Implementation

**Normal elements** — two strategies, cheapest (fewest API calls) wins:
- *Direct*: step-by-step `BringForward` / `SendBackward`
- *ViaReset*: `ResetOrder` to class default, then step to target

**Door / Window / Skylight** — special host manipulation:
ArchiCAD enforces a hard minimum of level 7 for openings embedded in a
host (Door/Window in Wall, Skylight in Roof or Shell). Levels 8–14 are
reached by stepping the host element up (the opening follows), then
stepping it back down (the opening stays elevated). Reset (`drawIndex=0`)
on an elevated opening must also go through the host. The host is found
via a forward scan of all walls/roofs/shells with
`GetConnectedElements`. Within each batch, openings are processed before
all other elements so the host manipulation always starts from the
host's natural position.

**Dead ends (do not reintroduce):**
- `APITool_BringToFront` — unreliable on Wall and its sub-elements
- `APITool_SendToBack` — does not reliably reach level 1 in sparse files

## Known limitations

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Door/Window/Skylight, levels 1–6 | Unreachable (ArchiCAD constraint, min = 7) |
| Opening below its host's current level | Unreachable |
| Multiple openings in the same host, different targets, same batch | All end up at the same level (last processed wins) |
| `Opening` (API_OpeningID, generic void) | Fully immovable — all Grouping_Tool calls are no-ops; ArchiCAD displays level 0 for these elements |
| Morph / Railing / PolyLine, `drawIndex=0` | `ResetOrder` is a no-op; simulated via step-by-step to class default |

title: Archicad crashes when setting GDL parameters on Curtain Wall Panel subelements (SetGDLParametersOfElements)
body:
**Environment**

- Archicad version: 29.0.0
- OS: Windows
- Tapir version: 1.5.0
- Grasshopper node used: SetElementGDLs

**Description**
Archicad consistently crashes (force-closes) when using the SetGDLParametersOfElements command (exposed in Grasshopper as the SetElementGDLs node) to write a GDL parameter value to a Curtain Wall Panel subelement. The crash happens regardless of which GDL parameter or which panel is targeted.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Get a Curtain Wall element GUID using ElementsByType (ElementsType = CurtainWall).
2. Use the Subelements node with SubelementType = CurtainWallPanel to get the GUIDs of the panels (confirmed working, returns valid panel GUIDs).
3. Flatten the SubelementGuids output and isolate a single panel GUID using List Item (confirmed: a single, valid GUID is passed forward — verified visually in a Panel component).
4. Confirm that GetGDLParametersOfElements can successfully READ the parameter on this panel GUID (e.g. parameter "BMlaag2", type "BuildingMaterial", value 135) — this read operation works correctly.
5. Connect the single panel GUID to SetElementGDLs → ElementGuids.
6. Set ParameterName to a valid parameter name copied directly from the GetGDLParametersOfElements output (e.g. "BMlaag2").
7. Set Value to a valid value (tested with both an Integer parameter and a BuildingMaterial index, e.g. 135 or 136 — both material indices confirmed to exist in the project's Attribute Manager).
8. Click "Execute".
9. Archicad crashes immediately (force-closes). No error message or Bug Report detail is shown — only a generic crash dialog asking to describe what happened.


**Expected behavior**
Either the parameter is written successfully, or the command returns a controlled error message (e.g. "parameter not editable on subelements") instead of crashing the application.

**Additional notes**

- The same SetElementGDLs node, with the same parameter types (Integer and BuildingMaterial), works correctly without any issue when targeting independent GDL Objects (not Curtain Wall subelements), using GUIDs obtained via the SelectedElements node.
- This isolates the issue specifically to writing GDL parameters on Curtain Wall Panel subelements (hierarchical elements), not to the parameter type, value, or general node usage.
- The crash is 100% reproducible — it occurs every time, regardless of which specific parameter or which specific panel is targeted.
- No detailed Bug Report / Bug ID is available after the crash; only the generic Archicad crash dialog appears.
author: kushya-oss

title: BUG: CreateSlabs crashes ArchiCAD on multi-slab requests (vertex-count dependent)
body:
## Summary

A `CreateSlabs` request that contains more than one slab reliably crashes
ArchiCAD. The process terminates and the JSON connection closes mid-request
(`Remote end closed connection without response`); ArchiCAD must be restarted.
A request with a single slab never crashes, regardless of the slab's
complexity.

Isolating the variables shows the crash is tied to the slabs' outer vertex
count, not to the number of slabs, geometry validity, holes, or curves:

1. A multi-slab request is reliable only when every slab has the same vertex
   count and that count is low (at or below 11 in this data set).
2. Mixing different vertex counts in one request crashes, even when all the
   counts are small.
3. A homogeneous request of high-vertex-count slabs (12 or more here) crashes
   with as few as 2 slabs, even though a homogeneous request of 185 four-vertex
   slabs succeeds.

This suggests a per-request buffer or allocation problem in the multi-element
handling of `CreateSlabs`, for example a memo sized from one slab and then
reused across slabs that have a different or larger vertex count.

## Environment

- ArchiCAD build: 28.4.0 (7006) AUS FULL
- OS: macOS 15.7.7 (Apple Silicon)
- Tapir version 1.5.3
- Tapir `CreateSlabs` command version 1.0.3
- Requests sent to the JSON API on localhost, wrapped in
  `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` with `commandNamespace: "TapirCommand"`,
  `commandName: "CreateSlabs"`.

## Request and response shape

Single-slab request (always succeeds):

```json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": { "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "CreateSlabs" },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
      "slabsData": [
        {
          "level": 168.98,
          "thickness": 7.0,
          "referencePlaneLocation": "Bottom",
          "polygonCoordinates": [
            {"x": -478.37, "y": -23.95},
            {"x": -471.52, "y": -25.58},
            {"x": -471.07, "y": -23.68},
            {"x": -477.92, "y": -22.05}
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Success response:

```json
{"succeeded": true, "result": {"addOnCommandResponse": {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "..."}}]}}}
```

On a crash no JSON is returned: the HTTP connection closes and the client
reports `Remote end closed connection without response`.

## Data set for the "real data" scenarios

592 slabs, all `referencePlaneLocation: "Bottom"`, positive thickness, valid
closed rings. Outer vertex-count distribution:

```
3v x2, 4v x185, 5v x5, 6v x63, 7v x13, 8v x74, 9v x13, 10v x48, 11v x17,
12v x49, 13v x21, 14v x26, 15v x9, 16v x23, 17v x8, 18v x10, 19v x5, 20v x6,
21v x3, 22v x1, 23v x4, 25v x1, 26v x2, 28v x2, 29v x1, 53v x1
```

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: synthetic, uniform simple slabs, one multi-slab request. Result: OK
10 identical 4-vertex square slabs in a single request, and separately 100
identical 4-vertex squares. `succeeded: true` with all GUIDs returned, no
crash, repeated several times. Many slabs per request are fine when each is
simple and identical.

### Scenario 2: synthetic, varied vertex counts, multi-slab request. Result: CRASH
592 slabs sent in batches of 100; each slab a generated convex polygon with a
random vertex count from 3 to 20 (no holes, valid, CCW). The payload shape is
identical to Scenario 1 except that vertex count varies per slab. Crashes
within the first batch.

### Scenario 3: real data, one slab per request. Result: OK
The 592 real slabs, each sent in its own request (one entry in `slabsData`),
vertex counts 3 to 53, some with holes. All 592 succeeded with zero crashes,
including a 53-vertex slab. Any individual slab is fine regardless of vertex
count or holes.

### Scenario 4: real data, mixed vertex counts in a request. Result: CRASH
The 592 real slabs with several slabs per request and mixed vertex counts:
- all 420 slabs of 11 vertices or fewer in one request (mixed 3 to 11);
- batches of 100, 10, and 2 (mixed counts).
Every case crashes on the first multi-slab request, including the batch of 2.
Mixing different vertex counts crashes even when every slab is small.

### Scenario 5: real data, grouped by exact vertex count (homogeneous). Result: OK at or below 11v, CRASH at 12v
The 592 slabs bucketed by exact outer vertex count, each bucket sent as one
request so every request is vertex-count-homogeneous:
- groups of 3 to 11 vertices all succeeded, including large single requests of
  185 x 4v, 74 x 8v, 63 x 6v, 48 x 10v, and 17 x 11v;
- the 12-vertex group (49 slabs) in one request crashed.

### Scenario 6: real data, homogeneous high-vertex group, shrinking request size. Result: CRASH until size 1
The 12-vertex group (49 slabs, all exactly 12 vertices):
- 20 per request: crash (first 20);
- 2 per request: crash (first 2);
- 1 per request: OK. Every group from 12v up to 53v, sent one slab per request,
  succeeded.

## Key observations

- Single-slab requests never crashed (any vertex count or holes; 53v confirmed).
- Homogeneous multi-slab requests succeed for slabs of 11 vertices or fewer even
  at 185 slabs per request, but a homogeneous request of 12-vertex slabs crashes
  at just 2 slabs. The discriminator is vertex count, not slab count.
- Mixed-vertex-count multi-slab requests crash even when all counts are small.
- Holes and curves are not required: Scenario 2 used simple, hole-free, valid
  convex polygons and still crashed.

## Suggested minimal repro

1. One request with N identical low-vertex (for example 4-vertex) squares:
   expect success.
2. One request with N identical high-vertex (for example 12-vertex or more)
   polygons, N of 2 or more: expect a crash.
3. One request with a few slabs of differing vertex counts (for example one 4v
   and one 5v): expect a crash.

The 11-versus-12 boundary is specific to this data set. The exact per-request
vertex threshold is worth confirming with a controlled sweep of vertex count
and slab count.
author: ImLovinIt

title: Regression: batched CreateSlabs crashes Archicad (per-item works) — same class as #417
body:
### Summary

Batching more than one slab into a single `CreateSlabs` call force-closes ArchiCAD. Creating the same slabs **one per call** succeeds. This looks like the same class of batch-create crash as #417 (`CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows`).

### Environment

- ArchiCAD **28** (German), Windows
- Tapir **1.5.3**
- Python `archicad` package (JSON/Python API)

### Symptom

A batched `CreateSlabs` (10 slabs in one call) terminates ArchiCAD outright — the process exits and the next command from the Python client fails with `ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054]`. No graceful per-item error is returned; the whole session (and unsaved work) is lost.

### Steps / context

Our converter builds a storey model, then walls, then slabs. The crash reproduces like this:

1. `CreateWalls` for ~68 walls, each with a **non-center `referenceLineLocation`** (`CoreOutside`/`CoreInside`, the field added in 1.5.3). All succeed.
2. `CreateSlabs` with **10 slabs in one call** → ArchiCAD crashes.

Isolating the slab phase (same project state, same 68 reference-line walls already placed):

- `CreateSlabs` called **one slab per call** → all 10 created successfully, no crash.
- `CreateSlabs` called **batched (10 in one call)** → crash.

Interestingly, in an earlier run where the walls were created with the **default (centered) reference line**, the identical batched `CreateSlabs(10)` call worked. So the crash appears to be **project-state dependent** — it reproduces once the project contains walls with a non-center reference line — which mirrors the state/locale dependence reported in #417.

The 10 slabs are plain floors/ceilings (3–12 point polygons, positive thickness, `Basic` structure) — the same data that creates fine one-at-a-time, so the individual slabs are not degenerate.

### Suspected cause

Same area as #417 (batched `CreateDoors`/`CreateWindows` crash, suspected PR #409 / #410 element-creation hardening). Possibly `CreateSlabs` shares the batch-create path that regressed.

### Workaround

Create slabs one per `CreateSlabs` call.

### Notes

I can put together a minimal standalone repro (a tiny script: place a couple of reference-line walls, then a batched `CreateSlabs`) if that would help pin it down — just let me know.

title: Add navigator view/layout commands (CreateLayout, SetLayoutSettings, view map operations)
body:
## Summary

Adds a full set of navigator commands for managing layouts, subsets, and view map items.

### New commands

**Layout Book**
- `CreateLayoutSubset` — create a subset with all numbering options (style, prefix, startAt, continueNumbering…)
- `CreateLayout` — create a layout with full `layoutParameters` (size, margins, numbering, master by name or ID)
- `GetLayoutSettings` — read all layout parameters (works on regular layouts and master layouts)
- `SetLayoutSettings` — modify layout parameters with enforced rules:
  - `horizontalSize` / `verticalSize` only allowed on master layouts
  - `showMasterBelow` verified by read-back (ArchiCAD ignores it silently on regular layouts)

**View Map**
- `CreateViewMapFolder` — create a folder in the View Map
- `CreateViewsInViewMap` — create independent views from Project Map items
- `CreateViewMapCloneFolder` — create a live-sync clone folder mirroring a Project Map folder
- `SetViewRotation` — set rotation (radians) on one or more views
- `GetViewSettings` — read view parameters (rotation, structureDisplay, saveZoom, d3styleName…)
- `SetViewSettings` — modify view parameters
- `GetView2DTransformations` — read DB-level zoom/rotation (independent of per-view rotation)

**Navigator (shared)**
- `RenameNavigatorItem` — rename any navigator item
- `MoveNavigatorItem` — move with optional `previousNavigatorItemId` for ordering
- `DeleteNavigatorItems` — delete layouts, views, folders (subsets not supported by AC API)

### AC25/AC26 compatibility

All new functions (`ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem`, `SetNavigatorItemPosition`, `DeleteNavigatorView`, `SearchNavigatorItem`, `ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase`, `ACAPI_Element_GetExtent`) were introduced in AC27. Shims added to `MigrationHelper.hpp` under `#ifndef ServerMainVers_2700` map them to the old `ACAPI_Navigator(code, …)` / `ACAPI_Database(code, …)` API for AC25 and AC26. `CreateLayout`'s optional `parent` parameter is also guarded.

### Design notes

- `IsMasterLayoutDatabase()` helper detects master vs regular layout via `ACAPI_Navigator_SearchNavigatorItem` (checking `result.itemType == API_MasterLayoutNavItem`), because `DatabaseIdResolver::GetDatabaseWithId()` always returns `typeID = 0`.
- `showMasterBelow` is verified by read-back after `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeLayoutSets` since AC silently ignores it on regular layouts.

## Tests

| File | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_layout_workflow.py` | CreateLayoutSubset (all options), CreateLayout (all params), GetLayoutSettings, SetLayoutSettings (all restrictions), RenameNavigatorItem, MoveNavigatorItem, DeleteNavigatorItems |
| `test_navigator_views.py` | CreateViewMapFolder, CreateViewsInViewMap, CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap, CreateViewMapCloneFolder, SetViewRotation, GetViewSettings (all fields), GetView2DTransformations, SetViewSettings, RenameNavigatorItem, DeleteNavigatorItems |

All tests pass on **AC25** and **AC29**.
author: MathiasJon

title: Feature request: Read and modify placement (position, scale, source link) of Drawing elements
body:
## Summary
There is currently no way to programmatically read the geometry (position, size, scale) 
or the source link of a Drawing element that has already been placed on a Layout. 
There is also no way to change/relink the source of an existing Drawing.

## What already works
- `CreateDrawings` can create a new Drawing linked to a navigator item, at a given 
  position and scale.
- `UpdateDrawings` can refresh the content of an existing Drawing from its current source.

## What is missing
- `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `{"error": "Not yet supported element type"}` when 
  called on a Drawing element.
- `Get2DBoundingBoxes` / `Get3DBoundingBoxes` return `{"error": "Element not supported"}` 
  for Drawing elements.
- There is no command to change the source (navigator item / view) that an existing 
  Drawing is linked to (the equivalent of the native "Link Drawing to..." command).

## Use case
We want to automate a repetitive workflow: on a template layout, a set of Drawings 
(floor plan excerpts) is manually arranged at specific positions/scales, each linked 
to a specific view. We then need to replicate that exact arrangement across many other 
layouts, but each time linking the Drawings to a different (but equivalently structured) 
set of views. Since the arrangement varies per project and can't be hardcoded, we need to:
1. Read the position, size, and scale of each Drawing on the template layout.
2. Either update the link of an existing Drawing, or recreate it with `CreateDrawings` 
   using the same geometry but a different source.

Since the underlying C++ API (`API_DrawingType`) already exposes anchor point, width, 
height and linked source, it seems like the geometry data is available internally – 
it's just not yet exposed through the JSON/Python commands.

## Requested commands (naming is just a suggestion)
- `GetDrawingParameters(elements)` → returns position, size, scale, and current 
  linked source (navigator item) for each given Drawing element.
- `ChangeDrawingLink(elements_with_new_source)` → relinks an existing Drawing to a 
  different navigator item, keeping its position/size/scale unchanged.

Happy to help test this if it gets implemented. Thanks for maintaining this great add-on!
author: FabienneGrogg

title: fix(walls): reject zero-length walls in CreateWalls instead of crashing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #433. `CreateWalls` with a wall whose `begCoordinate == endCoordinate` (zero length) **crashes Archicad** (access violation, connection reset) instead of returning an error. This happens easily with real source data when axis/corner intersection collapses a segment.

## Change

Guard at the top of `CreateWallsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`: if begin and end coordinates are the same (via the existing `IsSame2DCoordinate` helper), return a controlled `APIERR_BADPARS` error for that item instead of proceeding into `ACAPI_Element_Create` (which crashes). Other walls in the same batch are unaffected — they still succeed, and the offending item gets an error entry in the result, consistent with the command's existing per-item error handling.

```cpp
if (IsSame2DCoordinate (begCoordinate, endCoordinate)) {
    return CreateErrorResponse (APIERR_BADPARS, "Zero-length wall: 'begCoordinate' and 'endCoordinate' are identical.");
}
```

## Testing

- Built clean on AC26 and AC28 (Win, VS2019, DevKit 26.3000 / 28.3001).
- Before: a batch containing a zero-length wall force-closed Archicad (reproduced on AC26, ~18 walls in, matching #433).
- After: the zero-length item returns `APIERR_BADPARS` with the message above; the remaining walls in the batch are created normally; no crash.

Mirrors the existing degenerate-polygon guards elsewhere in this file (slabs/zones use `IsSame2DCoordinate` the same way).

title: CreateStairs: multi-segment baselines (L/U-shaped) always fail with error -2130313215
body:
## Summary
`CreateStairs` (added in 1.5.0, PR #388) works for straight (2-point) baselines but **fails for every multi-segment baseline** (L-shaped and U-shaped) with:

```json
{"elements":[{"error":{"code":-2130313215,"message":"Failed to create new Stair"}}]}
```

PR #388 states the implementation covers "straight and multi-segment stairs (L-shaped, U-shaped)".

## Environment
- Tapir 1.5.3
- Archicad 28 build 7006 INT (Intel-based Mac build, running on Apple Silicon via Rosetta)
- macOS 15.x (Darwin 25.5.0)

## Steps to reproduce
Straight baseline — **works**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":10.0,"y":0.0},{"x":16.3,"y":0.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

L-shaped — **fails**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":20.0,"y":0.0},{"x":20.0,"y":4.0},{"x":24.0,"y":4.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

U-shaped — **fails**:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":0.6,"y":0.0},{"x":0.6,"y":3.9},{"x":2.0,"y":3.9},{"x":2.0,"y":0.0}],"zCoordinate":0.0,"totalHeight":3.40,"flightWidth":1.20}]}
```

## Variants tried (all fail identically)
- With and without the optional parameters (`totalHeight`, `flightWidth`, `stepNum`, `riserHeight`, `treadDepth`)
- Consistent riser/tread/height combinations (22 x 0.16818 = 3.70)
- Larger geometry (legs 4-5 m, cross segments 1.4 / 2.0 / 2.5 m)
- Only the required parameters (`baseLinePoints` + `zCoordinate`)

Straight baselines succeed every time with the same tool defaults, so the default Stair settings solve fine.

Possibly related: #403, #425.
author: Bahaturov

title: fix(stairs): support multi-segment (L/U-shaped) baselines in CreateStairs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #444. `CreateStairs` (from #388) failed with `-2130313215 "Failed to create new Stair"` for **every** multi-segment (L-shaped / U-shaped) baseline, while straight 2-point baselines worked.

## Root cause

`SetTypeSpecificParameters` pre-filled `stairBaseLine.edgeData` / `vertexData` by hand. The allocation is cleared, so `segmentType` stayed `0` = `APIST_StepsSegment` on **every** edge. A multi-segment baseline whose corner edges are forced to be steps segments is unsolvable for the stair solver, so `ACAPI_Element_Create` rejected all L/U baselines.

## Change

Leave `edgeData`/`vertexData` null and let `ACAPI_Element_Create` derive them from the baseline geometry — the same pattern as the `Element_Test` example in the API DevKit (`Do_CreateStair` sets only `coords`/`parcs`/`polygon`). Net −10 lines.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Straight 2-point baseline (regression) | ✅ | ✅ unchanged (footprint 1.2 × 4.65 at totalHeight 3.4) |
| L-shaped 3-point baseline (issue repro) | ❌ `-2130313215` | ✅ stair created |
| U-shaped 4-point baseline, legs 3.0 m apart | ❌ `-2130313215` | ✅ stair created |
| U-shaped, legs only 1.4 m apart (issue's exact coordinates) | ❌ | ❌ solver error — expected: the flights/landings physically don't fit between legs that close (the UI rejects this geometry too) |

So after the fix the remaining `-2130313215` cases are genuine "stair rules cannot solve this geometry" results (per-item error, other items in the batch unaffected), not a blanket multi-segment failure.

Built clean on AC26 and AC28 (Win, VS2019, DevKit 26.3000 / 28.3001).

title: fix(walls,columns): explicit height overrides story top-link
body:
## Summary

`CreateColumns` with `height: 2.0` produces a 2.65 m column when the template's column tool default is top-linked to a story — the explicit value is silently ignored. The same template dependence is behind long-standing "`CreateWalls` `height` is not honored" reports: whether an explicit height works currently depends on whether the tool default happens to be story-linked.

## Root cause

`CreateWalls`, `CreateColumns`, `ModifyWalls` and `ModifyColumns` write `element.wall.height` / `element.column.height` but never touch **`relativeTopStory`**. When the default is top-linked (`relativeTopStory > 0`), Archicad derives the element height from the link and ignores the field.

## Change

Set `relativeTopStory = 0` whenever an explicit `height` is applied (in the Modify commands together with the corresponding mask bit). Callers who want story-linked elements keep using the linked tool default — creating **without** `height` is unchanged.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win, story grid UG −3.0 / EG 0.0 / OG 3.0)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateColumns` `height: 2.0` | bbox zMax 2.65 (link wins) | ✅ zMax 2.0 |
| `CreateColumns` without `height` | zMax 2.65 (template default) | ✅ zMax 2.65 — unchanged |
| `ModifyColumns` `height: 1.5` | no effect on linked column | ✅ zMax 1.5 |
| `CreateWalls` `height: 2.2` | template-dependent | ✅ zMax 2.2 |
| `ModifyWalls` `height: 1.8` | template-dependent | ✅ zMax 1.8 |

Built clean on AC26 and AC28 (Win, VS2019, DevKit 26.3000 / 28.3001).

title: Add/completing Get/Set/delete commands for attributes
body:
## Summary

Works toward a self-contained, uniform "100% Tapir" Get/Create/Modify/Delete surface for every attribute type, rather than mixing native `API.*` calls with `TapirCommand.*` calls. Several of the new Get commands below (e.g. `GetBuildingMaterials`) overlap with existing official Archicad JSON API commands (e.g. `API.GetBuildingMaterialAttributes`) — that overlap is expected and accepted, not a bug: consistency of interface (one command family, the same `{attributeIds, fields}` filtering convention on every Get, the same `overwriteExisting` convention on every Create/Modify) is valued over avoiding duplication with the official API. `Delete` is already fully generic (`DeleteAttributesCommand`) across all 12 attribute types and untouched here.

- **New Get commands** (v1.5.4): `GetLines`, `GetFills`, `GetZoneCategories`, `GetMEPSystems`, `GetPenTables`, `GetProfiles`, `GetComposites`, `GetSurfaces`, `GetLayers`, `GetBuildingMaterials`
- **`CreateProfiles` `newSkins`** (AC27+ only): authors arbitrary polygon/arc/multi-contour hatches in Profiles, including building a Profile's geometry entirely from scratch (`sourceAttributeId` now optional). Uses the internal, undocumented VectorImage module; pre-AC27 has no equivalent construction API.
- **4 write-path bugs fixed**, found via exhaustive live testing:
  - `CreateBuildingMaterials`: `cutFillBackgroundPen` read the wrong JSON key; `connPriority` wasn't converted back from Archicad's internal encoding on Get.
  - `CreateFills` / `CreateLines`: a partial `overwriteExisting` modify that didn't resupply vector/dash/symbol geometry failed outright instead of preserving the existing pattern.
  - `CreateSurfaces`: 7 reflection/shine fields extracted as C++ `short` against a JSON schema typed `"number"` — silently never applied. Also relaxed overly-strict required fields blocking partial modifies.
  - Fill's `Image` subtype was completely unhandled — `GetFills` misreported real Image fills as `"Vector"`.

## Test plan

- [x] 136-check live regression suite (`Examples/test_all_attributes.py`) — all pass on AC29
- [x] Compiles clean on AC25 / AC26 / AC27 / AC29
- [x] Verified visually in Archicad's Attribute Manager for every type/subtype covered
author: MathiasJon

title: Let Column/Slab/Object/Lamp/Beam/Stair/Roof/Morph creation take an explicit floorIndex
body:
## Summary

Several element-creation commands derived the new element's floor purely by guessing from a Z/level coordinate (`GetFloorIndexAndOffset`), with no way to pin the floor explicitly. A Z value near a story boundary could land on the wrong floor, and there was no way to force a specific one — the same class of bug already fixed for `CreateMeshes`/`CreateTexts`.

This adds an optional `floorIndex` input to the commands that were still missing it.

## What changed

- Added a shared helper, `ResolveFloorIndexAndOffset` (`CommandBase.hpp`/`.cpp`): identical to the existing Z-guess when no `floorIndex` is given, but an explicit `floorIndex` picks the story directly. The offset is still computed from the given Z (via `GetZPos`), so the element's **absolute 3D position is preserved exactly** — only which floor-plan it's grouped under changes.
- Applied it to:
  - `CreateColumns`
  - `CreateSlabs`
  - `CreateObjects` / `CreateLamps` (share `SetLibraryPartElementParameters`)
  - `CreateBeams`
  - `CreateStairs`
  - `ApplyRoofDetails` — shared with the existing modify-roof command, so modifying an existing roof's level also benefits, even though `CreateRoofs` itself is a separate pre-existing no-op (multi-plane pivot-edge setup was never implemented) unrelated to this change.
- `CreateMorphs` got its own fix: it never derived `header.floorInd` from position at all — it silently used whatever `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` defaulted to, regardless of the requested position. Now computed via the same helper, while its transform matrix's absolute Z placement (already correct) is left untouched.

## Not affected

- `CreateWalls` already had `floorIndex` support.
- `CreateWindows` / `CreateDoors` / `CreateOpenings` never had this bug: they're positioned relative to a host element (`ownerWallId` / `ownerElementId`), with no absolute Z to guess a floor from.

## Testing

Compiled cleanly on AC25/26/27/29.

Live-verified on AC29 and AC25 with a disposable test script: for Column, Slab, Beam, Stair, Morph, and Object, created one instance at a Z that would naturally guess floor B, both with no `floorIndex` (confirms the guess fallback still works) and with an explicit `floorIndex=A` that contradicts the guess (confirms the override wins) — read back via `GetDetailsOfElements`. 12/12 checks passed on AC29, 10/10 on AC25 (AC25's project incidentally has a basement story, so this also exercised a negative floor index).

Specifically double-checked that the fix changes the floor *assignment* and not the element's real position: creating a Column with `floorIndex=-1` at `z=0.5` (which would guess floor `0`) came back as:

```json
{
  "floorIndex": -1,
  "details": {
    "zCoordinate": 0.5,
    "bottomOffset": 3.3
  }
}
```

i.e. `floorIndex` reflects the override, `zCoordinate` stays exactly as requested (not snapped to floor `-1`'s own base level of `-2.8`), and `bottomOffset` is correctly back-computed (`0.5 - (-2.8) = 3.3`).
author: MathiasJon

title: Add full API_MorphType parameter coverage to Get/Create/Modify Morphs
body:
Every non-reserved field of API_MorphType is now readable and writable, not just geometry/material: placement rotation (xAxis/yAxis/zAxis), default surface, shadows, per-story visibility, link-to-story, floor plan display options, pens/line types, cover fill (including orientation/distortion), texture projection, level.

Also fixes a real bug found while testing: CreateMorphs silently lost its 'surfaceId' (default surface) because Archicad discards element.morph.material through ACAPI_Element_Create alone - worked around with an automatic follow-up ACAPI_Element_Change.

Two remaining limitations are documented rather than fixed, since they are confirmed Archicad SDK behavior, not bugs in this add-on: per-face surfaceId is broken pre-Archicad 27 and fixed from 27 onward, and showContour/showFill do not persist through either Create or Modify on any tested version (same class of issue as the existing bodyType/edgeType caveats).
author: MathiasJon

title: Add full Object/Lamp support and fix GDL parameter bugs
body:
## Summary

- Object and Lamp elements now expose every real field of `API_ObjectType`
  (Get, Create, and — for the first time — Modify), not just
  origin/dimensions/angle.
- Fixes a real, reproducible Archicad crash found while testing.
- Fixes five pre-existing bugs in the GDL parameter commands
  (`GetGDLParametersOfElements`/`SetGDLParametersOfElements`), unrelated
  to the Object/Lamp work but found along the way.

## Object / Lamp: before vs. after

Before this PR:
- **Create** only accepted `libraryPartName`, `coordinates`, `dimensions`
  — not even `angle`.
- **Modify did not exist at all.** There was no way to change anything
  on an already-placed Object/Lamp beyond generic floor/layer/draw order.

After this PR, both Create and the new `ModifyObjects`/`ModifyLamps`
commands support: `angle`, `pen`, line type, surface, section fill
attributes, the four "use library defaults" flags, `reflected`,
fixed-size/fix-point behavior, per-story visibility, link-to-story, and
(Lamp only) the light on/off state. Get reports every one of these
fields back, field-for-field symmetric with what Create/Modify accept.

Three fields (`offset`, `useFixedAngle`, and Lamp's `lightColor`) are
confirmed live to be silently discarded by Archicad through both Create
and Modify — documented in the schema as read-only in practice, the
same class of behavior already known from Morph's `bodyType`/`edgeType`.

## Crash fix

Building the new Create/Modify schemas by passing a large (~2000 char)
JSON fragment through `GS::UniString::Printf`'s `%s` crashed Archicad
reliably during add-on registration (`ACCESS_VIOLATION` in
`APICommandBridge.dll`, confirmed via Archicad's own FATAL crash
reports). Fixed by building the schema through plain string
concatenation instead of a single large `Printf` substitution.

## GDL parameter bugs fixed

- `SetGDLParametersOfElements` hardcoded the owner element type to
  `API_ObjectID` regardless of the actual element, so it likely never
  worked correctly on Window/Door/Skylight/Zone/Label/Drawing/
  CurtainWall* — confirmed broken and now fixed and verified live on a
  Window.
- A `libInd` inconsistency between Get (`-1`) and Set (`0`) is now
  aligned.
- A data-loss bug in "Step"-range GDL values: two sequential
  assignments meant the second silently clobbered the first, so
  `stepBegin` was always lost.
- Two of eight parameter flags (`BoldName`, `Open`) were never exposed.
- Per-array-item text labels (`arrayDescriptions`) were never read.

## Test plan

- [x] Compiles cleanly on AC25/26/27/29.
- [x] `Examples/test_object_lamp_full_support.py`: 30/30 checks pass —
      Create + Get + Modify on both Object and Lamp with every new
      field, plus a live demonstration of the GDL type-owner fix on a
      real Window.
- [x] Crash fix confirmed stable on AC29 (extensive) and AC27 (add-on
      registration + Tapir responding, no crash).
author: MathiasJon

title: Close out the Favorites feature area: apply/update/rename/delete
body:
## Summary

Favorites currently support create, read, import, export, and applying to an element type's tool defaults - but not applying to an already-placed element, updating an existing favorite, renaming one, or deleting one. This PR adds the four missing commands so the Favorites command surface is complete, closes #294, and includes two other fixes found along the way.

## What's new

- **`ApplyFavoritesToElements`** (closes #294) - applies a favorite's settings to real, already-placed elements, not just to a tool's defaults. Rejects cleanly if the favorite's element type doesn't match the target's. Takes four optional booleans (`applySettings` / `applyClassifications` / `applyCategories` / `applyProperties`, all `true` by default) so a caller can opt out of applying a given category.
- **`UpdateFavoritesFromElements`** - re-captures an element's current settings into an *existing* favorite, without losing its folder placement. Until now the only way to refresh a favorite was to delete and recreate it.
- **`RenameFavorites`** / **`DeleteFavorites`** - thin wrappers around the two remaining `ACAPI_Favorite_*` functions that had never been exposed.
- **`CreateFavoritesFromElements`** gains an optional `folder` parameter to place new favorites under a folder hierarchy in the Favorites palette.

## Notable implementation details

**`ApplyFavoritesToElements` uses `ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters`, not `ACAPI_Element_Change`.** `ChangeParameters` only ever touches settings-type parameters and always keeps the target element's own guid, which is exactly what "apply a favorite" should mean - it never moves, resizes, or re-identifies the element.

This matters because an earlier attempt used `ACAPI_Element_Change(..., withdel=true)`. The `withdel` flag means "delete the original instance and create a new one," not "change in place" - a live test caught it deleting elements outright when the recreate step failed after the delete had already gone through. Switching to `ChangeParameters` fixes this at the root: the concept of deleting-and-recreating doesn't exist there.

**Cross-version build fix:** `ACAPI_Category_SetCategoryValue` only exists from AC27 onward; AC25/26 use `ACAPI_Element_SetCategoryValue` (same signature, different name). A `TAPIR_Element_SetCategoryValue` migration wrapper was added to `MigrationHelper.hpp`, mirroring the existing default-element equivalent. Building only against AC29 would not have caught this.

## Testing

- Compiles clean on AC25/AC26/AC27/AC29.
- `Examples/test_favorites_commands.py` extended to exercise all of the above: nested `folder`, `ApplyFavoritesToElements` success + cross-type rejection + the `applySettings` opt-out, `UpdateFavoritesFromElements`, `RenameFavorites` (including a name collision), `DeleteFavorites`. `Test/ExpectedOutputs/test_favorites_commands.py.output` updated to match.
- Live-verified on Archicad 29: applying a real built-in favorite to a Wall correctly changes its construction/thickness while leaving position and floor untouched.
author: MathiasJon

title: ModifySlabs with polygonOutline causes fatal Archicad crash; empty holes array cannot clear holes (AC29, 1.5.3)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 5003 GER (Mac ARM), Tapir 1.5.3, Teamwork project.

**Repro:**
1. Create a slab via `CreateSlabs` (works fine).
2. Call `ModifySlabs` with `slabsWithDetails: [{elementId, polygonOutline: [...same outline...], holes: []}]`.
3. Archicad crashes fatally (Bug Reporter, process gone) — even with a tiny 26-point outline. Reproduced twice.

**Related observations:**
- `ModifySlabs` with ONLY `holes: []` returns error -2130313112 "No slab fields to modify" — an empty holes array is treated as "field absent", so holes can never be cleared via API.
- Workaround we use: delete + recreate the slab without holes.

**Expected:** either apply the outline/holes modification or return an error — never crash the host.

---
*Found during large-scale automation of an AC29 Teamwork project (bulk element creation via Tapir + JSON API). Happy to provide more repro details.*
author: mozzi86

title: CreateDoors: fails with certain favorites; centerOffset ignored in polygon walls; unclear errors (AC29, 1.5.3)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 5003 GER (Mac ARM), Tapir 1.5.3.

**Issue 1 — favorites:** `CreateDoors` (both via `favoriteName` param and after `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`) fails with -2130313110 "Failed to create door." for some door favorites (in our project: all "T ..." favorites based on library part "Tür 29" from Doors and Windows DACH), while a favorite based on "Eingang 01 1-Fl 27" works with identical parameters. Suggest surfacing the underlying library-part error.

**Issue 2 — polygon walls:** For polygonal walls (APIWtyp_Poly), `centerOffset` is stored on the door (readable via GetDetailsOfElements) but ignored for placement — the door is always placed at the same internal spot regardless of centerOffset (verified with 3 doors at centerOffset 0.6/1.7/2.8 landing identically; measured via Get3DBoundingBoxes since 2D boxes include the symbol). `MoveElements` on such doors shifts them unpredictably along band edges. If polygon-wall doors are unsupported, an explicit error would save users a lot of time.

**Issue 3 — minor:** `CreateDoors`/`CreateOpenings` on walls require `width` AND `height`; missing height yields "Can't use empty polygon!" — a clearer message ("height required") would help.

**Issue 4 — minor:** Wall `GetDetailsOfElements` in 1.5.3 does not return thickness/compositeId (present in current sources — version drift note for anyone pinning 1.5.3).

---
*Found during large-scale automation of an AC29 Teamwork project (bulk element creation via Tapir + JSON API). Happy to provide more repro details.*

title: Expose a Drawing's source link, and let it be relinked via ChangeDrawingLink
body:
There was no way to programmatically read which navigator item (view or layout) a placed Drawing was created from, or to relink it to a different source afterward - two closely related gaps in an otherwise fairly complete Drawing API (geometry read/write already existed via GetDetailsOfElements/ SetDetailsOfElements).

- GetDetailsOfElements now reports a Drawing's navigatorItemId (the field is internally called drawingGuid, but that name is misleading - Archicad's own doc comment calls it "for identification by autotext" when it is actually the source link, so the field is exposed under the name CreateDrawings already uses for the same concept).
- ChangeDrawingLink relinks a Drawing to a different source. Archicad has no API to change drawingGuid in place - confirmed live that ACAPI_Element_Change silently drops any change to it once the Drawing already exists, even though sibling fields (pos, angle, ...) change correctly through the same call. The only way to relink is to recreate: this command captures the old Drawing's full appearance (pos, angle, ratio, drawingScale, modelOffset, clipPolygon), creates a new Drawing against the new source with that same appearance, and deletes the old one. The new Drawing necessarily gets a new guid, which the command returns - any external references to the old guid need updating separately. The Drawing Title marker's position is not preserved; this appears to be an unresolved, undocumented corner of the API rather than something worth working around (even Graphisoft's own forum support responses on this exact recreate-a-drawing scenario don't address it).

Building this surfaced a real crash: a "oneOf" written inline inside a command's own GetResponseSchema() - rather than as a named entry in CommonSchemaDefinitions.json referenced via $ref - reliably crashes Archicad's schema validator (APICommandJSONSchema.dll), regardless of what the command's Execute() actually does. Every existing oneOf in this codebase already followed the named-entry convention; this one didn't yet. Fixed by adding a named ElementIdOrError definition.

Also fixes two small pre-existing bugs found while touching this code: DrawingSettings' schema only declared clipPolygon even though SetDetailsOfElements already handled pos/angle/ratio/drawingScale/ modelOffset for Drawings (dead code, now reachable), and a clipPolygon item schema referenced the nonexistent #/2DCoordinate instead of #/Coordinate2D.

Compiles clean on AC25/26/27/29. Examples/update_drawings.py is extended to exercise both the new navigatorItemId field and ChangeDrawingLink against real Drawings, with a matching Test/ExpectedOutputs update.

title: Add keyboard-shortcut-able + toolbar script slots to Tapir
body:
Lets users assign up to 6 scripts to slots via a new "Shortcuts" palette button opening a dedicated management dialog (one popup + editable menu label per slot). Each slot registers its own Add-On menu command (Run Script Shortcut 1-6) that Archicad's native Keyboard Shortcuts editor can bind a key to, running the assigned script directly via the existing ExecuteScript path. Assignments and custom labels persist through the palette's preferences blob (bumped to version 12) and are re-applied to the real menu items on Archicad startup via ACAPI_MenuItem_SetMenuItemText.

The main script dropdown also now shows "[Shortcut N]" next to any script that is assigned to a slot.

| **Properties** | Create/DeletePropertyGroups, Create/Delete/UpdatePropertyDefinitions, Get/SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes |

| **Library** (new group) | GetLibraries, ReloadLibraries, AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary, GetAvailableLibraryParts |
| **Favorites** | Import/ExportFavorites, ApplyFavoritesToElements, UpdateFavoritesFromElements, Rename/DeleteFavorites, GetFavoritePreviewImage |
| **IFC** (new group) | IFCFileOperation, GetElementsByIFCIds, GetIFCIds/Type/PropertiesOfElements |
| **Revision** (new group) | GetRevisionIssues/Changes, GetDocumentRevisions, GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts, GetRevisionChangesOfElements |
| **Navigator** | PublishPublisherSet, GetView2DTransformations, SetViewRotation, CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap, Set3DCutPlanes, Get/SetLayoutSettings, GetLayoutCustomScheme, CreateDetails/Worksheets/Layout/LayoutSubset/Drawings/Sections/ViewsInViewMap |
| **Element creation & modification** | CreateWalls/Beams/Columns/Slabs/Objects/Lamps with **native Rhino geometry inputs** (lines, points, polygon point-trees); CreateZones/Polylines/Texts/Meshes/Morphs/Stairs/Roofs/Windows/Doors/Openings, 3 dimension commands and all 9 Modify* commands with JSON-based inputs for their deeply nested schemas |

### Icons

- ~120 new SVG icons authored in the existing 24×24 line-art style (`IconSource/`), rasterized to PNG (`Resources/`) and wired through `Resources.resx` / `Resources.Designer.cs`
- Added icons to all 28 previously iconless components — **every component in the plugin now has an icon**
- Consistent visual language: + badge = create, pencil badge = modify/set, ✕ badge = delete; element glyphs reuse the existing house motifs (WallDetails, ColumnDetails, ...)

### Infrastructure

- Reusable abstract bases for JSON-passthrough accessors/executors (`NoInputJsonAccessorComponent`, `ElementsJsonAccessorComponent`, `JsonItemsExecutorComponent`, `AttributeDetailsJsonComponent`, `AttributeCreateJsonComponent`, `LibraryPartCreatorComponent`)
- New typed data contracts under `Types/` (DesignOptions, Favorites, Navigator, Properties, Commands, ...)
- `TapirGrasshopperPlugin.csproj`: enabled `GenerateResourceUsePreserializedResources` (required for the resx-referenced bitmaps when building with current .NET SDKs; `System.Resources.Extensions` was already referenced)

### Design notes

- Commands with deeply nested / highly variable schemas take their items as JSON objects matching the command's documented item schema, with an `AdditionalSettings` merge input on the geometry hybrids — so full schemas remain reachable while the common path stays Grasshopper-idiomatic
- All components follow the existing patterns (`ArchicadAccessorComponent` / `ArchicadExecutorComponent`, refresh/execute capsule buttons, 1-or-N input list conventions)

## Test plan

title: Fix CA1416 warning in ImageHelp; graceful fallback without a drawing backend
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #457: fixes the `CA1416` compilation warning in `ImageHelp.cs` and makes the preview-image components degrade gracefully on platforms without a `System.Drawing` backend.

```
warning CA1416: This call site is reachable on all platforms. 'Bitmap' is only supported on: 'windows'.
```

### Why suppress rather than gate to Windows

`System.Drawing.Common` is flagged as Windows-only by the platform analyzer on the plain `net7.0` target (Rhino 8 Mac), but Rhino ships a working `System.Drawing` implementation on every platform it supports — the same mechanism that renders all component icons on macOS (the project references the package with `ExcludeAssets="runtime"`, so Rhino's copy is used). Gating bitmap decoding to Windows would needlessly break Mac.

### Changes

- `ImageHelp.FromBase64`: local, documented `#pragma warning disable CA1416` plus a runtime fallback — `PlatformNotSupportedException` / `TypeInitializationException` / `DllNotFoundException` are caught and `null` is returned when the drawing backend is genuinely unavailable
- `GetElementPreviewImage`, `GetRoomImage`, `GetFavoritePreviewImage`: when the bitmap cannot be decoded, the component emits a remark ("use the Base64 output") instead of failing — the Base64 output always works

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — 0 warnings, 0 errors on all three target frameworks (net48, net7.0, net7.0-windows)

title: Add native browser palette as a tkinter alternative for Python scripts
body:
Native browser palette as a tkinter alternative for Python scripts

Summary

Tapir Python scripts can now show a real HTML/CSS/JS interface in a native Archicad palette (embedded Chromium browser) instead of building a tkinter window. The user interacts with the page, and the Python script retrieves the submitted data to continue its work — a genuine tkinter replacement, forms included.

How it works

  1. The script calls ShowScriptUI with an HTML string → the palette opens immediately.
  2. The page can call window.ACAPI.SubmitResult(json) (a direct JS↔C++ bridge, not an HTTP request) once the user submits.
  3. The Python script retrieves the response by polling GetScriptUIResult in a loop (time.sleep + poll), since a command can't block waiting for user input without freezing the very palette the user needs to interact with.
aclib.RunTapirCommand('ShowScriptUI', {'htmlContent': html})
while result is None:
    time.sleep(0.3)
    resp = aclib.RunTapirCommand('GetScriptUIResult', {})
    if resp['hasResult']:
        result = json.loads(resp['result'])

New commands

Command | Purpose -- | -- ShowScriptUI | Opens/refreshes the palette with the given HTML GetScriptUIResult | Returns (and clears) the last submitted result, if any

ShowScriptUI options (every relevant DG::Browser setting, all optional):

  • width / height / title / resizable
  • zoomEnabled / zoomLevel
  • scrollBarsVisible
  • contextMenuEnabled
  • navigationDisabled
  • allowSelfSignedCertificates
  • clearCookies
  • autoHeight — automatically resizes the palette to fit the content (via a small injected script, no JS authoring required from the calling script)

JS bridge exposed to the page: window.ACAPI.SubmitResult(json), window.ACAPI.ClosePalette(), window.ACAPI.ReportContentHeight(px).

Cross-version compatibility (25 → 29)

Archicad 25/26 use a different JS bridge API (DG::JSObject/JSFunction/JSValue) than Archicad 27+ (JS::Object/Function/Value, JavascriptEngine module) — same shape, different namespace. A type alias covers the difference; zoom control, self-signed certificates, and context-menu mode (all absent before 27) are wrapped in version-gated TAPIR_Browser_* helper functions.

Bugs found and fixed while testing

  • Feedback loop on autoHeight: our own resize re-triggered the content observer → added an in-flight guard plus an unchanged-height check.
  • Jitter during manual resize: the observer fired on every frame → added a 150ms debounce so it only reacts once the drag settles.
  • Both fixes apply to every Archicad version, not just 25/26.

Testing done

  • Full round trip (simple form, then a layer picker with search/checkboxes) on AC29 and AC25
  • Every option tested individually and in combination
  • Edge cases: missing parameter (clean error), unconsumed stale result (no leak between calls)
  • Size lock (resizable: false) combined with autoHeight
  • zoomEnabled, scrollBarsVisible, contextMenuEnabled, navigationDisabled verified visually

title: Structured outputs: replace JSON text outputs with per-property outputs (29 components)
body:
## Summary

Removes every JSON-text output from the Grasshopper components: **29 accessor components** that previously returned their command response as a single JSON string now expose **every property of the response as a separate, typed output** (follow-up to #457).

### Output design

- **Flat fields → typed lists** (text / integer / number / boolean / point / vector / colour / guid-wrapper), one item per queried input, in input order
- **Nested arrays → trees** with one branch per queried item (e.g. a Pen Table's pens become `PenIndices`/`PenColors`/`PenWidths`/`PenDescriptions` trees); doubly nested structures use `{item; subitem}` tree paths (profile skin edges/outline geometry, fill line lengths, revision change custom data)
- **Per-item errors keep alignment**: for "X or error" union responses, error positions hold nulls (lists) or empty branches (trees), and a final `ErrorMessages` output carries the per-item message — empty on success. Doubly nested unions (property values of attributes, classifications of elements) additionally get an inner error tree
- Coordinates become native `Point3d`/`Vector3d`, `ColorRGB` objects become GH colours, and id objects become the plugin's guid-wrapper types so they plug directly into other Tapir components

### Converted components

| Group | Components |
|---|---|
| Attributes (10) | GetLines, GetFills, GetZoneCategories, GetMEPSystems, GetPenTables, GetProfiles, GetComposites, GetSurfaces, GetBuildingMaterials, GetLayersDetails |
| Library (2) | GetLibraries, GetAvailableLibraryParts |
| Project (1) | GetCalculationUnits |
| Navigator (3) | GetLayoutSettings, GetLayoutCustomScheme, GetView2DTransformations |
| IFC (4) | GetIFCIdsOfElements, GetIFCTypeOfElements, GetIFCPropertiesOfElements, GetElementsByIFCIds |
| Elements (2) | GetSolidElementLinks, GetDimensionData |
| Revision (5) | GetRevisionIssues, GetRevisionChanges, GetDocumentRevisions, GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts, GetRevisionChangesOfElements |
| Properties (1) | GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes |
| Classifications (1) | GetClassificationsOfElements |

### Infrastructure

- `Helps/JsonOutputHelp.cs` — shared response-walking helpers (error-union detection, scalar/point/colour/guid extraction, branch alignment)
- New structured bases: `AttributeStructuredGetterComponent`, `ElementsStructuredGetterComponent`, `RevisionChangesOfEntitiesComponent`
- New output helpers in `Component.cs`: `OutNumberList`, `OutColors`, `OutPointTree`
- Deleted the obsolete JSON bases: `AttributeDetailsJsonComponent`, `NoInputJsonAccessorComponent`, `ElementsJsonAccessorComponent`
- All output field names verified against the C++ `GetResponseSchema` implementations and `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`

### Compatibility

`ComponentGuid`s, icons, command names, groups and inputs are unchanged — existing definitions resolve to the same components; only the outputs changed (which is the point of this PR).

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — 0 warnings, 0 errors on all target frameworks (net48, net7.0, net7.0-windows)
- [x] Every converted output mapping cross-checked against the add-on's response schemas
- [ ] Functional check in Rhino/Grasshopper against a running Archicad (attribute getters with a mixed valid/invalid guid list are a good smoke test for the null-alignment + ErrorMessages behavior)

title: Expose Drawing title settings via Get/SetDetailsOfElements
body:
## Context

Drawings placed on a layout have their own "title" — a name, an ID, and (since Archicad 10) a real placed GDL object showing that information. None of this was previously reachable through Tapir: `GetDetailsOfElements`/`SetDetailsOfElements` only exposed geometry-level fields for a Drawing (position, scale, clip polygon), with no way to read or replicate how a drawing's title is configured. This came up while automating batch generation of sale-plan layouts, where every generated drawing needs to match a reference drawing's title setup.

## What's added

- **`nameType` / `customName`** — how the title's displayed name is assembled (from the source view/file, from the view's ID+name, or a custom string)
- **`numberingType` / `customNumber`** — how the title's ID is assigned (from the layout, from the source view, or a custom string)
- **`isInNumbering`** — whether the drawing participates in the project's automatic drawing numbering sequence
- **`titleLibraryPartIndex`** (read/write) — the title object's own library part index
- **`titleElementId`** (read-only) — the id of the title object itself, once instantiated

All on the existing `DrawingDetails`/`DrawingSettings` schemas — no new command, no version bump.

## Implementation notes

- The title is a genuine placed GDL library part element (`API_DrawingTitle`, "object based elements from Archicad 10"), not just plain struct fields — its own guid is exposed as `titleElementId`, so its parameters (beyond the basic font/pen/size fields already on `API_DrawingTitle`) are reachable through the existing `GetGDLParametersOfElements`/`SetGDLParametersOfElements` commands, the same way as any other element.
- A negative/invalid `titleLibraryPartIndex` means no title object exists at all for that drawing. Writing a valid index (e.g. copied from another drawing that already has a title) is what makes Archicad instantiate the title's placed element — this is the mechanism a script needs to use before it can read/write that title's own GDL parameters.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_drawing_title.py` (included) — round-trips `nameType`/`customName`/`numberingType`/`customNumber`/`isInNumbering` on a drawing and restores the original values; separately, locates another drawing in the project that already has a title, copies its `titleLibraryPartIndex` and GDL parameters onto the test drawing, and verifies the title object gets created and populated
- [x] Only ever touches a layout named `TAPIR_TEST_DRAWING_TITLE`, restores every value it changes — safe to run against a real, in-use project
- [x] Verified live end-to-end on a real project (test layout created, both checks passed, layout deleted afterward)

title: SetDetailsOfElements fails on grouped elements with generic error -2130313112; group membership is undetectable via API
body:
**Environment:** macOS, Archicad 28, Tapir 1.5.5, raw JSON API (no wrapper — reproduced via direct HTTP POST to the Archicad port).

**Summary:** `SetDetailsOfElements` (changing only `layerIndex`) fails with `{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Failed to change element"}}` for every element that belongs to a **group**. The same call succeeds on ungrouped elements, and succeeds on the *same* grouped elements once **Suspend Groups** is activated manually in the Archicad UI.

**Repro (verified step by step):**
1. 24 Wall elements, grouped (Edit → Grouping → Group). Layers unlocked, elements visible/editable.
2. `SetDetailsOfElements` with `{"layerIndex": <valid index>}` → all 24 fail with -2130313112 (even writing the element's *current* layer index).
3. Control: same call on an ungrouped Wall → success.
4. Activate **Suspend Groups** in the UI (no API command exists for this) → repeat the exact same call → 24/24 success, both directions (layer A→B and B→A verified by re-reading).

**The bigger problem — this failure is undetectable and undiagnosable via API:**
- `FilterElements` with `IsEditable`, `InMyWorkspace`, `HasAccessRight`, `IsIndependent` → the grouped elements **pass all filters** (reported as editable).
- `GetConnectedElements` with `connectedElementType: "Group"` → returns empty.
- The error message ("Failed to change element") gives no hint about the cause.

**Requests (any subset would help):**
1. A meaningful error (e.g. "element is grouped; suspend groups to modify") instead of the generic code.
2. A way to read group membership of an element.
3. A `SuspendGroups` toggle command, or an option on Modify/Set commands to operate through groups (matching native Info Box behavior, which *can* change the layer of a grouped selection).

Context: we are automating interior-design documentation (interior elevations, annotation, layer hygiene) on a real residential project — happy to test patches.

title: Interior Elevation databases are unreachable via API: ChangeWindow fails (-2130313110); related navigator items cannot be modified (7403)
body:
**Environment:** macOS, Archicad 28, Tapir 1.5.5, raw JSON API (reproduced without any wrapper).

**Summary:** In a real interior-documentation workflow (room-by-room interior elevations), the Interior Elevation database type is effectively closed to automation:

**A. `ChangeWindow` cannot target an Interior Elevation:**
`ChangeWindow` with `windowType: "InteriorElevation"` and `databaseId` set to the navigator item guid of an IE viewpoint fails with `{"error": {"code": -2130313110, "message": "Failed to resolve target database."}}`. Reproduced for sub-views of composite (multi-direction) IE markers and for single-direction markers alike. Consequence: any command scoped to the active database (labels, dimensioning, reads) cannot be pointed at an IE view programmatically — the view must be opened by hand.

**B. Project Map items of native IE markers cannot be renamed (official API, for context):**
`RenameNavigatorItem` on the Project Map sub-views of a composite IE marker returns error 7403 "Navigator item cannot be modified" — even renaming to the *same* name. Workaround we found and verified: `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap` first, then renaming the **clone** in the View Map works reliably. We mention it here because Tapir is the natural place for an IE-aware convenience command.

**Why this matters:** interior architecture teams live in Interior Elevations — ours has ~30 IE views for a single floor. Judging by the issue tracker (zero issues mentioning "interior elevation" to date), this territory seems untested; we are happy to be the test case and can reproduce anything on request.

Related: #465 (same project, same audit session).

title: Keynote commands: manage the keynote tree and place keynote labels (Archicad 28+) with Grasshopper components
body:
## Summary

Fixes #470

Adds a new **Keynote Commands** group to the add-on, built on the Keynote API introduced in Archicad 28 (`ACAPI::Keynote`), plus a matching **Keynotes** group of Grasshopper components. On Archicad 27 and older the commands are registered but return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` with a clear message (same pattern as the Design Options group).

### New commands (all `1.5.6`, available from Archicad 28)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GetKeynoteTree` | Returns the whole keynote folder/item hierarchy from the root folder as a recursive structure (`keynoteFolderId`, key, title, reference, uiText, `subFolders`, `items`) |
| `GetKeynoteAutoTexts` | Returns the Key/Title/Description/Reference **autotext tokens** of the given keynote items (usable as label text content) |
| `CreateKeynoteFolders` | Creates folders under a given parent folder (or the root); returns created ids or per-item errors |
| `CreateKeynoteItems` | Creates items by key with optional title/description/reference; returns created ids or per-item errors |
| `ModifyKeynoteFolders` | Changes key/title/reference; only provided fields are changed |
| `ModifyKeynoteItems` | Changes key/title/description/reference; only provided fields are changed |
| `DeleteKeynoteFolders` | Deletes folders (root folder protected) |
| `DeleteKeynoteItems` | Deletes items |
| `CreateKeynoteLabels` | Places Label elements whose text references the given keynote items via autotext (selectable content fields), ported from the DevKit `Keynote_Test` example |

### Implementation notes

- Folders/items are addressed by **GUID**; since the Keynote API has no lookup-by-id, the commands traverse the tree from the root folder (shared `FindKeynoteFolderById` / `FindKeynoteItemById` helpers)
- All mutations run inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`; per-item results use the house `executionResults` / `idsOrErrors` patterns
- New shared schema definitions: `KeynoteFolderId`/`KeynoteItemId` (+`ArrayItem`, +`IdsOrErrors`) and the **recursive** `KeynoteFolderDetails` + `KeynoteItemDetails`
- **No build-system change needed**: the `KeynoteAPI` DevKit module is picked up automatically by the existing module glob (include dirs + import libs) in `Tools/CMakeCommon.cmake`

### Grasshopper components (group "Keynotes", one file per component)

- **GetKeynoteTree** flattens the recursive response into parallel lists: folder guids/keys/titles/references/parent-guids (root included with null parent) + item guids/keys/titles/descriptions/references/containing-folder-guids
- **GetKeynoteAutoTexts** outputs the four token lists with aligned per-item `ErrorMessages`
- **Create/Modify/DeleteKeynoteFolders**, **Create/Modify/DeleteKeynoteItems** executors with the house 1-or-N input pairing and optional fields
- **CreateKeynoteLabels** places labels at input points for the given items
- New guid wrapper types (`KeynoteFolderGuid`/`KeynoteItemGuid`) following the `GuidObject`/`GuidWrapper`/`GuidItemsObject` pattern
- 9 new icons in the house 24×24 line-art style: keynote hexagon-tag motif (tag + key text + leader line), folder-with-tag variant, and the standard +/pencil/✕ badges; all previews visually verified

### Example

`archicad-addon/Examples/keynotes.py` exercises the full command set: dump tree → create folder + item → modify both → get autotext tokens → place a label → delete the created item and folder (restores project state). Not registered in `Test/ExpectedOutputs` since the feature requires AC28+ and the golden-output harness is version-sensitive.

title: MEP commands: create, modify, connect and query MEP elements (Archicad 28+) with Grasshopper components
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **MEP Commands** group built on the modern `ACAPI::MEP` API (the `MEPAPI` DevKit module), plus a matching **MEP** group of Grasshopper components — covering **creation, manipulation and management** of MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements. Available from **Archicad 28**; on older versions the commands are registered but return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` (same pattern as the Design Options and Keynote groups).

### New commands (all `1.5.6`)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GetMEPElements` | All MEP elements with type (RoutingElement, RigidSegment, Elbow, Transition, Branch, Terminal, Accessory, Equipment, Fitting, FlexibleSegment, TakeOff) and domain (Ventilation/Piping/CableCarrier), optionally filtered by both |
| `GetMEPRoutingElements` | Route details: domain, MEP system attribute, route polyline, segments with cross-section data (width/height/shape), nodes with positions |
| `GetMEPPorts` | Ports of MEP elements: position, direction, shape, size, domain, MEP system, physical connection status and the connected element/port |
| `GetMEPDistributionSystems` | The distribution-systems graph: domain, MEP system attribute and member elements per system |
| `CreateMEPRoutingElements` | Places duct/pipe/cable-carrier routes along 3D polylines with optional cross-section (width/height/shape/reference id) and MEP system |
| `CreateMEPElements` | Places Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting elements at given positions with optional orientation |
| `ModifyMEPRoutingElements` | Changes MEP system, cross-section of all segments, and node positions of existing routes |
| `ConnectMEPElements` | Connects routes to other routes/MEP elements via the MEP API's logical connection — merging routes, splitting routes or creating Branch elements — and reports the resulting changes (deleted/split route, created branch) |

### Implementation notes

- Investigated the full `ACAPI::MEP` surface across AC27–AC30 DevKits first: the API used here is **uniform from AC28** (`ConnectLogically`, `IsPhysicallyConnected`, map-based `Place`), so a single `ServerMainVers_2800` gate suffices; the only cross-version difference is the `IsBend`→`IsElbow` predicate rename (handled with a `ServerMainVers_2900` guard). AC27's incompatible `Place` signature is why the group starts at AC28.
- Elements are addressed by `API_Guid` and adapted via `Adapter::UniqueID`; MEP system attributes are exposed as attribute guids using the existing `GetAttributeGuidFromIndex`/`GetAttributeIndexFromGuid` helpers (interoperating with the existing `GetMEPSystems`/`CreateMEPSystems` attribute commands)
- Enumeration uses `ACAPI_Element_GetElemList (API_ExternalElemID, …)` + the `MEPAdapter` classID predicates
- Creation goes through the `*Default` objects (cross-section configured on the routing-segment default, so `Place` runs with defaults applied); mutations run in undoable scopes
- New shared schema defs: `ElementIdOrError`, `ElementIdsOrErrors`
- **No build-system change**: the `MEPAPI` module include dirs and import libs are picked up by the existing DevKit module glob in `Tools/CMakeCommon.cmake`

### Grasshopper components (group "MEP", one file per component)

Structured inputs/outputs throughout (no JSON passthrough): route polylines as point trees (branch per route), per-element tree outputs for segments/nodes/ports, native Point3d/Vector3d, guid-wrapper types for element and MEP-system ids, 1-or-N input pairing. 8 new icons in the house 24×24 line-art style (bent duct, node-route polyline, pipe-with-port, branching system, link rings; +/pencil badges), all previews visually verified.

### Example

`archicad-addon/Examples/mep_elements.py`: creates two duct routes + a pipe route, places a terminal, queries elements/details/ports, connects the routes, modifies a cross-section, lists distribution systems.

### Deleting MEP elements

No dedicated delete command is needed: MEP elements are ordinary Archicad elements, so the existing generic `DeleteElements` command (and Grasshopper component) deletes them — the same approach the DevKit `MEP_Test` example uses. The `GetMEPElements` descriptions note this, and `mep_elements.py` now cleans up its created elements via `DeleteElements`.

### Not in scope (possible follow-ups)

Preference-table management (per-shape table classes need a design pass), FlexibleSegment/TakeOff placement, library-part swapping on placed elements (`SetObjectId`), and the AC30 Electrical domain.

## Test plan

- [x] Add-on builds clean: **AC27** (gated path), **AC28**, **AC29**
- [x] Grasshopper plugin builds clean on net48 / net7.0 / net7.0-windows, 0 warnings
- [x] No duplicate ComponentGuids or CommandNames
- [x] Live smoke test against Archicad 28/29: run `Examples/mep_elements.py` (route creation → query → connect → modify → distribution systems), plus the GH components

title: Element grouping commands: GetGroupsOfElements, GetElementsOfGroups, Get/SetSuspendGroupsMode
body:
## Summary

Fixes #465

Adds four commands to the **Element Grouping** group, wrapping the group query and Suspend Groups functions of the API, plus matching Grasshopper components.

### `GetGroupsOfElements` — executes `ACAPI_Grouping_GetGroup`

- Input: `{ "elements": [...] }` (`#/Elements`)
- Response: `{ "groupGuids": [ ... ] }` — one item per input element using the existing **`#/GroupIdOrError`** definition:
  - grouped element → `{ "groupId": { "guid": ... } }`
  - ungrouped element → per-item error `"The element is not part of any group."`
  - lookup failure → per-item error with the API error code

### `GetElementsOfGroups` — executes `ACAPI_Grouping_GetGroupedElems`

- Input: `{ "groups": [ ... ] }` (`#/GroupIdArrayItem` items)
- Response: `{ "elementsOfGroups": [ ... ] }` — one item per input group using the new shared **`#/ElementsWrapperOrError`** definition: `{ "elements": [...] }` with the directly contained elements (nested sub-group content not included, per the API), or a per-item error
- The two commands compose in both directions with `CreateGroups` (its returned `groupId` feeds `GetElementsOfGroups`; `GetGroupsOfElements` results feed back as `parentGroupId`)

### `SetSuspendGroupsMode` — executes `ACAPI_Grouping_ChangeSuspendGroup`

- Input: `{ "suspendGroups": true|false }`; response: `{ "executionResult": ... }`
- On Archicad versions older than 27, where only the **`APITool_SuspendGroups` toggle** exists, the command reads the current state first and toggles only when it differs from the requested one — so it behaves as a proper setter on **all supported versions**

### `GetSuspendGroupsMode` — executes `ACAPI_View_IsSuspendGroupOn`

- Response: `{ "suspendGroups": true|false }`
- Included because the API documentation requires restoring the previous Suspend Groups state after a suspended operation, which is impossible without reading it; on old SDKs the function maps to `APIEnv_IsSuspendGroupOnID` via a new `MigrationHelper` define

All four commands work on all supported Archicad versions (the group queries via the existing `ACAPI_ElementGroup_*` MigrationHelper mappings).

New shared schema definitions: `ElementsWrapper`, `ElementsWrapperOrError` (complex `oneOf` kept in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` per house convention; verified with the duplicate-key-aware JSON check).

### Grasshopper components (Elements group)

- **GetGroupsOfElements**: `ElementGuids` → `GroupGuids` (null for ungrouped, aligned with input) + per-item `ErrorMessages`. Introduces the `GroupGuid`/`GroupGuidWrapper` types (`"groupId"`).
- **GetElementsOfGroups**: `GroupGuids` → `ElementGuids` tree (one branch per group) + per-group `ErrorMessages`.
- **SetSuspendGroupsMode** / **GetSuspendGroupsMode**: boolean setter (default on) and getter for the mode.
- Icons derive from the CreateGroups dashed-group motif: extract-arrow and group-unpacked variants for the queries, pause-bars variants for Suspend Groups (pencil badge on the setter); all previews visually verified.

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build clean (older build dirs were cleaned locally; CI covers AC25–AC29 including the pre-27 toggle path)
- [x] Grasshopper build clean (net48/net7.0/net7.0-windows)
