title: Shortcut menu: disable unassigned items and add a Manage Script Shortcuts item
body:
## Summary

The six **Run Script Shortcut** menu items were always enabled — clicking an unassigned one only popped an error alert. They are now **disabled (greyed out) whenever no script is assigned** to the slot, and enable/disable live as slots change.

> Note: the Archicad API offers no way to *hide* add-on menu items (`APIdefs_Interface.h` exposes only `API_MenuItemDisabled` and `API_MenuItemChecked`), so greying out is the closest achievable behavior to the requested "disable or hide".

### Changes (`TapirPalette.cpp`)

- `ApplyShortcutMenuItemText` — after setting the item text, it now also syncs the `API_MenuItemDisabled` flag from the slot state (`scriptShortcutSlots[slot].IsEmpty ()`), using the same Get/modify/Set round trip as the existing palette check-mark code. The flag calls use the 2-argument form required by the pre-AC27 `MigrationHelper` macros.
- `SetShortcutSlot` — now ends with `ApplyAllShortcutMenuItemTexts ()`, refreshing **all six** items, because assigning a script to one slot can implicitly clear it from another (the dedup loop).
- Startup state comes free: `AddScriptsFromPreferences` already ends with `ApplyAllShortcutMenuItemTexts ()` (forced at launch via `TapirPalette::Instance ()` in `Initialize`), so unassigned items are greyed out right after preferences load — including all six on a fresh install.
- The empty-slot alert in `RunShortcutSlot` stays as a defensive fallback.

### Manage Script Shortcuts menu item

A new **"Manage Script Shortcuts..."** item sits in the Tapir menu directly above the six shortcut slots, separated from the items above it (`MenuFlag_SeparatorBefore`). It opens the same shortcuts dialog as the palette's Manage Shortcuts button (`TapirPalette::OpenShortcutsDialog`), so shortcuts can be assigned without opening the palette first — which also gives greyed-out slots an obvious path to becoming useful.

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 build clean
- [x] AC30 build attempted: the only errors are the pre-existing AC30 incompatibilities fixed by #477 (`ToLowerCase`, `hasClearenceCollision`, ProjectCommands) — this change introduces none
- [ ] Live check: the Tapir menu shows separator + "Manage Script Shortcuts..." above the slots and the item opens the dialog; fresh start → all six shortcut items greyed out; assign a script in the Manage Shortcuts dialog → the item enables immediately; reassign the same script to another slot → the old slot's item greys out; clear a slot → greys out; restart Archicad → persisted state honored

title: CreateWindows/CreateDoors on AC29: command returns a GUID but no opening is created (single item, no crash) — even with a valid favoriteName
body:
### Summary

On **Archicad 29 (build 5003, CHE)** with **Tapir 1.5.5**, `CreateWindows` and `CreateDoors` **report success** — the response contains an element GUID for each item — but **no window/door is actually created**. `GetElementsByType("Window", filters: ["IncludeSubElemObjects"])` returns **0** immediately afterwards, and the host wall (`GetDetailsOfElements`) shows no opening. Archicad does **not** crash.

This happens **even for a single item** and **with a valid `favoriteName`** applied, so it appears distinct from the batched-crash regression in #417 (there, single-item works and the failure is a crash; here single-item silently produces nothing and there is no crash).

### Environment

- Archicad **29**, build **5003**, language **CHE** (Swiss) — `API.GetProductInfo` → `{ "version": 29, "buildNumber": 5003, "languageCode": "CHE" }`
- Tapir **1.5.5** (`TapirAddOn_AC29_Mac.bundle`), macOS
- Native JSON server → `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` → `TapirCommand.CreateWindows` / `CreateDoors`
- "Türen und Fenster DACH" library loaded. `GetAvailableLibraryParts` shows the window/door parts (typed as `Object`, e.g. `Fenster (Wand)`, `Tür (Wand)`), and `GetFavoritesByType("Window")` returns 7 favorites (e.g. `AF_0.90x1.50_A_0.08_L_0.24`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. `CreateWalls` — one plain straight wall (6 m long, 0.30 m thick, `Center` reference line). Persists fine.
2. `CreateWindows` with a **single** item:
   ```json
   { "windowsData": [ { "ownerWallId": { "guid": "<wall-guid>" }, "centerOffset": 3.0, "width": 1.2, "height": 1.5, "sillHeight": 0.9 } ] }
   ```
   Response looks successful:
   ```json
   { "elements": [ { "elementId": { "guid": "<new-guid>" } } ] }
   ```
3. Immediately query:
   ```json
   { "elementType": "Window", "filters": ["IncludeSubElemObjects"] }
   ```
   → returns **0** elements. The owner wall shows no opening.
4. Same with `favoriteName` set to a value returned by `GetFavoritesByType("Window")` → same result (GUID returned, 0 windows persisted). Same behaviour for `CreateDoors`.

No Archicad crash occurs; subsequent API calls work normally.

### Observations / possible cause

- In `archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, `CreateWindowsCommand::Execute` pushes the element GUID only when `ACAPI_Element_CreateExt(&element, &memo, 1UL, &marker)` returns `NoError`. Since a GUID *is* returned, `CreateExt` is reporting `NoError`, yet the element is not present afterwards — suggesting the created sub-element is not committed / is discarded during regeneration on this AC29 CHE build.
- Regular elements created via the same framework in the same session (`CreateWalls`, `CreateSlabs`, `CreateColumns`, `CreateBeams`, `CreateMorphs`) **do** persist. Only the opening (Window/Door) sub-elements do not.
- May be related to #417 (batched opening creation) but the manifestation differs: no crash, and single-item also fails here.

Happy to provide a minimal standalone repro script or logs if useful.

title: feat(roofs): implement CreateRoofs for single- and multi-plane roofs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #467. `CreateRoofs` (from the v1.4 extended commands package, #369) was crash-hardened into an unconditional reject: the original implementation left the roof under-specified for `ACAPI_Element_Create`, which made the core throw and pop a modal dialog that hung the JSON API. This completes the command for both roof classes.

## Change

**Multi-plane (default, existing schema now functional):** following the DevKit's `Do_CreatePolyRoof` example, force `overHangType = API_OffsetOverhang` so the contour polygon is derived automatically by offsetting the pivot polygon — the missing piece; `pivotPolyEdges` are optional per the API docs and not needed. Dropped the manual contour duplication. `eavesOverHang` keeps the tool default unless `eavesOverhang` is given; `levels` fill `levelNum`/`levelData` as before.

**Single-plane (new):** pass `pivotLine {begCoordinate, endCoordinate}` and optionally `angle` (radians) to create an `API_PlaneRoofID` roof. Polygon goes into `memo.coords/pends/parcs` (slab pattern); the plane rises on the left side of the pivot-line direction (flip the line to tilt the other way).

Mixed payloads (`levels`/`eavesOverhang` with `pivotLine`, `angle` without it) and zero-length pivot lines are rejected with clear per-item errors.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Multi-plane, issue's exact payload (rectangle, 1 level, 35°) | ✅ hip roof created (bbox z rises above `level` as expected) |
| Multi-plane with `eavesOverhang: 0.5` | ✅ contour exactly 0.5 m outside the pivot polygon |
| Multi-plane without `levels` (tool defaults) | ✅ created |
| Single-plane `pivotLine` + `angle: 0.5236` (30°) | ✅ plane rises ≈ tan(30°)·depth on the left of the line |
| `levels`+`pivotLine` / `angle` without `pivotLine` | ✅ clean per-item errors |
| Stability | ✅ no crash, no modal hang; counts verified; all test roofs deleted |

title: Failing commands return `{"error": ...}`, which their own response schema forbids → error 4009
body:
## Summary

When a command takes its error path, the add-on returns `{"error": {code, message}}` as the
whole response payload. But the command's declared `GetResponseSchema()` sets
`"additionalProperties": false` and does not declare an `error` property, so Archicad rejects
the add-on's own response and replaces it with:

```
code 4009 — Invalid command response (The JSON is invalid according to the JSON schema.
Validation failed on schema rule 'additionalProperties' while trying to validate field on path '#/error'.)
```

The actual error message never reaches the caller.

This is the same failure mode as #323 (closed, `GetZoneBoundaries`), still reproducible on
1.5.5 with other commands — so it looks like it was addressed per command rather than at the
framework level.

## Environment

- Archicad 28.0.0 RUS, build 5200, arm64 (`API.GetProductInfo` → `{"version": 28, "buildNumber": 5200, "languageCode": "RUS"}`)
- macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon
- Tapir add-on 1.5.5 (`GetAddOnVersion` → `{"version": "1.5.5"}`)

## Reproduction

**1. `GetDesignOptions`** — in a project with no design options
(`GetDesignOptionCombinations` succeeds and returns `{"designOptionCombinations": []}`):

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19723 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetDesignOptions"}
  }
}'
```

```json
{"succeeded": false, "error": {"code": 4009, "message": "Invalid command response (The JSON is invalid according to the JSON schema. Validation failed on schema rule 'additionalProperties' while trying to validate field on path '#/error'.)"}}
```

**2. `GetDesignOptionForElements`** with any valid `elements` — same 4009.

**3. `FilterElements`** without the optional `filters` parameter — same 4009. With
`"filters": ["IsVisibleByLayer"]` the command succeeds, so only its *error path* is
unreachable. This one is the clearest demonstration that the bug is in error handling
rather than in the command itself.

## Cause

`archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.cpp` — the error payload is the response:

```cpp
GS::ObjectState CreateErrorResponse (GSErrCode errorCode, const GS::UniString& errorMessage)
{
    GS::ObjectState error;
    error.Add ("code", errorCode);
    error.Add ("message", errorMessage.ToCStr ().Get ());
    return GS::ObjectState ("error", error);
}
```

`archicad-addon/Sources/DesignOptionCommands.cpp` — `GetDesignOptionsCommand::GetResponseSchema()`:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "designOptions": { "type": "array", "items": { "$ref": "#/DesignOptionDetails" } }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["designOptions"]
}
```

`designOptions` is required and `error` is not allowed, so as soon as such a command fails,
its response can never satisfy its own schema. Every command that declares a response schema
is affected — the two design option commands are just where it currently shows.

## Suggested fix

Handle this once in the framework rather than per command: either wrap each declared response
schema in a `oneOf` with the error shape
(`{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}}`), or skip response-schema validation when the
command returned an error result.

## Minor, same area

`GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId` returns an unsubstituted placeholder when the navigator
item has no associated database (reproduced with a `ScheduleItem`):

```json
{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Navigator item {navigatorItem.itemType} has no associated database"}}
```

title: Add full GET/SET/Create support for pure 2D drafting elements
body:
## Summary

- Adds full GET/SET/Create support for the pure 2D drafting elements: **Line, Arc, Circle, Hotspot, PolyLine, Hatch**. Geometry (including curves, and for Hatch, holes) and settings fields (pen, line type, room-separator, fill attributes) are now all readable, settable, and creatable.
- Adds Create + GET for **Spline** (geometry SET is not supported here — see below).
- New commands: `CreateLineElements`, `CreateArcs`, `CreateCircles`, `CreateHotspots`, `CreateHatches`, `CreateSplines`.
- Extends `GetDetailsOfElements` / `SetDetailsOfElements` with type-specific details/settings for all six types.

## Details

**PolyLine / Hatch geometry SET** (including changing the vertex count) needed two undocumented ACAPI polygon-memo requirements, found via a real usage example and live testing — neither is mentioned in the `ACAPI_Element_Change` or `API_Polygon` reference docs:
- `vertexIDs[0]` must hold the max vertex ID used across the shape.
- For Hatch, each contour (outline + each hole) restarts its own vertex ID numbering at 1, instead of continuing sequentially across contours.

Without these, every attempt (from-scratch memo, GetMemo-seeded memo, `ACAPI_Polygon_InsertPolyNode`/`DeletePolyNode`) reproducibly failed with `APIERR_BADPOLY` / `APIERR_IRREGULARPOLY`.

**Spline**: Create + GET only. `ACAPI_Element_Change`'s own documentation states geometry (coordinates/closed) cannot be modified for this type in the current Archicad version — confirmed live (a SET attempt is silently a no-op). Settings fields (`roomSeparator`/`linePenIndex`/`lineTypeId`) remain fully settable.

**`penWeight` is deliberately not exposed** anywhere (GET/SET/Create), on any type. Confirmed live that a raw `penWeight` override does not reliably take visible effect in Archicad — line thickness is controlled by which pen is assigned (`linePenIndex`), since each pen carries its own weight in the project's pen table. Exposing a field that doesn't functionally apply would be misleading.

**Naming**: the new Line-element create command is `CreateLineElementsCommand` / `"CreateLineElements"`, not `CreateLinesCommand` / `"CreateLines"` — that name was already taken by the pre-existing command for the Line **attribute** (dash pattern) type. Both concepts naturally wanted the name "Line".

## Test plan

- [x] `archicad-addon/Examples/test_2d_elements_exhaustive.py` — live regression test, 40/40 checks, covering every field (geometry + settings) across all six types: create → GET → SET → GET, including Hatch holes-with-curves and PolyLine/Hatch vertex-count changes.
- [x] Compiles clean on AC27.
- [x] Verified no command-name collisions against existing attribute commands.

title: Fix two ScriptUI palette lifecycle bugs: reappearing after close, and a quit-time crash
body:
Fixes two issues reported against the ScriptUI palette (#485, #486).

**#485** - the palette reappeared with stale content after being explicitly closed (close button or `window.ACAPI.ClosePalette()`), whenever the user then navigated away from a Schedule or an open GDL object tab. Archicad sends `APIPalMsg_HidePalette_Begin`/`_End` around those contexts to temporarily declutter the screen, and the old handler unconditionally re-showed the palette on `_End` if it happened to be hidden - not distinguishing "we hid it via `_Begin`" from "the user already closed it". A `hiddenByForcedHideBegin` flag now tracks that distinction, cleared whenever the palette is closed explicitly, and only consulted (then reset) by `_End`. Live-verified: close the palette, open/leave a schedule, confirm it stays closed.

**#486** - Archicad crashed on quit on macOS (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in the `DG::Browser` destructor, per the reporter's crash log) after `ShowScriptUI` had been used. `ScriptUIPalette::instance` is a static `GS::Ref`, so its destructor was running at DLL/dylib unload time - after Archicad's own browser subsystem may have already begun tearing down, which a Chromium-based control does not tolerate. `FreeData` (called by Archicad while its environment is still fully alive, unlike static destruction order at unload) now explicitly releases the instance via a new `ScriptUIPalette::Release()`, so the browser is torn down deterministically before Archicad's own shutdown proceeds. Not reproducible on Windows; fix addresses the exact crash site and timing described in the report.

## Test plan
- [x] Builds clean on AC27.
- [x] Live-verified #485: opened the palette, closed it via the close button, opened/left a Schedule window, confirmed it stayed closed (previously reopened).
- [ ] #486 is macOS-only and could not be reproduced/re-tested on this Windows dev machine - fix targets the exact destructor/timing described in the crash report.

title: Add GetRelationsOfElements command
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **GetRelationsOfElements** command (Element Commands group, 1.5.7) that calls `ACAPI_Element_GetRelations` and returns the type-specific relations of the given elements. The relation variant depends on the element type:

- **Walls / beams / beam segments** (`wallConnections` / `beamConnections` / `beamSegmentConnections`): five connection lists - connected to the beginning point, to the end point, with their reference line to the endpoints, to the reference line (not at endpoints), and reference line intersections. Each item carries the connected element id and whether it connects with its beginning or end point.
- **Zones** (`zoneRelations`): related elements grouped by element type, plus the boundary sections of walls, beams and curtain wall segments (element id, adjacent zone polygon edge index, begin/end distance along the element).
- **Windows / doors / skylights / curtain wall panels** (`openingRelations`): the zones on the two sides (`fromRoom` / `toRoom`).
- **Roofs / shells** (`roofOrShellRelations`): the connected zones.

The optional `otherElementType` input filters the relations to one element type. Per-element errors (unsupported type, missing element) are reported inline without failing the whole command. Available from Archicad 26 (the relation structures were reworked in the AC26 API); older versions report a not-supported error.

- `ElementCommands.{hpp,cpp}`: the new command; relation handles are disposed with the matching `ACAPI_Dispose*RelationHdls` functions; the roof/shell `rooms` array uses a defensive ownership pattern that is correct whether the API fills a caller-provided array or allocates its own.

- `AddOnMain.cpp`: registration in the Element Commands group with version 1.5.7.

title: Give the Modify Grasshopper components typed input parameters
body:
## Summary

Fixes #490.

The nine Modify* Grasshopper components (`ModifyWalls`, `ModifyBeams`, `ModifyColumns`, `ModifyDoors`, `ModifyMeshes`, `ModifyWindows`, `ModifyMorphs`, `ModifyRoofs`, `ModifySlabs`) previously exposed a single `ItemsData` JSON text input, which was impossible to use without reading the command schema. They now expose:

- **ElementGuids** - identifiers of the elements to modify (same generic input as the other element components), and
- **separate typed optional inputs** for the commonly used fields of each command (numbers, booleans, integers, texts, points and attribute guids). Each input follows the same 0/1/N rule as the Create components: supply one value to apply it to every element, or one value per element. Only connected inputs are changed on the elements.
- an optional **AdditionalSettings** JSON input (one object per element, or one for all) for the rarely used or deeply nested fields - slab/roof outline polygons and holes, roof `levels`, morph `body`/display/texture settings, mesh `polygonCoordinates`/`sublines` - merged into each item, so the full command schema remains reachable.

Examples of the new typed inputs: ModifyWalls gets BegPoints, EndPoints, ArcAngles, Heights, Thicknesses, BottomOffsets, Offsets, StructureTypes, BuildingMaterialGuids, CompositeGuids, ProfileGuids; ModifyWindows/Doors get Widths, Heights, SillHeights, CenterOffsets, Reflected, RefSide, OSide; ModifyMeshes gets Levels, SkirtTypes, SkirtLevels, Ridges, ShowLines, FloorIndices, ContourPens, LevelPens (written into the command's nested `meshData` object).

## Implementation

- New `Components/ModifyElementsComponentBase.cs`: declarative shared base - subclasses list their fields (input name, JSON key, kind, description); the base creates the inputs, enforces the 0/1/N pairing, builds the per-element JSON items and merges AdditionalSettings. ModifyMeshes uses the base's `itemWrapKey` to target the nested `meshData` object.
- The nine components are now thin field lists. Component GUIDs, names and icons are unchanged. Existing definitions that used the old single-JSON input need rewiring (the input set changed), which is the point of the issue.
- `JsonItemsExecutorComponent` is untouched - other components still use it.

title: Fix the add-on auto-update on macOS
body:
## Summary

Fixes #489 ("Update and Restart Archicad" does nothing on macOS).

The palette downloads `Tools/update_addon_and_restart_archicad.py` from `main` and runs it detached via `uv`, so failures in the script are invisible to the user. The script had three macOS-specific defects:

1. **Archicad was never quit.** `QuitArchicad ()` returned early in its macOS branch (before sending the `QuitArchicad` command), so nothing visible happened - exactly what the issue reports.
2. **The relaunch could not work.** `subprocess.Popen ([archicadLocation], shell=True)` with a *list* argument on POSIX runs `sh -c "<path>"`, and every real Archicad path contains spaces, so the shell split it apart. The relaunch now uses `open <app bundle>` on macOS (handles spaces and LaunchServices activation) and a plain argument list on Windows.
3. **Nothing waited for Archicad to terminate.** On Windows the file-replacement retry loop waits implicitly because the loaded add-on file is locked; on macOS files of a running process can be overwritten, so the script would have replaced the bundle and "relaunched" while the old instance was still shutting down. A new `WaitForArchicadToQuit` polls the JSON port (with a request timeout) until the connection is refused before proceeding.

Additionally, the bundle is now extracted with `ditto -x -k` on macOS instead of `zipfile.extractall`, which drops Unix permission bits and symlinks.

Because the palette always fetches this script from `main` at update time, merging this PR fixes the update flow for existing installs immediately - no add-on release is required.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m py_compile` passes
- [ ] On a Mac with an older Tapir version: Tapir menu > Check for updates > Update and Restart Archicad - Archicad quits, the bundle is replaced, Archicad relaunches with the new version
- [ ] On Windows: verify the update flow still works (quit is now awaited via the port poll before the retry loop)

title: Fix component base classes configured from constructor parameters
body:
## Summary

Fixes a construction-order bug in the shared Grasshopper component base classes (reported by @tlorantfy): `GH_Component`'s constructor calls `RegisterInputParams` - and through it the `AddInputs()` override - **before** the derived constructor bodies run. The declarative bases (`ModifyElementsComponentBase` from #494, `CreateElementsComponentBase` from #496) and `JsonItemsExecutorComponent` stored their configuration (field lists, array keys, input names) in readonly fields assigned in the constructor body, so `AddInputs` read them while they were still null.

## Fix

The configuration moved from constructor parameters to overridable members, which are safe to call during base construction because the overrides return constants or static data:

- `ModifyElementsComponentBase`: `ArrayKey` (abstract), `ItemWrapKey` (virtual, null), `Fields` (abstract `IReadOnlyList<Field>`).
- `CreateElementsComponentBase`: `ArrayKey`, `Fields`, `HasAdditionalSettingsInput` (virtual, true).
- `JsonItemsExecutorComponent`: `ArrayKey`, `ItemWrapKey`, `InputName`, `InputDescription`.

All 31 derived components now declare their field lists as `private static readonly List<Field> FieldDefinitions` plus property overrides (9 Modify*, 18 creation components, 4 JSON-items components). A comment on each base documents the constructor-order constraint so it is not reintroduced.

No component names, GUIDs, input sets or JSON payloads change - this restores the intended behavior of the previous PRs.

## Test plan

- [ ] In Grasshopper: place a Modify* and a Create* component and verify the inputs appear correctly

title: Accept the error response in every command response schema
body:
## Summary

Fixes #483. When a command took its error path, the whole response was `{"error": {code, message}}` - but the declared response schemas set `"additionalProperties": false`, so Archicad rejected the add-on's own response with schema validation error 4009 and the real error message never reached the caller (same failure mode as the closed #323).

## Fix

`CommandBase::GetResponseSchema` is now `final`: it takes the schema the command declares (renamed to `GetRawResponseSchema`, a mechanical rename across all command classes) and wraps it as

```json
{ "anyOf": [ <raw schema>, <inlined error-object schema> ] }
```

- **anyOf, not oneOf** - some raw schemas (e.g. `GetZoneBoundaries` -> `ZoneBoundariesOrError`) already allow an error object themselves; a response matching two alternatives must stay valid.
- **Inlined error schema, not `#/ErrorItem`** - commands constructed with `CommonSchema::NotUsed` provide no schema definitions, so a `$ref` would be unresolvable for them.
- Commands with no declared response schema keep returning none (no validation).
- `RegisterCommand`/documentation generation keeps using the **raw** schema, so the generated docs are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build succeeds
- [x] The composed wrapper was extracted from the source and verified to produce valid JSON with the expected anyOf structure
- [ ] Live: call a command with invalid input (e.g. `GetZoneBoundaries` with a bogus guid) and verify the error `{code, message}` now reaches the caller instead of error 4009

title: Fix duplicated LibPartBasedElementDetails in the GetDetailsOfElements docs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #426 (GetDetailsOfElements documentation shows `LibPartBasedElementDetails { }` twice).

## Root cause

`ObjectDetails`, `WindowDoorDetails` and `LabelDetails` composed their shared base by putting a top-level `"$ref": "#/LibPartBasedElementDetails"` NEXT TO their own `properties`. Both the documentation renderer (`renderer.js` replaces any node containing `$ref` with the referenced definition, dropping the siblings) and standard JSON Schema ignore siblings of `$ref` - so all three definitions rendered as bare `LibPartBasedElementDetails` entries (the repeats collapse to an empty `{ }`), duplicating the real `LibPartBasedElementDetails` branch of `TypeSpecificDetails`.

## Fix

The three inherited properties (`libPart`, `ownerElementId`, `ownerElementType`) are inlined into each of the three definitions and the top-level `$ref` is removed; `libPart` joins the `required` list of ObjectDetails/WindowDoorDetails (not LabelDetails - text labels have no library part). The generated `docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js` is regenerated from the fixed definitions so the live docs are corrected on merge.

This also makes the schemas standard-conforming: under strict JSON Schema semantics the old sibling properties were dead (ignored next to `$ref`), so e.g. `ObjectDetails`' own fields were formally not part of the schema at all.

## Test plan

title: Fix ModifySlabs crashing/failing on any outline or hole change
body:
Fixes #452.

`ModifySlabs` could reliably crash Archicad or reject the request with `APIERR_BADPOLY` for anything beyond resending an unchanged outline: adding/removing/clearing holes, growing or shrinking the point count, or changing arcs - covering #452's exact crash (a same-size outline resend with holes cleared) plus every geometry-changing case around it.

## Root causes

Found and fixed one at a time against real live tests, in `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp` (`ApplySlabPolygonChange`):

- **`BMReallocPtr` on `sideMaterials`** (a raw `Ptr`, not a GS `Handle`) corrupted the heap when its size changed - this was the original crash report. Rebuilding the polygon memo now uses Graphisoft's own `ACAPI_Polygon_InsertPolyNode`/`DeletePolyNode`/`InsertSubPoly`/`DeleteSubPoly` primitives (matching the DevKit's own reference example for this exact scenario) instead of a from-scratch handle rebuild.
- **`ACAPI_Polygon_InsertPolyNode`'s `nodeIndex`** needs to be set to the position the new node will occupy (matching the DevKit example's own `neig.inIndex + 1`), not "insert after this index" as the header comment's wording alone suggests - using the wrong index reliably returned `APIERR_BADPARS`.
- **`vertexIDs` must never be manually renumbered.** Per Graphisoft's own `API_ElementMemo` docs, existing IDs must be preserved as-is and new vertices inserted with ID `0`, left for Archicad itself to assign - every earlier attempt at inventing an ID scheme (sequential, global, per-contour) failed in some case.
- **A hole's memo needs +2 (not +1) coordinate slots**: index 0 is the unused dummy slot and the last index holds the closing duplicate - under-allocating by one silently corrupted adjacent heap memory, surfacing as a crash much later on an unrelated commit.
- **`polygonArcs` needs to be resized to the exact new arc count**, not overwritten address-by-address in place - reusing a stale-sized handle left old arc entries stuck around after they should have been replaced or cleared.

## Also

`holes` can now be sent on its own, without `polygonOutline`, to add/remove/clear holes without resending the (possibly large) unchanged outline - previously a holes-only request silently fell through to `"No slab fields to modify."`.

## Test plan

- [x] `archicad-addon/Examples/test_modify_slabs_exhaustive.py` (new, 21 checks): the exact #452 repro, the holes-only shorthand, outline point count growing and shrinking, multi-hole add/shrink with mixed shapes, arc replacement and clearing, and a combined single-call change touching all of the above at once. 21/21 passing live on AC27.
- [x] Verified zero crashes across every geometry-changing scenario tested (previously several of these reliably crashed Archicad or corrupted the heap).

title: GetDetailsOfElements: ObjectDetails is defined but missing from the TypeSpecificDetails oneOf, so Object/Lamp responses don't match the declared schema
body:
**Environment:** macOS, Archicad 28, Tapir add-on 1.5.7.

### Summary

`GetDetailsOfElements` returns the full `ObjectDetails` payload for `Object` (and, by the same struct, `Lamp`) elements, but the response schema does not allow it: `ObjectDetails` exists as a definition in `common_schema_definitions.js`, yet it is **not listed in the `TypeSpecificDetails` oneOf** that `GetDetailsOfElements` declares as its per-element `details`. The only variant available for library-part-based elements is still `LibPartBasedElementDetails`, which allows just `libPart`, `ownerElementId` and `ownerElementType`.

The result is that the declared schema contradicts the actual response for these element types. Any client that validates responses against the published schema fails on every Object and Lamp.

### Verification against the 1.5.7 tag

Parsing `docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js` at tag `1.5.7`:

- `"ObjectDetails" in defs` -> **True**
- `TypeSpecificDetails.oneOf` -> 18 variants:
  `WallDetails, BeamDetails, SlabDetails, ColumnDetails, DetailWorksheetDetails, WindowDoorDetails, LibPartBasedElementDetails, PolylineDetails, ZoneDetails, CurtainWallDetails, CurtainWallSegmentDetails, CurtainWallPanelDetails, CurtainWallFrameDetails, MeshDetails, MorphDetails, DrawingDetails, LabelDetails, NotYetSupportedElementTypeDetails`
- `"ObjectDetails" in TypeSpecificDetails.oneOf` -> **False**

### Actual response

For a single Object element, the add-on returns (fields abbreviated):

```json
{
  "libPart": { "name": "Skylight Flat ...", "guid": "..." },
  "origin": { "x": 569.632265602, "y": 318.986426431, "z": 3.1 },
  "dimensions": { "x": 0.6, "y": 0.6, "z": 0.28 },
  "angle": 0,
  "pen": 4,
  "lineTypeId": { "guid": "28A7C677-..." },
  "sectionFillId": { "guid": "2A41CB21-..." },
  "sectionFillPen": 104,
  "sectionFillBackgroundPen": 124,
  "sectionContourPen": 24,
  "useObjectPens": true,
  "useObjectLineTypes": true,
  "useObjectMaterials": true,
  "useObjectSectionAttributes": true,
  "reflected": true,
  "useFixSize": true,
  "fixPoint": 0,
  "offset": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "useFixedAngle": false,
  "isAutoOnStoryVisibility": false,
  "visibility": { "...": "..." },
  "linkToSettings": { "...": "..." }
}
```

That is exactly the `ObjectDetails` shape introduced in #450 — the definition was added, but not wired into the union.

### Suggested fix

Add `ObjectDetails` to the `TypeSpecificDetails` oneOf.

If `LibPartBasedElementDetails` is still the intended variant for some other library-part-based type, both can coexist in the oneOf; the discriminating fields differ enough that validation stays unambiguous.

Happy to test a fix against a real project — we have ~30 interior elevation views and a few hundred library objects to throw at it.

title: GDLParameterDetails declares dimension1/dimension2 as required, but the add-on only returns them for array parameters
body:
**Environment:** macOS, Archicad 28, Tapir add-on 1.5.7.

### Summary

In `common_schema_definitions.js`, `GDLParameterDetails` lists `dimension1` and `dimension2` in its `required` array — while the description of those same two fields says they only apply to arrays:

```json
"dimension1": { "type": "integer", "description": "The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value)." },
"dimension2": { "type": "integer", "description": "The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value)." }
```

```
GDLParameterDetails.required =
  ["name", "displayName", "index", "type", "dimension1", "dimension2", "value", "isLocked", "flags"]
```

The add-on behaves as the descriptions say: for scalar parameters it omits both fields, which is correct. But the schema declares them mandatory, so the response does not validate against its own published schema.

### Reproduction

`GetGDLParametersOfElements` on a single Door (a 4200x2920 aluminium terrace door, 940 GDL parameters) -> **1802 validation errors**, i.e. two per parameter, all of the form:

```
gdlParametersOfElements.0.parameters.0.dimension1
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'name': 'A', 'displayName': ..., 'HaveCustomValue': False}]
gdlParametersOfElements.0.parameters.0.dimension2
  Field required [type=missing, ...]
```

Every failing parameter is a scalar (`A`, `B`, `ZZYZX`, `AC_WallContours`, `ac_bottomlevel`, `ifc_LiningDepth`, …). Array-valued parameters carry both fields and validate fine.

### Suggested fix

Move `dimension1` and `dimension2` out of `required` in `GDLParameterDetails`, so they are optional and only present for array values — matching both the field descriptions and the actual behaviour.

### Note

This was previously reported downstream as a client-side schema problem (SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP#25). Having now checked the source schema at tag 1.5.7, the mismatch originates here, not in the client.

title: Wall/Slab/Column/Beam: fill the gaps left by the existing commands
body:
## Summary

Wall, Slab, Column and Beam already had Create/Get/Modify commands, but each one only covered a subset of the element's real Archicad fields - callers could place these elements but not fully read back or edit them (materials, pens, fills, story visibility, cross section, custom profiles, etc. were all missing). This normally completes the four element types end to end: every field returned by `GetDetailsOfElements` is now also settable via the matching Create/Modify command, and vice versa.

- **Wall**: referenceLineLocation, slant (`profileType` + slantAlpha/slantBeta), top offset/story, zoneRel, story visibility (+ isAutoOnStoryVisibility), reference/opposite/side materials, cut fill pens, and a working `structureType=Profile` (previously broken even at creation - the existing code forced an invalid polygonal plan shape that has nothing to do with a profiled cross section).
- **Slab**: referencePlaneLocation, top/side/bottom materials, cut fill pens, floor fill (pens, fill attribute, hatch orientation). Also fixes the `ModifySlabs` polygon-editing crash: outline/hole changes now go through `ACAPI_Polygon_InsertPolyNode/DeletePolyNode/InsertSubPoly/DeleteSubPoly` + `ACAPI_Element_ChangeMemo` instead of an unsafe from-scratch memo rebuild, version-gated to `ACAPI_Goodies` on pre-AC27 builds.
- **Column**: axis rotation, slant, wrapping, top offset/story, coreAnchor, cut fill pens, cover fill, and full cross section support that didn't exist before: width/depth/circleBased/isWidthAndHeightLinked/buildingMaterialId/profileId are now all readable and settable, including real profile-based ("complex profile") columns.
- **Beam**: beam shape, slant, flip, profile angle, anchor point, holes, cut fill pens, cover fill, and the same new cross section support as Column, including profile-based beams.

`CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` documents all of the above, including notes on the Archicad-side field interactions this had to reverse-engineer (height vs relativeTopStory, topOffset needing relativeTopStory on Wall, Core reference line locations needing Composite/Profile structure, isFlipped being a no-op on a circular column).

**Remaining known gap**, left out as a separate, larger chantier: floorIndex is still create-only for all four types (moving an existing element to another floor needs different handling than a plain field).

## Note on overlap with other open PRs

This branch was extracted from an older working tree and predates #463 ("SetDetailsOfElements: modify any element type..."), which restructures the `Modify*` command bodies and the `Apply*Details` dispatch. If #463 merges first, this PR will need a rebase - the field additions here are independent of that refactor's mechanics.

Also fixes the same `ModifySlabs` polygon crash as #504/#500 (this PR ports the #504 fix, already reviewed there).

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 build clean, live-tested: 84/84 checks in `test_wall_slab_column_beam_details.py`, covering every field above under maximalist combinations (curved/multi-hole slabs, all-fields-at-once Modify calls, profile-based columns/beams) plus the ModifySlabs crash regression
- [x] AC25 build clean
- [x] AC27 build clean

title: ModifyBeams: `profileAngle` is missing, and `slantAngle` is silently ignored
body:
## Summary

Two related problems with beams in `ModifyBeams` / `CreateBeams` (tested on Tapir 1.5.2,
Archicad 29 STUDIO, Windows):

1. **`profileAngle` is not supported at all.** There is no way to set the beam's
   *Profile Rotation Angle* (the "軸回転" / "Rotation Angle" field in the
   *Reference Axis* group of Beam Settings) through the API. `API_ColumnType` has an
   equivalent field exposed as `axisRotationAngle` in `ModifyColumns`, but the beam
   counterpart `API_BeamType::profileAngle` is not exposed anywhere.

2. **`slantAngle` reports success but has no effect.** `ApplyBeamDetails` writes
   `element.beam.slantAngle` and sets the mask bit, but never sets
   `API_BeamType::isSlanted`. Archicad therefore keeps the beam in "Horizontal" mode
   and discards the angle. `ModifyBeams` still returns `success: true`.

Additionally, `GetDetailsOfElements` does not return either value for beams, so a
caller cannot even read back what is currently set. `slantAngle` is always reported
as `0.0`.

## Use case

Placing purlins on a curved (barrel) roof. Each purlin has to be rotated about its
own axis so that its web stays perpendicular to the roof surface. The angle is
computed from a guide curve, then written back per element. Everything works except
the final write — the geometry is correct, only the rotation cannot be applied.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place a horizontal beam.
2. Send a single `ModifyBeams` request that changes two fields at once:

```json
{
  "beamsWithDetails": [
    {
      "elementId": { "guid": "<beam-guid>" },
      "offset": 0.2,
      "slantAngle": 0.5
    }
  ]
}
```

3. Response: `{"executionResults":[{"success":true}]}`
4. Call `Get3DBoundingBoxes` on the same element.

**Expected:** the bounding box shifts by 0.2 m *and* becomes wider/taller because the
cross-section is rotated by 0.5 rad.

**Actual:** the bounding box shifts by exactly 0.2 m (so the request *was* applied,
and this is not a caching or rebuild problem), but the cross-section extents are
unchanged. `RebuildView` with `regenerate: true` does not change this.

Verified values (100 x 50 profile):

| | xMin | xMax | zMin | zMax |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1.808605 | 1.858605 | 18.961467 | 19.061467 |
| after  | 1.608605 | 1.658605 | 18.961467 | 19.061467 |

Width stays 0.050 and height stays 0.100.

## Suggested fix

In `archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, `ApplyBeamDetails ()`:

```cpp
    auto slantAngle = GetOptionalDouble (details, "slantAngle");
    if (slantAngle.HasValue ()) {
        element.beam.slantAngle = slantAngle.Get ();
        element.beam.isSlanted  = true;                              // <-- added
        ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET (mask, API_BeamType, slantAngle);
        ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET (mask, API_BeamType, isSlanted);      // <-- added
        changed = true;
    }
    auto profileAngle = GetOptionalDouble (details, "profileAngle"); // <-- new block
    if (profileAngle.HasValue ()) {
        element.beam.profileAngle = profileAngle.Get ();
        ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET (mask, API_BeamType, profileAngle);
        changed = true;
    }
```

plus the matching `"profileAngle"` entry in the `ModifyBeams` / `CreateBeams` input
schemas, and both fields in the `GetDetailsOfElements` beam output so they can be
read back.

Note on `isSlanted`: I am not sure what the intended neutral value of `slantAngle`
is (Beam Settings shows 90.00 deg for a horizontal beam, but `GetDetailsOfElements`
currently reports `0.0`). If `PI/2` is the neutral value, guarding the flag with
`isSlanted = fabs (slantAngle.Get () - PI / 2.0) > EPS;` would be more correct than
setting it unconditionally.

title: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection: no command can return an API_SectElemID, making the command unreachable
body:
# CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection: no command can return an API_SectElemID, making the command unreachable

**Tapir add-on:** 1.5.7 · **Archicad:** 29 (build 3200, CZE) · **OS:** Windows 11
**Source references:** `main` @ `f76377a` (ADDON_VERSION 1.5.7)

## Summary

`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` requires `sectionElementId` to reference an element of
type `API_SectElemID`. No Tapir command returns such a GUID: every element-listing path converts
section elements to their owner element. The only place a raw section GUID escapes is
`GetDimensionData`, i.e. reading back a dimension that already exists — which makes the command
unreachable for any new work.

`"SectElem"` *is* accepted as an input type string (`CommandBase.cpp:492` maps it to
`API_SectElemID`), but no command ever emits one. This looks like incomplete plumbing rather than
an intentional design.

## Expected

Given a section database, list the elements drawn in it and pass one to
`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`.

## Actual

Every obtainable GUID is the owner GUID, which the command rejects:

```
{"code": -2130313112,
 "message": "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element."}
```

## Where the two sides disagree

**Producer side** — conversion is unconditional, no flag disables it:

- `ElementCommands.cpp:137` — `GetParentElemOfSectElem`, returns `element.sectElem.parentGuid`
- `ElementCommands.cpp:202` — the `else` branch applies it to every element
- `ElementCommands.cpp:193` — same for objects
- `ElementCommands.cpp:1943` — `GetSelectedElements` converts as well
- `ElementCommands.hpp:15` — `GetAllElementsCommand` derives from `GetElementsByTypeCommand`,
  so it goes through the same path

**Consumer side** — requires exactly what the producer side removed:

- `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp:560-580` — `LoadSectionElementAndParent`:

```cpp
if (ACAPI_Element_Get (&sectionElement) != NoError ||
    GetElemTypeId (sectionElement.header) != API_SectElemID) {
    return "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element.";
}
```

**Only leak** — `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp:4639`, `GetDimensionData`, which returns
`baseElementId` of existing witness points.

## Reproduction

```python
db = RunTapirCommand('GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId',
                     {'navigatorItemIds': [{'navigatorItemId': {'guid': SECTION_NAV_GUID}}]})['databases'][0]

els = RunTapirCommand('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'SectElem', 'databases': [db]})['elements']
# -> owner GUIDs. GetDetailsOfElements reports their type as "Wall"/"Slab", never "SectElem";
#    93 of them are members of the floor plan's Wall list.

RunTapirCommand('CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'sectionElementId': els[0]['elementId'],
    'referencePoint': {'x': 1.0, 'y': -1.0},
    'preset': 'SlabCompositeFaces',
    'direction': {'x': 0, 'y': 1}}]})
# -> "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element."
```

Verified that no path yields a usable ID:

- `GetAllElements` on the section database: 1040 elements, none of them a section element
- `GetElementsByType`: owner GUIDs for every type
- `GetSelectedElements`: with `GetCurrentWindowType` confirmed as `"Section"` and 7 cut elements
  picked by hand in that window (ceiling slab, two floor slabs, foundation slab, partition wall,
  foundation blocks, footing), all 7 came back as owner GUIDs — each present both in the converted
  `"SectElem"` listing and in the floor plan database.

The command itself works correctly once a real ID is supplied:

```python
data = RunTapirCommand('GetDimensionData', {'elements': [{'elementId': {'guid': EXISTING_DIM}}]})
sect_guid = data['dimensionsData'][0]['witnessPoints'][1]['baseElementId']
# same call with this GUID -> chain is created
```

## A: make section element IDs obtainable

1. An opt-in flag on `GetElementsByType` / `GetAllElements` (e.g. `keepSectionElements: true`)
   that skips `GetParentElemOfSectElem`.
2. A new command, e.g. `GetSectionElementsOfElements`, mapping owner GUIDs + database to the
   section elements drawn for them.
3. Letting `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` take an owner GUID plus the target database and
   resolve internally would be the nicest API, but it is ambiguous: one element can produce several
   section elements in the same section (a wall crossed at two places), with no way to say which
   one is meant. Options 1 and 2 do not have this problem.

## B: multi-element chains do not bind, even with valid section element IDs

This is a **separate defect**, not a consequence of A, and it was verified with IDs proven valid in
the same run.

Every preset uses the single `sectionElement.header.guid` for all of its points, so one call can
only ever dimension one element. Real section dimension chains span many elements — a typical
exterior chain runs: bottom of footing → top of footing → finished grade → facade insulation change
→ window sill → window head → soffit → ridge, i.e. 5-10 witness points on 5-10 different elements.

The general `CreateAssociativeDimensions` looks like it should cover this, since
`ParseAssociativeDimensionPoint` (`ExtendedElementCommands.cpp:432-448`) derives `point.elementType`
from the element header via `LoadElementHeaderByGuid` rather than from a parameter — so a section
element ought to be accepted. It is not.

Test, Tapir 1.5.7, section window active, both GUIDs harvested from `GetDimensionData` and
confirmed as `type == "SectElem"` by `GetDetailsOfElements`:

```python
A = '3635A7E4-...'   # SectElem, layer "Dosky - podlahy exteriér", section y = -0.010
B = '17F32439-...'   # SectElem, layer "Základy - pásy",            section y = -3.200

# proof that A is a live, valid API_SectElemID:
RunTapirCommand('CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'sectionElementId': {'guid': A}, 'referencePoint': {'x': -8.0, 'y': -1.0},
    'preset': 'SlabCompositeFaces', 'direction': {'x': 0, 'y': 1}}]})
# -> succeeds, chain created

# the same GUID plus a second one, through the general command:
RunTapirCommand('CreateAssociativeDimensions', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'referencePoint': {'x': -9.0, 'y': -1.0}, 'direction': {'x': 0, 'y': 1}, 'floorIndex': 0,
    'witnessPoints': [{'elementId': {'guid': A}, 'inIndex': 1},
                      {'elementId': {'guid': B}, 'inIndex': 1}]}]})
# -> a dimension IS created in the section database, but both witness points collapse to
#    (0.000, 0.000) with dimensionValue 0 and no baseElementId. Same for inIndex 2 and 0.
```

Control run — the identical call with the identical witness point shape works on the floor plan:
with the floor plan window active and two plan wall GUIDs, both points bind with real coordinates
and `baseElementId` set (`x=0.200 y=0.200` and `x=0.200 y=6.800`, `dimensionValue 6.600`). So the
failure is specific to the section context, not to the elements or to the request shape.

The points are not bound even though the IDs are valid section elements. Fixing A alone would
therefore still leave section dimensioning limited to one small chain per element, which is not
what section drawings look like.

Requested: make `CreateAssociativeDimensions` bind witness points that reference section elements
when the target database is a section, or accept an explicit `witnessPoints` array in
`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`. Presets would remain a convenience on top of that.

title: CreateWallThicknessDimensions returns a new element GUID but creates nothing when a section window is active
body:
**Tapir add-on:** 1.5.7 · **Archicad:** 29 (build 3200, CZE) · **OS:** Windows 11
**Source references:** `main` @ `f76377a`

## Actual

With a section window active, `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` reports success and returns a fresh
element GUID, but no dimension is created anywhere. The returned GUID exists in none of the
project's databases.

```python
RunTapirCommand('CreateWallThicknessDimensions', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'wallId': {'guid': WALL_GUID},
    'referencePoint': {'x': 2.0, 'y': -2.0},
    'direction': {'x': 1, 'y': 0}}]})
# -> {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "BC7DADCB-ED97-46FE-AB05-0D6C8A99065A"}}]}
```

Checked all 29 databases of the project (stories, sections, elevations, worksheets, details) for
the returned GUIDs: not present in any of them. Dimension counts were unchanged before and after
(floor plan 242, sections 24 / 19 / 0). Three of four test walls behaved this way; the fourth
returned a proper error (`"Failed to create wall thickness dimension."`), which is the correct
behaviour.

## Expected

Either create the dimension, or return an error. Reporting a GUID for an element that does not
exist is the problematic part — a caller has no way to detect the failure.

## Possible cause

`ExtendedElementCommands.cpp:4016` sets

```cpp
element.header.floorInd = wall.header.floorInd;
```

which is a floor-plan assumption. In a section database there is no floor index to speak of, so
the element is likely created into a database where it cannot live, then discarded — while the
GUID has already been handed back to the caller.

title: fix(dimensions): verify created dimensions exist instead of returning ghost GUIDs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #510. With a section or elevation window active, `ACAPI_Element_Create` for a floor-plan dimension can report success and hand back a GUID although **no element was created in any database**. `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` (and `CreateAssociativeDimensions`, which shares the failure mode) then returned that ghost GUID to the caller, who had no way to detect the failure.

## Change

After a successful create, load the element back via `ACAPI_Element_Get`. If it does not exist, return a controlled per-item error pointing at the active-window cause ("is a section or elevation window active? Activate a floor plan window and retry") instead of a non-existent id. Applied to both `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` and `CreateAssociativeDimensions`.

An alternative would be to switch to the floor-plan database before creating (and restore afterwards) so the call works from any window — happy to build that instead if preferred; the post-create check felt like the least invasive correct behaviour.

## Testing (live against AC28, Win)

- Normal path (floor plan active): wall-thickness dimension still created and returned normally — the guard does not fire on success.
- The ghost scenario is environment-dependent (reported on AC29/CZE with a section window active); the guard is a conservative post-check that can only convert a ghost GUID into a clean error, never affect a successful create.

Built clean on AC28 (Win, VS2019).

body:
## Summary

A Morph body could only ever be built as a closed volume: `CreateMorphs`/`ModifyMorphs` required at least 4 vertices and 4 faces (a tetrahedron) for ANY body, even for `bodyType: Surface` - which is Archicad's own open-shell body type and has no closedness requirement at all. `ACAPI_Body_*` itself never enforced this (an edge is only ever required to have *at most* two side polygons per its own doc - having zero or one is a normal open/boundary/standalone edge); this was Tapir's own validation being stricter than necessary.

- A Surface body's real minimum (confirmed live) is 2 vertices joined by a single edge - either a real face loop or just a standalone `wireEdge`. A lone vertex with no edge at all is rejected by Archicad itself (`ACAPI_Element_Create` fails), not something Tapir can work around.
- New `"filled": false` flag on a `polygons` entry: creates that loop's edges without an actual face (e.g. a wireframe rectangle outline, or a pyramid with a filled base but wireframe-only sides).
- New `"wireEdges"` field, symmetric between Get and Create/Modify (same shape as `edgeOverrides`/`polygons`): standalone edges belonging to no face at all. Previously these were entirely invisible on read - an edge with no adjacent polygon never appeared in `polygons`, so a caller reading back a body containing wire geometry had no way to know it was there, and the "extra" vertices Archicad keeps for those edges looked like unexplained bloat in the vertex list.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live on AC27 (build + deploy + test): 17/17 checks in the new `test_morph_open_shells.py` - the absolute minimum (single edge, no face), a lone-vertex rejection, a single open face, a box missing a face, a wireframe-only loop, standalone `wireEdges` round-tripped through Create, and a mixed filled-base/wireframe-sides pyramid (also used to confirm Get's vertex indices - which Archicad is free to renumber after `ACAPI_Body_Finish` - stay internally consistent by decoding edges/polygons through the returned vertex coordinates rather than assuming they match the caller's original input order)
- [x] The pre-existing `create_modify_delete_morph.py` closed-box sample still runs clean, no regression on the ordinary case
- [ ] AC25/29 build not re-verified in this PR (iterated on AC27 only this session) - flagging for a maintainer/CI check before merge

title: Fix CreateLayerCombinations/ModifyLayerCombinations dropping per-layer stats
body:
Closes #513.

## Summary

`CreateLayerCombinations` accepted per-layer `isHidden`/`isLocked`/`isWireframe`/`intersectionGroupNr`, but they were silently lost on both create and modify (`overwriteExisting`): only the combination's name and layer membership actually saved, every per-layer stat came back at its default (visible, unlocked, not wireframe, group 1) regardless of what was requested.

Two independent bugs were stacked in the same function, both confirmed live against a 59-layer test project.

**Main bug**: a layer combination's stat table is not sparse. The AC27 devkit's own remark on `API_LayerCombType` says `lNumb` "has the same value in all layer combinations" - i.e. it's the project's total layer count, and Archicad expects one `API_LayerStat` entry per project layer, not just for the ones a caller mentions. The existing code built `layer_statItems` with only the requested layer(s). Reading the combination back showed every layer NOT explicitly listed with scattered, inconsistent flags (mostly `isHidden=true`, one random layer `isWireframe=true`) instead of the documented "new layers appear as visible and unlocked" - Archicad was reading past the sparse table into uninitialized memory for any layer index it was never given.

**Fix**: seed a full entry for every project layer first (preferring the combination's own existing stat table as the seed when modifying, so untouched layers keep their existing state instead of being reset to defaults; falling back to enumerating every project layer via `ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesByType` for a brand new combination), then apply the caller's overrides on top - the same pattern `CreatePenTables`/`CreateProfiles` already use.

**Second bug**, found while testing the first fix: the override step used `GS::HashTable::Add`, which is a no-op returning `false` when the key already exists (every key was already seeded) - the requested overrides still never landed even with a fully seeded table. `Put` is required to unconditionally replace an existing entry.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live on AC27 against the issue's exact repro plus every variant from its own falsification sweep (single layer, multiple layers in one request, the full 59-layer list with one flag flipped), plus modifying one layer while confirming another layer's already-set custom flags are preserved: 12/12 checks in the new `test_layer_combination_stats.py`
- [x] AC25 build clean
- [x] AC29 build clean
- [ ] AC26 not checked this round

title: main: no add-on commands are registered at all — Initialize() stops at TapirPalette::Instance()
body:
Summary

On current main (ADDON_VERSION 1.5.7) the add-on loads and its UI works, but not a single JSON add-on command is registered. Every API.ExecuteAddOnCommand call fails with:

4010  Archicad does not have the registered Add-On command with the name : TapirCommand.<name>

The released 1.5.2 binary works fine on the same machine, and so does the 1.5.2 tag built by me with the identical toolchain. I bisected it down to one line in Initialize():

cpp
TapirPalette::Instance ();

Commenting out that single line in archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnMain.cpp restores all commands.

Why the symptom looks confusing

The ordering inside Initialize() is:

  1. ACAPI_MenuItem_InstallMenuHandler (...) — menu handlers
  2. TapirPalette::RegisterPaletteControlCallBack () / ScriptUIPalette::...
  3. TapirPalette::Instance ();
  4. RegisterCommand<...> for every command

Because the menu handlers are installed before step 3 and the command registrations come after it, the add-on looks perfectly healthy from the UI side:

  • Add-On Manager lists it as loaded, version 1.5.7
  • The Tapir menu is present and fully populated
  • About Tapir… opens and reports Version: 1.5.7, Port: 19723

…while every JSON client is dead. That is consistent with execution stopping at step 3 (an exception escaping the singleton construction), so err |= accumulation never even reaches the command block.

Environment

  • Archicad 29 STUDIO, build 5101, JPN, Windows 11
  • API DevKit 29.3000
  • VS Build Tools 2022, toolset v143 (MSVC 14.41.34120), Windows SDK 10.0.22621.0
  • CMake 4.4.1, generator Visual Studio 17 2022, config RelWithDebInfo
  • Compiler flags: /source-charset:.1252 /execution-charset:.1252 (needed on a Japanese locale, otherwise C4819 is promoted to an error by /WX)

Steps to reproduce

  1. Build main for AC29 and install the resulting .apx
  2. Restart Archicad and open any project
  3. POST http://127.0.0.1:19723 with:
json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": { "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetAddOnVersion" },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {}
  }
}
  1. Response:
json
{"succeeded": false, "error": {"code": 4010, "message": "Archicad does not have the registered Add-On command with the name : TapirCommand.GetAddOnVersion"}}

API.GetProductInfo succeeds on the same connection, so the JSON server itself is fine.

Test matrix

Build | Commands registered -- | -- Official 1.5.2 release binary | yes 1.5.2 tag, built by me, same toolchain | yes main @ f76377a, built by me | no main @ f76377a minus TapirPalette::Instance (); | yes PR #507 branch, built by me | no PR #507 branch minus TapirPalette::Instance (); | yes

The toolchain, Archicad build, locale and edition are constant across all rows, so the difference is purely in the source.

Impact

If this ships, every JSON / Python / Grasshopper client loses all Tapir commands while the add-on still appears installed and healthy in the UI. The failure mode gives no hint that the palette is involved.

Notes / guesses

The comment above the call says it forces the palette singleton and its saved shortcut-slot preferences to load immediately. Reading those preferences at Initialize() time is my first suspect — possibly it throws when the preference blob is absent, or is in an unexpected state. It may well be locale- or profile-dependent, which would explain why CI and other developers have not hit it.

Suggested minimal hardening regardless of root cause: move the command registrations before the palette warm-up, and/or wrap the warm-up in a try/catch so that a palette problem can never take the JSON API down with it.

I am happy to test any patch — I have a working local build setup and can reproduce this reliably.

title: GRASSHOPPER PLUGIN - ELEMENT CREATION & MODIFICATION SUBCATEGORIES: CREATE TOOGLEABLE INDIVIDUAL INPUTS FOR ADDITIONAL SETTINGS
body:
GitHub Issue: Refactor "Additional Settings" into Dynamically Toggleable Parameters
Description:
The current "additional settings" input is confusing and not functionally intuitive for users. To improve interface clarity and prevent canvas clutter, please deprecate this single input and expose all additional settings as individual, discrete input parameters.

Because exposing all parameters simultaneously would create an excessively long component node, these new inputs must be dynamically hidden or shown based on user preference, mimicking the behavior seen in the new Elefront plugin.

Technical Implementation Directives:
To achieve this in our compiled C# Grasshopper plugin, please implement the following mechanisms:

1. State Management & Serialization (Critical)

Create internal private boolean flags (e.g., _showSettingA, _showSettingB) to track the visibility state of each optional parameter.

You must override the Write(GH_IWriter writer) and Read(GH_IReader reader) methods to serialize these boolean states. If you do not save the visibility state, the dynamically added parameters will cause deserialization errors or simply vanish when the user closes and reopens the .gh canvas document.

2. Context Menu Injection

Override the AppendAdditionalComponentMenuItems(ToolStripDropDown menu) method.

Add checkable menu items for each optional parameter using Menu_AppendItem().

Include a "Show All" or "Reset to Default" menu option to quickly restore the standard parameter layout.

3. Canvas & Parameter Mutations

When a menu item is toggled, wrap the logic in RecordUndoEvent("Toggle Parameter") so the user can safely Ctrl+Z the interface change.

To add a parameter: Instantiate the specific parameter type (e.g., Param_Number, Param_String) and use Params.RegisterInputParam().

To remove a parameter: Find the parameter in Params.Input and use Params.UnregisterInputParameter().

You must invoke Params.OnParametersChanged() followed by ExpireSolution(true) to force Grasshopper to redraw the node and recalculate the data tree execution.

4. Alternative ZUI Approach (Optional Consideration)

While the right-click menu is our primary target for this refactor, keep in mind that Grasshopper also supports a Zoomable User Interface (ZUI). This allows users to modify inputs and outputs by zooming in until Insert [ ⊕ ] and Remove [ ⊖ ] controls are visible on either side of the component. If evaluating this route as a cleaner alternative to the right-click menu, implement the IGH_VariableParameterComponent interface instead of the manual menu overrides.

title: Register all commands before loading the palette singleton
body:
## Summary

Fixes #516 — on `main` (1.5.7) no JSON add-on command was registered at all: every `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` returned `4010 Archicad does not have the registered Add-On command`, while the Add-On Manager, the Tapir menu and the About dialog all looked perfectly healthy. Reported independently by two users, both of whom had to downgrade to 1.5.2.

## Root cause

`Initialize()` forced the palette singleton *before* the command registrations:

```cpp
TapirPalette::Instance ();   // <- added in #479, purely to refresh shortcut menu labels
{ // Application Commands
    err |= RegisterCommand<GetAddOnVersionCommand> (...);
    ...
```

`TapirPalette` is a `DG::Palette`; constructing it that early aborts the remainder of `Initialize()` on some configurations (the reporter bisected it to exactly this line, and confirmed that removing it restores all commands). Because the menu handlers are installed *before* that line and every `RegisterCommand` call comes *after* it, the add-on kept a fully working UI while every JSON/Python/Grasshopper client was dead — a failure mode that gives no hint the palette is involved.

## Fix

The singleton load moves to the very end of `Initialize()`, after all command groups, and is wrapped so no failure can escape:

```cpp
try {
    TapirPalette::Instance ();
} catch (...) {
}
```

Commands are therefore always registered regardless of what the palette does. The palette load only affects the shortcut menu labels and their enabled state, which is cosmetic — if it fails, those are applied later, the first time the palette is actually opened or a shortcut is triggered (exactly the behavior before #479).

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build succeeds
- [x] Install the built add-on and confirm `GetAddOnVersion` responds (instead of error 4010), and that the shortcut menu labels/enabled states still appear at startup on a machine where the palette constructs normally

title: Add ObjectDetails to the TypeSpecificDetails union
body:
## Summary

Fixes #505. `GetDetailsOfElements` returns the full `ObjectDetails` payload (origin, dimensions, angle, pens, attributes, visibility, …) for `Object` and `Lamp` elements, but `ObjectDetails` was never added to the `TypeSpecificDetails` `oneOf` when it was introduced in #450. The only variant that could match those responses was `LibPartBasedElementDetails`, which allows just `libPart`, `ownerElementId` and `ownerElementType` — so every Object and Lamp failed schema validation for clients that check responses.

## Fix

`ObjectDetails` is added to the `TypeSpecificDetails` union (19 variants now), right after `LibPartBasedElementDetails`. The union stays unambiguous: `LibPartBasedElementDetails` has `additionalProperties: false` with only those three properties, so a full Object payload can only match `ObjectDetails`.

The generated `docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js` is refreshed from the definitions so the published docs reflect it on merge.

## Test plan

title: Make slantAngle take effect on beams and columns
body:
## Summary

Fixes #508. Note that two of the three reported points were already fixed on `main` after the report (which was against 1.5.2) by 0cc70c9 "Wall/Slab/Column/Beam: fill the gaps left by the existing commands": `ModifyBeams` gained `profileAngle` and `isSlanted`, and `GetDetailsOfElements` now returns `slantAngle`, `isSlanted` and `profileAngle` for beams. What remained is the actual silent no-op and the create-side gap.

## What this changes

**1. `slantAngle` alone no longer silently does nothing.** `API_BeamType::isSlanted` (and `API_ColumnType::isSlanted`) must be set for Archicad to leave "Horizontal"/"Vertical" mode; otherwise the angle is discarded while the command still reports `success: true`. `slantAngle` now derives `isSlanted` (`slantAngle != 0`) when the caller does not pass `isSlanted` explicitly — an explicit value always wins. Applied in `ApplyBeamDetails`, `ApplyColumnDetails` (same latent bug) and the `CreateBeams` path.

**2. `CreateBeams` gains `isSlanted` and `profileAngle`**, matching `ModifyBeams`, so a slanted or profile-rotated beam can be created in a single call instead of create-then-modify.

## Test plan

title: Offer value lists for the string inputs with fixed options
body:
## Summary

Fixes #522. Inputs that accept only a fixed set of strings had to be typed by hand — `"ReferencePlaneLocation"`, `"ReferenceLineLocation"`, `"StructureType"` and friends — and any typo produced a command-side error rather than a hint.

Nine value lists are added and the creation/modification components now **attach the matching one automatically** when dropped on the canvas (the same behavior `GetConnectedElements` already had with the element type value list), so the options can be picked from a dropdown right away:

| Value list | Attached to |
|---|---|
| StructureTypes | CreateWalls, CreateRoofs, ModifyWalls, ModifySlabs, ModifyRoofs |
| ReferenceLineLocations | CreateWalls |
| ReferencePlaneLocations | CreateSlabs |
| AnchorPoints | CreateBeams (AnchorPoints), CreateColumns (CoreAnchors) |
| TextJustifications | CreateTexts |
| MeshSkirtTypes / MeshRidgeTypes | CreateMeshes, ModifyMeshes |
| DimensioningPresets | CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection |
| MEPDomains | (available for the MEP group) |

They are ordinary value lists too, so they can be placed manually from the same subcategory panel as the components they serve — Grasshopper has no second-level subcategory, so that is as close to the requested "utility node for that subcategory" as the API allows.

## Implementation

- `Types/Generic/OptionEnums.cs` — the option sets as C# enums, so the offered values are generated from one place and stay in sync with the command schemas.
- `Components/OptionValueLists.cs` — the nine `ValueList` classes.
- `CreateElementsComponentBase` / `ModifyElementsComponentBase` — `Field` gains an optional `valueList` factory, and `AddedToDocument` attaches it to that field's input (offset by one in the Modify base, where ElementGuids comes first).

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build TapirGrasshopperPlugin.sln` succeeds with 0 warnings/errors
- [ ] Drop CreateWalls on the canvas: StructureTypes and ReferenceLineLocations dropdowns appear pre-wired; the same for CreateSlabs (ReferencePlaneLocations) and CreateTexts (Justifications)

title: Support a per-item favoriteName in the creation commands
body:
## Summary

Fixes #519, implementing what was asked for in the issue: **all element types, applied per item.**

Every command built on `CreateElementsCommandBase` now takes an optional `favoriteName` per item — CreateWalls, CreateBeams, CreateColumns, CreateSlabs, CreateStairs, CreateZones, CreateMeshes, CreateObjects, CreateLamps, CreatePolylines, CreateTexts, CreateLabels and the six 2D creators (Lines, Arcs, Circles, Hotspots, Hatches, Splines). The favorite's settings are applied first, then the fields given explicitly in the same item override them, so one call can create elements from different favorites.

`CreateWindows` / `CreateDoors` keep their existing `favoriteName` implementation — they are markered types needing `ChangeDefaultsExt` with the favorite's marker sub-element, and their create path clones the tool defaults itself.

## How it works, and the one caveat

Favorites can only be applied through the **tool defaults**, which are global and outlive the command. The implementation therefore:

- snapshots the tool defaults before the loop (only when at least one item names a favorite — otherwise nothing extra happens and the previous code path is untouched);
- applies the favorite, re-reads the defaults, and creates the element from them;
- **restores the snapshot before any item that does not name a favorite**, so a mixed batch does not silently inherit the previous item's favorite;
- restores the snapshot again at the end, so the user's next manual placement is unaffected.

A favorite belonging to a different element type is rejected per item with `APIERR_REFUSEDPAR` rather than corrupting the tool state.

The shared helper `ApplyFavoriteToElementDefaults` mirrors `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaultsCommand` (element state + classifications + category values + user properties — some favorites are rejected by the create call without that extra metadata).

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build succeeds
- [ ] Live: `CreateWalls` with two items naming **different** wall favorites creates two differently-configured walls
- [ ] Live: a mixed batch (item 1 with `favoriteName`, item 2 without) — item 2 must come out with the plain tool defaults, not item 1's favorite
- [ ] Live: after the call, placing an element manually still uses the tool defaults from before the call
- [ ] Live: a wrong-type favorite (e.g. a door favorite passed to `CreateWalls`) reports a per-item error and does not disturb the other items

Follow-up (not in this PR): the creators implemented through `ExecuteCreateWithElements` — CreateMorphs, CreateRoofs, CreateOpenings and the associative dimensions — use a different create path and would need the same treatment; happy to do that next if wanted.

title: CreateWalls: a complex-profile Wall tool default silently overrides explicit parameters (defaults memo leak)
body:
## Summary

When the seat's **Wall tool default** is set to a complex-profile wall, `CreateWalls` silently ignores every explicit parameter except `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate`. The wall is created without error — at the tool default's size and structure. With the tool default set to a Basic wall, the identical call produces exactly the requested wall.

This is not a regression: we reproduced it identically on three builds (`0cc70c97` / 3 Aug, `ef7f5226` / 9 Aug main, and one PR build), Archicad 28 build 6003 INT, Windows 11.

## Repro

1. In the Archicad UI: open Wall default settings, set Structure to **Complex Profile** (any profile), OK.
2. Call:

```json
{ "command": "CreateWalls", "parameters": { "wallsData": [ {
  "begCoordinate": { "x": 0.0, "y": 15.0 },
  "endCoordinate": { "x": 1.0, "y": 15.0 },
  "height": 1.111,
  "thickness": 0.333
} ] } }
```

3. Measure the created wall (`Get3DBoundingBoxes`, or `GetDetailsOfElements`).

**Expected:** a 333 mm thick, 1.111 m high Basic wall.
**Actual:** the wall matches the tool default — in our case 100 mm / 2.45 m, `structureType: "Profile"` with a **null** profile guid (`00000000-…`), `profileType: "Poly"`, `flipped: true`. No error anywhere.

4. Set the Wall tool default to any **Basic** wall, repeat the call: the wall measures 333 mm / 1.111 m exactly.

## Analysis

`CreateElementsCommandBase::Execute` fetches `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults (&element, &memo)` once, then `CreateWallsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` writes the `element.wall` fields (`type = APIWtyp_Normal`, `modelElemStructureType = API_BasicStructure`, `height`, `thickness`, …) — but nothing clears the **memo**, which for a profile-wall default still carries the profile/poly data. `ACAPI_Element_Create (&element, &memo)` appears to resolve in the memo's favour, so the element-field writes are lost.

Suggested fix: clear/dispose the profile-related memo handles (or re-fetch defaults appropriate to the requested structure) before `ACAPI_Element_Create`, so explicit parameters always beat whatever the seat's tool palette happens to hold. The same pattern presumably applies to the other element creates that start from `GetDefaults`.

## Workaround

Set the Wall tool default to a Basic wall before any scripted create. We now also create-measure-delete a "fingerprint" wall with deliberately odd dimensions before every batch, and stop if the measured size differs from the requested one — happy to share that guard if useful.

Separately (can file as its own issue if wanted): on the `ef7f5226` build, a schema-correct `GetFavoritesByType {"elementType": "Wall"}` hard-crashed Archicad (connection reset, process gone) while we were diagnosing this.

Thanks for Tapir — the JSON surface is carrying a lot of real production work for us.
