title: CreateOpenings: basePoint.z is ignored — openings land at the default anchor altitude (AC28, 1.5.3)
body:
### Summary

`CreateOpenings` accepts a world-space `basePoint`, but its **Z component has no effect**. Every created opening ends up with its middle at the opening default's anchor altitude above its home storey (1.0 m in our template), regardless of the Z we send.

X and Y are honoured; only Z is lost. `width`/`height` are honoured too.

### Environment

- Archicad **28** (INT, German UI), Tapir add-on **1.5.3**, python `archicad` package, Windows 10.

### Reproduction

Create an opening in a wall with a sill clearly away from storey level:

```python
_tapir(conn, "CreateOpenings", {"openingsData": [{
    "ownerElementId": wall_id,
    "basePoint": {"x": 7.63, "y": -4.20, "z": 2.348},   # <- Z ignored
    "width": 0.82,
    "height": 1.657,
}]})
```

Then read the created opening's sill back — built-in property "opening sill height to project zero" (`Öffnung/Brüstungshöhe zu Projektursprung`, GUID `6a3caf9c-f738-4b76-8e02-8be257eef324`):

- **expected** sill: `2.348`
- **actual** sill: `0.233`

The actual value is exactly `storey_level + 1.0 − height/2`, i.e. the opening's **middle** sits at the default anchor altitude (1.0 m) above the home storey. Verified across **52 openings** in one project: `sill == storey + 1.0 − height/2` held for every one to within **1 µm**, with sent Z values spanning −3.5 … +5.6 m. 19 of the 52 were off by more than 5 cm, worst case **2.11 m**.

This is easy to miss: a typical floor-level opening ~2.1 m tall accidentally lands within a few cm of correct, so only tall or high-up openings show the bug clearly.

### Cause (as far as we can tell from the sources)

In `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, `CreateOpeningsCommand::Execute`, the pre-AC29 branch sets

```cpp
element.opening.extrusionGeometryData.frame.basePoint = basePoint;
```

after `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults`, but nothing touches the opening's vertical **anchor** (`anchorIndex` / `anchorAltitude` / linked storey) that the defaults bring in. The anchor then determines the vertical position and the frame base point's Z is effectively overridden.

We haven't tested the `ServerMainVers_2900` branch (`PlacePolygonal`) on AC 29 — it may well behave differently.

### Suggested fix

Either derive the anchor from the supplied `basePoint.z` (so the documented `basePoint` fully positions the opening), or expose the anchor explicitly in the schema (e.g. `anchorAltitude` + `anchorIndex`, like the sill/head parameters on `CreateWindows`). Honouring `basePoint.z` would match the schema's `Coordinate3D` and the behaviour of the other creation commands.

### Workaround

For anyone hitting this: create the opening, read its actual sill from the property above, then shift it with `MoveElements` by the difference. `MoveElements` moves openings reliably. Note that `GetDetailsOfElements` answers `"Not yet supported element type"` for openings and `Get3DBoundingBoxes` returns a degenerate box (a void has no body), so that property is the only usable read-back we found.
author: Liquidmasl

title: Accept floating point index values in SetDetailsOfElements
body:
## Summary

Fixes #530. `SetDetailsOfElements` silently ignored `floorIndex`, `layerIndex` and `drawIndex` when they arrived as JSON floats (`2.0` instead of `2`), while still reporting success.

## Root cause

JSON has no separate integer type, so many clients send whole numbers as floats. The three fields were read straight into integer targets:

```cpp
if (details->Get ("floorIndex", elem.header.floorInd)) {   // short&  -> false for 2.0
Int32 layerIndex;
if (details->Get ("layerIndex", layerIndex)) {             // Int32&  -> false for 2.0
details->Get ("drawIndex", drwIndexTarget);                // short&  -> false for 2.0
```

`GS::ObjectState::Get` returns `false` when the stored value is a double, so the field was skipped and no mask bit was set — no error, no change. As the reporter noted, the published schema calls these `"type": "integer"`, but the documentation renders them as numbers, which makes the trap easy to walk into.

## Fix

A small `GetIndexValue` helper reads the integer target first and falls back to reading a double and **flooring** it. Used for all four index reads in the file (the three above plus the draw-order pass). Integers keep working exactly as before.

`std::floor` rather than a cast: truncation rounds toward zero, so a negative index — stories below 0 are ordinary — would go the other way from a positive one (`-1.4` → `-1` instead of `-2`).

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build succeeds
- [ ] Live: `SetDetailsOfElements` with `{"floorIndex": 1.0, "layerIndex": 3.0, "drawIndex": 2.0}` on an Object moves it to that story/layer/draw order, matching the integer form
- [ ] Live: a fractional value floors consistently in both directions (`1.4` → `1`, `-1.4` → `-2`)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `8554be4`, untitled project from the default template. `SetDetailsOfElements` with `drawIndex: 2.7` → `2`.
author: tlorantfy

title: Add the GetSectionElements command
body:
## Summary

Fixes #509, implementing the option chosen in the issue thread (a dedicated command, with the owner mapping in the same response, leaving the listing commands' owner conversion untouched).

`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` requires a `sectionElementId` of type `API_SectElemID`, but no command could produce one — `GetElementsByType`, `GetAllElements` and `GetSelectedElements` all run every guid through `GetParentElemOfSectElem`, so callers only ever saw the owner element and the command rejected it. The only leak was reading back an already existing dimension.

## The command

**`GetSectionElements`** (Element Commands, 1.5.7)

- Input: `databases` — the section / elevation / interior elevation databases to list. Optional; the current database is used when omitted.
- Response: `sectionElements` — one item per element drawn in those databases:
  - `sectionElementId` — the raw section element guid, which is exactly what `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` wants;
  - `ownerElementId` — the owner element it was generated from (what every other listing command returns), so layer, type and bounding box remain resolvable without a second round-trip;
  - `ownerElementType` — the owner's type, included only when its header is readable from the section database (the owner lives in the model, so this is not guaranteed; it is therefore not a required property).
- `executionResultForDatabases` reports per-database success exactly like `GetElementsByType`, and the same `ExecuteActionForEachDatabase` helper takes care of switching databases and restoring the original one.

No existing behavior changes: the owner conversion in the listing commands is deliberately left as it is.

`Examples/get_section_elements.py` closes the loop from the issue's reproduction — find a section in the Project Map, resolve its database, list the section elements, then dimension a wall on it.

## Test plan

- [x] AC29 add-on build succeeds
- [x] Live: run `Examples/get_section_elements.py` on a project with a section containing walls — `sectionElements` is non-empty and the `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` call at the end succeeds instead of returning "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element."
- [x] Live: calling it without `databases` while a section window is active returns that window's elements
- [x] Live: `ownerElementId` values match what `GetElementsByType` returns for the same section

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `8554be4`, untitled project from the default template. Two walls, a section across them, `GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId` → `GetSectionElements`: 2 section elements with `ownerElementType=Wall` and section guids distinct from the owners. The never-opened-database caveat reproduces exactly and clears once the section is opened.
author: tlorantfy

title: Hand out the command responses the Grasshopper components were dropping
body:
Follow-up of the command ↔ component synchronization check. The inputs turned
out to be in sync everywhere and no command is missing its component, but a
large group of components threw the response away.

## What was lost

| Components | Lost from the response |
| --- | --- |
| the 11 `Modify*` element components | `executionResults` — a failed element looked exactly like a successful one |
| the 9 attribute creators, `SetLayers`, `SetLayerCombinations` | `attributeIds` — the ids the element components need for `buildingMaterialId` / `compositeId` / `profileId` / `fillId`, so the created attributes were unusable |
| `CreateGroups`, `CreatePropertyGroups`, `CreateDesignOptions`, `CreateDesignOptionCombinations`, `CreateKeynoteFolders`, `CreateKeynoteItems`, `CreateKeynoteLabels`, `CreateSections`, `CreateDetails`, `CreateLayout`, `CreateWorksheets`, `CreateDrawings`, `CreateViewsInViewMap`, `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`, `CreateMEPElements`, `CreateMEPRoutingElements`, `CreateProjectInfoFields` | the identifiers of everything they created |
| `ConnectMEPElements` | the deleted / split / created branch element ids |
| `ImportFavorites` | `firstConflictName` |
| `ChangeSelection` | both execution result lists |
| `SetSuspendGroupsMode` | its `executionResult` (now reported as a component error) |
| 31 further components | `executionResults` |
| `GetDetailsOfElements` | `floorPlanPolygons` |

## How

Each of them now has the matching output. The shared bases fix a whole family
at once (`ModifyElementsComponentBase` → 11 components,
`AttributeCreateJsonComponent` → 9), and the repeating mapping lives in
`Component.SetCadValuesWithErrorMessages` / `SetCadValuesWithCreatedIds` and
`ExecutionResultsResponse.ErrorMessages`, so a component that reports per-item
results is a two-line change from here on.

A failed item yields an empty identifier at its own index and the message in
`ErrorMessages` at the same index, so the outputs stay aligned with the inputs.

## Schemas

The audit also caught the response schemas lying about the same thing: the
attribute, element, drawing and database creators report a per-item failure as
an error item, but their schemas declared the strict identifier item only
(`additionalProperties: false`), so a partially failed response did not match
its own schema. They now use the `*OrErrors` unions —
`AttributeIdsOrErrors` and `DatabaseIdsOrErrors` are new in the shared
definitions, `ElementIdsOrErrors` already existed. The generated docs are
regenerated accordingly.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- `dotnet build TapirGrasshopperPlugin.sln` → 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` passes the strict duplicate-key check and every
  `$ref` resolves.
- Not verified live: the new outputs need a running Archicad to confirm the
  values, in particular the `floorPlanPolygons` curves and the MEP connection
  results.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `8554be4`, untitled project from the default template. `floorPlanPolygons` returns the wall footprint; the attribute creators return `attributeIds` and a per-item `"Already exists."` error; `Modify*` returns per-element `executionResults`; and `ConnectMEPElements` reports all three result shapes — `deletedRoutingElementId` on a merge, `splitRoutingElementId` + `createdBranchId` on a branch, and a per-connection error otherwise.

title: GetFavoritesByType crashes Archicad on a schema-correct call (main build ef7f5226, AC28 Win)
body:
Split out of #531 at @tlorantfy's request.

### What happens

A schema-correct `GetFavoritesByType` call takes Archicad down. The connection is forcibly closed and the process is gone. No dialog, no error response, nothing to catch.

### Call

```json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": {
      "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
      "commandName": "GetFavoritesByType"
    },
    "addOnCommandParameters": { "elementType": "Wall" }
  }
}
```

### Environment

- Add-on: main build `ef7f5226`, `TapirAddOn_AC28_Win.apx`, from run 31321602202 (9 Aug 2026). It self-reports as 1.5.7 through `GetAddOnVersion`, so the version string is not a reliable way to identify a CI build.
- Archicad 28, build 6003, NZE localization, Windows 11.
- Project: a test file from the standard NZE template, a handful of walls. The favourites are the template's own, nothing hand-made.

### Expected

A list of favourite names for the type, or an error response. Not a process exit.

### It does not happen on the 3 Aug build

Retested today on `0cc70c97` (3 Aug), same Archicad, same machine, same project. The call returns normally for every type I tried: `Wall`, `Beam`, `Column`, `Slab`, `Object`, `Window`, `Door`. Seventeen wall favourites come back, the process is untouched. So the crash arrived somewhere in `0cc70c97..ef7f5226`.

That range is twenty-five commits. I have not bisected it, and I do not want to guess loudly, but the one that looks nearest to the symptom is #523, "Register all commands before loading the palette singleton" (`78bcb137`), since it moves command registration relative to palette init and the failure is a command call taking the process down at the point of dispatch. Treat that as a starting point rather than a finding.

### Honest limits

The crash is a single observation from 9 Aug. I have not reproduced it since, because my seat is pinned to `0cc70c97` for unrelated reasons and I no longer have the 9 Aug binary locally. The artifact is still up (run 31321602202, expires 7 Nov), so I can reinstall it and confirm the crash properly if that is useful before anyone digs.
author: kozure-dev

title: Expose customUiId / customName / uiId on navigator items in GetNavigatorItemTree
body:
### What's missing

`API_NavigatorItem` carries three fields that no Tapir command exposes:

| Field | SDK description |
|---|---|
| `bool customUiId` | "Custom ID of the item (relevant only in the View Map and Layout Map)." |
| `bool customName` | "Custom name of the item (relevant only in the View Map and Layout Map)." |
| `char uiId[128]` | "The ID of the navigator item." |

Ref: https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/struct_a_p_i___navigator_item.html

`NavigatorItemToObjectState` (NavigatorCommands.cpp:1481) already receives the
populated `API_NavigatorItem`, but serialises only `type`, `name`,
`navigatorItemId`, and a `prefix` that is set for `API_StoryNavItem` only. The
two booleans and `uiId` are dropped on the floor.

Interestingly Tapir already *writes* `customName` — `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`
(:1151), `CreateViewMapFolder` (:1224) and `RenameNavigatorItem` (:1349) all set
it — so it's currently write-only. `customUiId` and `uiId` aren't referenced
anywhere in Sources/.

### Why it's useful

These two booleans are the answer to "is this View's ID/Name set to Custom, or
inherited from the Project Map?" — the View Settings radio buttons. That matters
for any drawing-register or naming-standard QA: on a large project you want to
find the views someone has hand-overridden, because those silently stop tracking
their source.

Right now that question can only be answered by a heuristic — read the view's
ID/Name, read its Project Map source's ID/Name, and compare. It works, but it
cannot distinguish "By Project Map" from "Custom, but typed identical to the
source", so it systematically under-reports. The flags would make it exact.

This is the direct analogue of what `GetDetailsOfElements` already does so well
for Drawings, where `numberingType` / `nameType` are returned verbatim. I've been
using that to audit Drawing ID/Name overrides and it's been excellent — it's
precisely the same question one level up the chain, and navigator items are the
one place it can't be answered.

### Suggested change

Three lines in `NavigatorItemToObjectState`:

    itemOS.Add ("customUiId", item.customUiId);
    itemOS.Add ("customName", item.customName);

and widening the existing `prefix` (or adding `uiId`) to carry `item.uiId` for
non-story items, rather than only `floorNum` for stories.

`isIndependent` would be a welcome bonus in the same object, since it's right
there and answers a related question.

Happy to test a build against a real project — I have a ~290-view Archicad 27
project with a mix of inherited and custom view IDs that exercises this well.

### Environment

- Tapir 1.5.7
- Archicad 27 build 6080 (AUS), macOS
author: pgalliford

title: Report the navigator item's ID and its custom ID/name flags
body:
Fixes #538.

`NavigatorItemToObjectState` received the populated `API_NavigatorItem` but
serialised only `type`, `name`, `navigatorItemId` and a `prefix` that is filled
for stories only. `uiId`, `customUiId`, `customName` and `isIndependent` never
left the add-on — `customName` was even write-only, since
`CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`, `CreateViewMapFolder` and `RenameNavigatorItem`
all set it and nothing read it back.

All four are now in every navigator item of the response:

```json
{
  "type": "ViewItem",
  "name": "Ground Floor Plan",
  "navigatorItemId": { "guid": "..." },
  "prefix": "",
  "uiId": "A-101",
  "customUiId": true,
  "customName": false,
  "isIndependent": false
}
```

As the issue explains, the two flags are the only exact answer to "is this
view's ID/name Custom or By Project Map?" — the View Settings radio buttons.
Comparing the view's strings to its Project Map source cannot distinguish
them, because a custom value typed identical to the source's reads as
inherited, so a naming-standard audit systematically under-reports the
overrides.

## Version gating

None needed: `uiId[128]`, `customUiId`, `customName` and `isIndependent` are
present with the same names and types in the AC25, AC26, AC27, AC28 and AC29
DevKit headers (checked in `APIdefs_Navigator.h` of each).

## Drive-by fix

`get_section_elements.py` (added in #535) called Tapir's `GetNavigatorItemTree`
through `aclib.RunTapirCommand` but passed the *official* command's parameters
(`navigatorTreeId`) and read the official command's response shape
(`navigatorTree.rootItem`). Tapir's command takes `navigatorMapId` and answers
with `navigatorItemTree`, so that example could never have run — the call would
have been rejected on the input schema. It now uses
`aclib.RunCommand('API.GetNavigatorItemTree', …)` like every other example that
walks a navigator tree. My mistake in #535.

## Not included

The Tapir `GetNavigatorItemTree` still has no response schema (it never
overrode `GetRawResponseSchema`), so the new fields are undocumented in the
command reference. Writing one means a self-referential `$ref` for the
`children` recursion; that is a separate change I would rather not fold into a
field addition, especially with #537 open.

The Grasshopper `NavigatorTree` component is unaffected: it calls the
*official* `API.GetNavigatorItemTree`, not Tapir's, so exposing these fields
there would mean switching it to the Tapir command and changing its inputs.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- Not verified live: the field values need a running Archicad with a View Map
  that has hand-overridden IDs. @pgalliford offered to test a build — the
  new `Examples/get_navigator_item_tree.py` prints exactly that audit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `8554be4`, untitled project from the default template. All 30 View Map items carry `uiId`, `customUiId`, `customName` and `isIndependent`, and the values vary — "Site" reads custom/custom while the plain stories read inherited with `uiId` "1.", "2.".
author: tlorantfy

title: Revert the anyOf response schema wrapper
body:
Reverts #499. Reopens #483.

#499 made `CommandBase::GetResponseSchema` `final` and had it wrap every
command's declared schema in `{"anyOf": [<schema>, <error object>]}`, so a
failing command's `{"error": {code, message}}` response would survive
Archicad's schema validation.

@tlorantfy built this revert and tested it against a live Archicad: **the
regressions disappear**. A top-level `anyOf` is not something the response
schemas may use.

## What this restores

- `GetResponseSchema` is the plain, non-`final` virtual the commands override
  again — `GetRawResponseSchema` is gone.
- The schema a command declares reaches Archicad verbatim, with no wrapper.
- `RegisterCommand` reads it back through `GetResponseSchema ()`.

The rename is undone by hand rather than with `git revert -m 1 2d5acab`,
because roughly forty commands added since #499 override
`GetRawResponseSchema` and would not compile once the base declaration is
removed. The rename is 1:1 mechanical in both directions, so the result is
the same source state #499 changed, applied to today's tree. Zero occurrences
of `GetRawResponseSchema` remain.

No schema content changes: the generated docs already used the raw schema, so
`docs/archicad-addon/command_definitions.js` is unaffected.

## What comes back

#483: a failing command returns `{"error": {...}}` as the whole response,
which its own schema forbids (`additionalProperties: false`), so Archicad
discards it with schema validation error 4009 and the caller sees a generic
failure instead of the actual message.

That needs a different fix, and the codebase already contains the shape of
one. About fifteen commands never had this problem, because their response
schema is a `#/<Name>OrError` definition in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` —
`FavoritesOrError`, `AttributeHeadersOrError`, `ZoneBoundariesOrError` and so
on — each a `oneOf` of the success shape and `#/ErrorItem`. Those have always
worked in production, which suggests the problem is specifically a union
written at the root of the response schema string, not unions as such. I will
work that up separately against #483 rather than fold it into a revert that
fixes live breakage.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- Live: regressions gone, per @tlorantfy's test of this exact build.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: tlorantfy

title: Stop declaring a response schema to Archicad
body:
Fixes #483. Stacked on #540 — **base branch is `revert/response-schema-anyof`**, so review #540 first.

The `anyOf` wrapper is gone for good. This is the alternative: nothing new is
handed to Archicad's schema machinery at all.

## The reasoning

Archicad uses the response schema for exactly one thing — validating what the
command returns. The DevKit is explicit about it:

> `GetResponseSchema` — "This schema will be used to validate the incoming
> request response."

Nothing publishes it to callers. The command reference on the docs site is
generated from the add-on's own `CommandInfo` registry, not from anything
Archicad holds.

Now look at what that validation actually does. A failing command answers
`{"error": {code, message}}` as the whole response, which the command's own
schema forbids (`additionalProperties: false`, plus `required` fields the
error does not have). Archicad discards the response and reports schema
validation error 4009 — the caller gets a generic failure and never sees the
message. That is #483.

I measured it across the current command set:

| | commands |
|---|---|
| reject their own error response | **225** |
| accept it (`#/<Name>OrError` unions in the shared definitions) | 6 |
| declare no response schema at all | 3 |

The 6 that work — `FavoritesOrError`, `AttributeHeadersOrError`,
`ZoneBoundariesOrError`, `ConnectedElementsOrError`,
`ElementsWithExecutionResultsOrError` — are the reason those commands have
always reported errors properly.

So response validation cannot pass on the error path unless all 225 commands
get their own union definition, and when it does pass it buys nothing: it is a
check on the add-on's own output whose only effect on failure is to destroy
the response before it reaches the caller. Dropping it costs no one anything.

## The change

`CommandBase::GetResponseSchema` is `final` and returns nothing. Commands
declare their schema through `GetRawResponseSchema`, which `RegisterCommand`
records for the documentation.

Net effect over the two PRs together — **two files**:

```
archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.cpp | 32 +++-----------------------------
archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.hpp | 11 +++++++----
```

The 53-file rename in this PR exactly undoes the rename in #540, so if you
would rather not have the churn twice in history, squash-merging #540 and then
this one leaves the same result. I kept them apart so the revert you already
tested stays reviewable on its own.

## Why not the alternatives

- **A union per command in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`** (the `*OrError`
  idiom): 225 new definitions, each duplicating a response shape, for a check
  that only ever rejects our own output. Not worth the surface.
- **Relaxing `required` and adding an optional `error` to every schema**: same
  225-command reach, and impossible for the 38 commands whose schema is a bare
  `$ref`.
- **Keeping a top-level union**: what just broke.

## What is lost

Archicad no longer catches a malformed add-on response. In exchange, a command
that fails now delivers its error message. Given the failure mode of the check
was to silently swallow that message, I think this is the right trade — but
it is a real change in behaviour and worth a second opinion.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- Command reference unchanged: `RegisterCommand` already recorded the raw
  schema, so `docs/archicad-addon/command_definitions.js` needs no
  regeneration.
- Not verified live: that a failing command's message now reaches the caller
  needs a running Archicad — e.g. `GetSpecialFolders` with an invalid folder
  type, which should return its own error text instead of 4009.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `31c296e`, untitled project from the default template. Verified through #544, which landed this change on `main`: a bare `{error}` response is delivered intact instead of being discarded with `4009`.
author: tlorantfy

title: Start every batch item from the tool defaults
body:
Found while running the live verification that the recently merged PRs still owed.

## The bug

`CreateElementsCommandBase::Execute` read `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` **once**
before the item loop and then reused the same `API_Element` for every item,
while `SetTypeSpecificParameters` only writes the fields an item actually
names. So whatever one item set survived into the next item that stayed silent
about it.

Confirmed live on Archicad 29:

```
CreateBeams [{slantAngle: 0.3}, {}]   -> slant=0.3 isSlanted=True | slant=0.3 isSlanted=True
CreateWalls [{arcAngle: 0.5},   {}]   -> arcAngle=0.5             | arcAngle=0.5
```

A single item is clean both before and after those calls, so the tool defaults
themselves are not polluted — the leak lives entirely inside one command. It
reaches **every optional field of every batch creation command**: walls, slabs,
beams, columns, objects, lamps, roofs, meshes, morphs and the rest.

Passing the field explicitly still wins (`[{slantAngle: 0.3}, {slantAngle: 0}]`
behaves), so the symptom only shows when a caller relies on an omitted field
meaning "leave it at the default" — which is exactly what the schemas promise,
since every one of these fields is optional.

## The fix

Re-read the defaults for each item, so each starts from the tool defaults
rather than from its predecessor's leftovers.

The per-item `favoriteName` path added in #519 already did this re-read, which
is why the leak never showed there — the re-read is now unconditional, and its
error is reported per item instead of being dropped.

## Cost

One extra `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` per item. That is what the favourite path
has been doing per item since #519, so the shape is proven; the comment claiming
the common path was left "exactly as it was" was accurate, and that turned out
to be the problem.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- ~~- **Not verified live yet**: the running Archicad has an older `.apx` loaded, so~~
  confirming the fix needs the new build loaded (which means restarting
  Archicad). The two commands above are the check — both should come back with
  the second element unslanted / unbent.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

### ✅ Live verification — passed

Archicad 29, add-on built from `d00a2a1`, untitled project from the default template. `CreateBeams [{slantAngle: 0.3}, {}]` → `slant=0.3 | slant=0`, `CreateWalls [{arcAngle: 0.5}, {}]` → `arc=0.5 | arc=0`, and four beams `[0.3, -, 0.15, -]` → `0.3 | 0 | 0.15 | 0`. The leak is gone and an explicitly named field still wins.
author: tlorantfy

title: Put the IFC logo on the IFC components
body:
The five IFC components carried unrelated line art — a box, a document, an
arrow — so nothing on the canvas said IFC. They now carry the buildingSMART IFC
logo.

All five would be indistinguishable with the bare logo, so each keeps a small
badge in the bottom right corner:

| Component | Badge |
|---|---|
| `GetIFCIdsOfElements` | arrow out — elements → IFC ids |
| `GetElementsByIFCIds` | arrow in — IFC ids → elements |
| `GetIFCPropertiesOfElements` | list lines |
| `GetIFCTypeOfElements` | T |
| `IFCFileOperation` | up/down arrows — import/export |

## Vector, not the bitmap

The logo is drawn as vectors instead of embedding the artwork. At the 24 px the
canvas actually uses, a downscaled bitmap turns to mush — the four interlocking
rings collapse into each other well before that size, and by 11 px it is an
unreadable blob. The vector version stays crisp at every size.

Its proportions are measured off the official artwork rather than eyeballed: I
took the colour bounding boxes of the four rings (294 px each, centres 161.5 px
apart, stroke ≈ 57 px on a 461 px canvas) and scaled them into the icon space —
ring 15.2, centre spacing 8.4, stroke 2.9. The four brand colours are unchanged:

title: Land the #483 fix on main
body:
Re-targets #541 at `main`. Same commit, nothing new to review.

## What went wrong

I opened #541 as a stacked PR with `revert/response-schema-anyof` as its base,
so that #540 — the revert you had tested — stayed reviewable on its own. When
both were merged, #540 went into `main` as intended, but #541 went into

$ git show origin/main:archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.hpp | grep ResponseSchema
    virtual GS::Optional<GS::UniString> GetResponseSchema () const override;

So `main` still declares the response schemas, and #483 is still live there —
which matches what I measured on the running Archicad while verifying, where
`GetElementPreviewImage` with a bad guid answers `4009` instead of its own error

author: tlorantfy

title: Let basePoint place an opening vertically
body:
Fixes #533.

`CreateOpenings` documents `basePoint` as a `Coordinate3D`, but the Z never
positioned the opening. Both branches were wrong — in different ways, and the
AC29 one was not previously known.

## Up to AC28 — Z is discarded

The vertical position of an opening comes from `anchorAltitude`, measured from
the home story up to the anchor point. The DevKit is explicit that it governs:

> `anchorAltitude` — *"Altitude of opening anchor. Valid only if constraint is forced horizontal or aligned."*

The command set `extrusionGeometryData.frame.basePoint` and never touched the
anchor, so with the stock centre anchor every opening's **middle** landed at the
default altitude. @Liquidmasl measured `sill == storyLevel + 1.0 − height/2`
across **all 52 openings** of a project, for Z spanning −3.5 … +5.6 m, worst case
**2.11 m** out.

The requested Z is now converted into the altitude the configured anchor
expects, so the bottom edge lands on it:

```cpp
const double bottomAboveStory = basePoint.z - GetZPos (element.header.floorInd, 0.0, stories);
extrusionParameters.anchorAltitude =
    bottomAboveStory + GetAnchorHeightOffset (extrusionParameters.anchor, extrusionParameters.height);
```

`GetAnchorHeightOffset` returns `height` for the `?T` anchors, `height/2` for
`?M`, `0` for `?B`. The anchor's horizontal half is deliberately untouched, so
horizontal placement is unchanged.

## On AC29 — Z is honoured, but the opening hangs a full height too low

This is new — the issue says the `PlacePolygonal` branch was untested, so I
tested it. **Measured live on AC29 before the fix:**

| sent z | height | sill | z − sill |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.5 | 1.5 | 0.5 |
| 2.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| 2.0 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 2.0 |
| 2.0 | 2.5 | −0.5 | 2.5 |
| 1.0 | 1.5 | −0.5 | 1.5 |
| 3.5 | 0.8 | 2.7 | 0.8 |

`sill == basePoint.z − height`, exactly, every time: the base polygon spans
`0..height` along a local +Y that runs **down** the host's plane, so the
rectangle hangs below the base point, i.e. `basePoint` was effectively the
opening's top edge.

The polygon now spans `-height..0`. Spanning the polygon rather than shifting
the point matters: on a host plane that is not vertical, a world-Z correction
would be wrong by `cos(slant)` while the local-space fix stays correct.

## Result

Both branches now agree with each other, and with what `basePoint` means in
every other creation command — the point the element is placed at.

## Verification

- `cmake --build Build/AC29 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean.
- `cmake --build Build/AC28 --config RelWithDebInfo` → clean. AC28 matters here
  because the anchor code only compiles on the pre-2900 branch, so an AC29 build
  alone would not have covered it.
- The AC29 misplacement above is measured on the **pre-fix** build; the
  post-fix numbers still need a run, which takes an add-on reload.
- The AC25–AC28 branch cannot be verified from my seat at all. @Liquidmasl —
  you have AC28 and the 52-opening project; if you can run this branch, the
  check is that the sill now equals the Z you send.

title: Add the CreateInteriorElevations command
body:
Fixes #471 (the primitive half — see below).

Tapir could already list interior elevations, switch to one with `ChangeWindow`,
and read what one draws through `GetSectionElements`. Only creating them was
missing.

## The command

Every consecutive pair of `nodeCoordinates` becomes one segment with its own
viewpoint, so the corner points of a room produce an interior elevation of that
room. Repeating the first point closes the chain and adds the fourth wall.

```json
{
  "interiorElevationsData": [
    {
      "nodeCoordinates": [
        {"x": 0, "y": 0}, {"x": 5, "y": 0}, {"x": 5, "y": 4}, {"x": 0, "y": 4}, {"x": 0, "y": 0}
      ],
      "depth": 4.5,
      "name": "Living Room"
    }
  ]
}
```

`depth`, `name`, `id` and `floorIndex` are optional. Segments look to the left
of their direction, so a chain running clockwise faces into the room.

## The headers describe a different element than the one Archicad accepts

My first implementation followed `API_InteriorElevationType` as documented —
two main coordinates per segment, `nSegments` / `nLineCoords` / `poly` filled
in, a computed `sectionSegmentDepthCoords` array, each segment seeded from the
defaults. Built and run: **`APIERR_BADPARS`, every time.**

The DevKit ships a working reference (`AC25/Examples/Element_Test/Src/Element_Basics.cpp`,
`Do_CreateInteriorElevation`) and it differs in essentially every structural
detail:

| | headers suggest | what actually works |
|---|---|---|
| main coordinates | 2 per segment | **one shared polyline**, `segment.nMainCoord` = node count |
| `intElevSegments` | seeded from the defaults segment | **zeroed**, one per gap between nodes |
| `nSegments`, `nLineCoords`, `poly` | set them | **leave them alone**, Archicad derives them |
| depth | `sectionSegmentDepthCoords` | `segment.ieCreationSegmentDepth` |

The implementation now follows the reference. Worth knowing for anyone touching
section-like elements later: the field docs are not a reliable guide here.

## Corroboration for #413

The reference also reads the marker's parameters from **the marker's own
library part** (`marker.subElem.object.libInd`), not from a separately resolved
marker parent. That is exactly the fix I proposed on #413 for the
`APIERR_REFUSEDPAR` failures in `CreateWindows`/`CreateDoors`, where the current
code takes params from `GetMarkerParent` while leaving `libInd` untouched. This
command does it the DevKit's way from the start.

## Verification

**Live on AC29**, with the branch built and loaded:

- five-point chain around a 5 × 4 room → one interior elevation, and the Project
  Map shows **four `InteriorElevationItem` viewpoints** under it, one per segment
- two-point chain → a single segment, created
- one point → refused by the input schema (`minItems`)
- two identical consecutive points → refused with a clear message

`GetDetailsOfElements` answers `"Not yet supported element type"` for the
created element — pre-existing, and the same gap the #533 reporter hit for
openings. Not addressed here.

## What this deliberately does not do

The issue asks for the zone-driven half — *"based on Zones shape"*. That needs
the questions I raised on the issue answered (short edges, curved edges, depth,
one-per-zone, naming). This PR is the primitive underneath it, and
`Examples/create_interior_elevations.py` shows the zone workflow already works
on top of it: read the zones, feed each outline in. The convenience layer can
follow once @grzegorzwilk replies.

author: tlorantfy

title: Refuse polygonal walls and name the missing opening size
body:
Addresses issues 2 and 3 of #453.

## Issue 2 — polygonal walls

**Archicad cannot place an opening in a polygonal wall.** The DevKit's own
`Do_CreateWindow` refuses the case outright before it ever reaches
`ACAPI_Element_CreateExt`:

```cpp
if (element.wall.type == APIWtyp_Poly) {
    WriteReport_Alert ("No way to put openings into polygonal walls");
    return;
}
```

Going ahead anyway does not fail — the window or door is placed at a fixed spot
inside the wall and every `centerOffset` lands in the same place, which is
exactly what @mozzi86 measured with three doors at 0.6 / 1.7 / 2.8. That is the
worst kind of failure: a success response and silently wrong geometry.

`CreateWindows` and `CreateDoors` now check the owner wall's type and answer

> The owner wall is polygonal, and Archicad cannot place a window in one.

## Issue 3 — the missing size

`CreateOpenings` builds its base polygon from `width` and `height`, so omitting
one reached Archicad as an empty polygon and came back as *"Can't use empty
polygon!"*, which names nothing. It now says:

> Both 'width' and 'height' are required to create an opening.

**Windows and doors are deliberately not size-checked.** There the size is
optional — the tool defaults or the named favourite supply it — and adding the
same check would have broken working callers. Verified live that both still
create with no `width` or `height` at all.

## Issues 1 and 4

Not addressed here.

- **Issue 1** (some door favourites fail with `-2130313110`) is the same family
  as #413, #532, #399 and #481. It needs a seat where it reproduces; mine does
  not. Notably it fits the pattern: the reporter's failing favourites are all
  based on one library part (`Tür 29`) while a favourite on another
  (`Eingang 01 1-Fl 27`) works with identical parameters.
- **Issue 4** is a version-drift note against 1.5.3 — `thickness` and
  `compositeId` are already returned by current `main`.

## Verification

Live on AC29:

```
  window, no width/height     : OK          <- unchanged
  door, no width/height       : OK          <- unchanged
  window, sized               : OK
  opening, no height          : ERR: Both 'width' and 'height' are required to create an opening.
  opening, no width           : ERR: Both 'width' and 'height' are required to create an opening.
  opening, neither            : ERR: Both 'width' and 'height' are required to create an opening.
  opening, both               : OK
```

The polygonal-wall guard is **not** exercised live: Tapir's `CreateWalls`
cannot make an `APIWtyp_Poly` wall (the schema has no polygon input), so I
could not build one to test against. The check is a direct read of
`wall.type`, and the DevKit statement above is the authority for the rule
itself. @mozzi86 — you have such walls; the expected result is now a clear
error instead of three doors landing on top of each other.

title: Bump the version to 1.5.8
body:
1.5.7 is released, so the version has to move on before anything else is added
under it.

Bumped with `tools/update_version.py`, which carries `package_info.json` into
the four other places the version lives:

| file | |
|---|---|
| `tools/package_info.json` | 1.5.7 → 1.5.8 |
| `archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnVersion.hpp` | `ADDON_VERSION` |
| `grasshopper-plugin/…/TapirGrasshopperPlugin.csproj` | `<Version>` |
| `grasshopper-plugin/…/TapirGrasshopperPluginInfo.cs` | `AssemblyVersion` |
| `grasshopper-plugin/YakPackage/manifest.yml` | `version:` |

## The command that was mislabelled

`GetSectionElements` (#535) went in **after** the 1.5.7 tag but was registered
as `"1.5.7"`, so the command reference would have told callers it exists in a
release that does not contain it.

I checked the whole set rather than assuming, by diffing the registrations at
the tag against `main`:

```
$ git show 1.5.7:archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnMain.cpp | grep -B1 '"1.5.7"'
$ git show origin/main:archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnMain.cpp | grep -B1 '"1.5.7"'
```

Sixteen commands carry `"1.5.7"` at the tag and seventeen on `main` — the one
difference is `GetSectionElements`, now `"1.5.8"`.

`CreateInteriorElevations` is registered as `"1.5.7"` on the #546 branch and has
the same problem; I have fixed it there rather than here, so each PR carries its
own correction.

author: tlorantfy

title: Let an empty value clear a project info field
body:
Answers the question directly: **no, it was not intentional — empty is a perfectly valid state for a project info field in Archicad, and the restriction was ours.**

The DevKit says so outright, on `ACAPI_AutoText_SetAnAutoText`:

> *"You can set the autotext value empty by passing **nullptr** in the autotextValue parameter."*

What blocked it was Tapir's own input schema:

```json
"projectInfoValue": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
```

That `minLength: 1` arrived with the commit that first added the command, with no
rationale recorded — it reads as a copy of the constraint on `projectInfoId`,
where requiring a non-empty key is genuinely right. No code stood behind it:
`Execute` passed `&projectInfoValue` unconditionally, so the documented nullptr
case was never reachable.

## The change

- `minLength: 1` dropped from `projectInfoValue` (kept on `projectInfoId`)
- an empty string is passed to Archicad as `nullptr`, i.e. the documented clear
- the failure message distinguishes clearing from setting

No new command: `SetProjectInfoField` with `""` now means "clear", which matches
the API's own model. `DeleteProjectInfoFields` is not the answer to this — it
removes a *custom* field entirely and will not touch the built-in ones.

## Verification

Live on AC29:

```
field   : PROJECTNAME
set to 'Tapir test value'   -> now: 'Tapir test value'
clear with ""               -> now: ''            PASS
set again to 'Back again'   -> now: 'Back again'
```

The third step matters: clearing does not leave the field in a state that
refuses later writes. The original value is restored afterwards.

author: tlorantfy

title: Feature request: read classification of Building Material / attribute-level classification commands
body:
Currently there's no way to read the classification assigned to a Building Material (or other attributes) via the Tapir/Archicad JSON API. dev_get_classifications_of_elements only works for elements, not attributes, and attributes_get_building_materials / attributes_get_attributes_by_type don't expose classification data either.

Use case: in composite walls/complex profiles measured via "measição por componentes", each skin's Building Material is classified into a BOQ chapter (e.g. via the "Mapa de Quantidades" classification system), so quantities can be automatically routed to the correct chapter per material layer. Right now the only workaround is duplicating the classification into a custom property on the material, which is fragile (easy to get out of sync with the real classification).

Would it be possible to add something like GetClassificationsOfAttributes / SetClassificationsOfAttributes, analogous to the existing element-level commands?
author: dmacielarq-creator

title: CreateWindows/CreateDoors: marker (window stamp) settings are silently replaced with library part defaults
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3100 (Norwegian), Tapir 1.5.7 and 1.5.8, Windows 11.

**Summary:** Windows and doors created through `CreateWindows`/`CreateDoors` always get the library part's factory marker (window stamp) instead of the tool default's marker. This makes it impossible to produce localized permit drawings via the API when the template's stamp settings differ from the library defaults (in our case: frame outer dimensions `BxH: 12x12` vs the factory `WHD 1 230…` wall hole dimensions, and pen 241 vs 166).

**Root cause (read from source):** In `archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults`:

1. The tool default marker is fetched correctly via `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt` with `APISubElement_MainMarker`.
2. Its parameters are then **overwritten** with `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams` (library factory values): `marker.memo.params = markAddPars;` — currently line 322 on `main`.
3. The marker pen is additionally hardcoded: `marker.subElem.object.pen = 166;` — line 323.

The same `marker.memo.params = markAddPars;` assignment also appears at line 6601, so a fix probably needs to cover both call sites.

**What we tried from the client side** (all verified live on a clean model):

| Approach | Response | Effect on stamp |
|---|---|---|
| `favoriteName` in `CreateWindows` | accepted | none |
| `ApplyFavoritesToElements` on a window | "type mismatch" error | – |
| `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` | `success` | none |
| `SetGDLParametersOfElements` on the window | `success` | none |
| `SetGDLParametersOfElements` on the stamp object itself (found via `GetElementsByType` + `IncludeSubElemObjects`) | `success` | none — every value unchanged when read back |

Setting the tool default by hand in the template does not help either, since the overwrite happens after the default is read.

**Suggested fix:** keep the tool default's marker parameters (skip the overwrite) unless the caller explicitly asks for factory defaults, and drop the hardcoded pen.

**Side finding:** `GetElementsByType` supports an undocumented `IncludeSubElemObjects` filter that exposes stamps as readable objects (227–232 parameters). Reading works; writing silently no-ops. If writing marker parameters is not supported, returning an error would be far more debuggable than `success: true`.

Thanks for Tapir — it is doing the heavy lifting in a Norwegian building-permit drawing pipeline, and this is the only stamp-related blocker we have left.
author: tomerikjansen-crypto

title: CreateSolidElementLinks: roofs are always rejected as operator (roof as target works)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3100 (Norwegian), Tapir 1.5.7/1.5.8, Windows 11.

**Summary:** `CreateSolidElementLinks` works in general (wall/slab verified in both directions), but every attempt with a **roof as operator** fails with `Failed to create solid element link` — regardless of operation type (subtraction with and without upwards extrusion), active window (floor plan or 3D), and story. A roof as **target** works.

**Repro:**
1. Create a wall that crosses a pitched roof plane.
2. Call `CreateSolidElementLinks` with the roof as operator and the wall as target, operation `subtraction`.
3. The call fails. The same operation performed in the GUI succeeds.

**Why it matters:** trimming gable walls to the underside of roof planes is the standard way to close a gable. Without roof-as-operator, API users have to model the gable triangle separately — we build it as a Morph — which duplicates geometry the roof already defines, and the two can drift apart when the roof changes.

Since the operation is routine in the GUI, this looks like a restriction in the command's element-type validation rather than a core API limitation.

Happy to provide a minimal reproduction file if that helps.
author: tomerikjansen-crypto

title: GetNavigatorItemTree: allow selecting a publisher set by name
body:
## The problem

`GetNavigatorItemTreeCommand::Execute` passes a hardcoded index to
`ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet`:

```cpp
API_NavigatorSet navSet = {};
navSet.mapId = mapId;
Int32 idx = 0;
GSErrCode err = ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet (&navSet, &idx);
```

The DevKit documents that parameter as *"Index of the required set. Used only
for Publisher Sets"*. So in a project with more than one publisher set, every
caller gets the **first** set's tree regardless of which set they wanted -
silently, because the response looks perfectly valid.

This also makes `selectedNavigatorItemIds` on `PublishPublisherSet` unusable in
practice. The navigator item ids come from the first set, the publish call
targets the named set, that set does not recognise them, and the **whole set is
published** instead of the selection. From the outside it looks like the
parameter is ignored - it took us a source read to find the real cause.

## The change

Adds an optional `publisherSetName` to `GetNavigatorItemTree`, resolved through
the `GetPublisherSetNameGuidTable ()` helper that `PublishPublisherSet` already
uses a few lines above in the same file. Behaviour without the parameter is
unchanged, so this is backwards compatible.

## Verification

Archicad 29 (build 3100, Norwegian), a project with 8 publisher sets, built
from this branch:

| call | root children |
|---|---|
| no `publisherSetName` | `Skisse/forprosjekt, Byggesøknad, Detaljprosjekt, Illustrasjoner` |
| `"Utskrift"` (first set) | same as above - confirming the old behaviour was always set #1 |
| `"Lagre som PDF"` | `0000-Bygningsnavn ARK Skisse/forprosjekt, ... Byggesøknad, ...` |
| `"Lagre som DWG"` | `0000 ARK DWG-eksport` |

End to end: publishing `"Lagre som PDF"` with `selectedNavigatorItemIds` taken
from that set's own tree produced **7 PDFs** (the selected branch) instead of
all **23** - which is what the same call produced before the fix.

Build is clean with `/W4 /WX` (`Visual Studio 18 2026`, `-T v143`, AC29).

## Note, not part of this PR

The root item of a publisher set tree comes back with `"name": "???"`, which is
why a caller cannot tell which set they received. Happy to look at that
separately if you consider it worth changing.
author: tomerikjansen-crypto

title: Let Claude triage issues and review pull requests
body:
Three workflows that run Claude on GitHub's runners, so none of this needs
anyone's machine to be on. They use `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`.

## What you have to do

Add one repository secret: **`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`**. Run
`claude setup-token` locally (Pro or Max subscription) and paste the result
into Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Runs then draw on the
subscription rather than being billed per token.

It is already set — the review workflow reviewed this pull request twice while
it was open, which is where most of the changes below came from.

## `claude_pr_review.yml`

Reviews every pull request and posts inline comments plus one summary, on Opus
5. Its checklist is ordered by what actually goes wrong here: DevKit
correctness with memo handling called out, version gating across AC25–AC29,
agreement between schema / C++ / description / Python example / Grasshopper
component, the registered version being the unreleased one, and whether the
response schema admits the per-item errors the command can produce.

Runs on `pull_request_target` rather than `pull_request`, because GitHub
withholds secrets from fork-originated `pull_request` runs — on that trigger
the review would only ever have covered branches pushed straight to this
repository, missing exactly the outside contributions worth reading. That is
safe here only because the pull request's code is never checked out or
executed: the checkout pins the base commit and the review reads the change
through `gh pr diff`.

## `claude_issue_triage.yml`

Two jobs, split on trust.

**`triage`** answers every newly opened issue: closes it naming what already
fixed it, asks the one question that would unblock it, or explains the defect.
It holds `contents: read` and `issues: write` and an allowlist of read-only
tools — an issue body is text written by anyone on the internet, and the
action's own security guidance is to restrict tools "to the minimum required".

**`fix`** writes the fix and opens a draft pull request. It runs only when
someone applies the **`claude-fix`** label, and applying a label requires write
access — so its trigger is a human deciding to act, which is the review step
that same guidance asks for, expressed as a permission GitHub already enforces.

Its pull requests are drafts and say so in the body, because GitHub starts no
workflow runs from events a workflow token caused: no AC25–AC29 build check and
no review runs on them until a maintainer pushes a commit or reopens by hand.

## `claude_auto_merge.yml`

Merges pull requests that clear three gates:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Author has write access** | `admin`, `write` or `maintain` |
| **Every check green** | pending, failing or cancelled all stop it |
| **No release critical path** | `.github/`, `archicad-addon/Tools/`, `tools/`, plus `CMakeLists.txt`, `*.cmake` and `*.csproj`, which the release job executes while signing |

Also refused: bots, drafts, anything based on a branch other than `main`,
anything with no checks reported, and anything not cleanly mergeable. The merge
is pinned with `--match-head-commit`, so a push landing between the gates and
the merge fails rather than merging code no gate saw.

Two things worth knowing. **The gates are shell, not a prompt** — reviewing is
a judgement call and Claude does that in the review workflow, but merging is a
rule, and a rule that hands out repository credentials should fail closed
identically every time. And **it never checks out the pull request's branch**;
without that, a pull request could edit a build script and delete its own gate
before it was evaluated.

It triggers on `workflow_run` from the two build checks, not `check_suite` —
GitHub does not fire `check_suite` for suites created by Actions, and every
check here is an Actions job, so that trigger would never have run.

## What this will not do

A runner has no Archicad seat. Triage and review can read code, quote the
DevKit and reason about schemas, but cannot reproduce a crash or confirm a
geometry fix — expect "here is the mechanism, here is the check to run" rather
than "verified". Both prompts are told to say so rather than assert.

title: DeleteElements and MoveElements silently no-op on elements whose layer is hidden (returns success, element remains) — AC28, 1.5.7
body:
`DeleteElements` returns `{"success": true}` for `Object` elements and does not delete them. Slabs,
Roofs, Meshes and Doors delete correctly in the same session, so this appears specific to Objects.

Because the call reports success, any script that verifies by return value believes the delete
happened. Objects placed via the API cannot then be removed except by hand in the UI.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Archicad | 28, build 6003, NZE |
| Tapir add-on | 1.5.7 |
| Project | single-user, not Teamwork, floor plan active |

## Minimal reproduction

```python
before = len(RunTapirCommand('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'])

created = RunTapirCommand('CreateObjects', {'objectsData': [
    {'libraryPartName': 'Chair 01', 'coordinates': {'x': 70.0, 'y': 70.0, 'z': 0.0}}]})
eid = created['elements'][0]['elementId']

RunTapirCommand('DeleteElements', {'elements': [{'elementId': eid}]})
# -> {"success": true}

after = len(RunTapirCommand('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'])
assert after == before          # FAILS: after == before + 1
```

**Expected:** the object is deleted, count returns to `before`.
**Actual:** `{"success": true}` and the count is unchanged. The object is still in the model.

## Control — the same call works for other types

Created and deleted in the same session, minutes apart:

| element type | created | deleted |
|---|---|---|
| Slab | yes | **removed** |
| Roof | yes | removed |
| Mesh | yes | removed |
| Door | yes | removed |
| **Object** | yes | **no-op** |

## Ruled out

- **Not library-part specific** — reproduced with `Chair 01`, `Bed 01`, `Sofa 01`, `Car 01`.
- **Not a stale element id** — the guid returned by `CreateObjects`
  (`BEC370CC-8CE6-412C-BA44-A0F04DB6940C`) is exactly the guid that appears in a subsequent
  `GetElementsByType`, so `DeleteElements` is being given the correct identifier.
- **Not a locked layer** — moving the object to a layer where Slabs delete successfully
  (`Des: Site Structures`) changes nothing.
- **Not selection state** — adding the elements via `ChangeSelectionOfElements`
  (which reports `success: true` per element) before deleting changes nothing.
- **Not a general failure at that moment** — a throwaway Slab created and deleted cleanly
  immediately after an Object delete had no-opped.

## Not tested

Whether Objects placed **by hand in the UI** delete correctly. Only API-created Objects were
tested, so the fault may lie in creation rather than deletion.

## Impact

The silent success is the substantive part. `DeleteElements` returns `{"success": true}`
regardless, so a caller cannot distinguish a delete that happened from one that did not without
re-reading the element count. It would be more useful if the command reported per-element results
the way `CreateObjects` and `ModifyRoofs` do, or returned an error when nothing was removed.
author: kozure-dev

title: `SetGDLParametersOfElements` on a Cadimage CI Tools Window: `glazingPanelType` hangs Archicad, `glazingPanelN` returns success and corrupts the element
body:
## Environment

- Archicad 28.0.0 R1 (6003), NZE
- Tapir add-on 1.5.7
- Windows 11
- Cadimage CI Tools Window (library part shipped with Cadimage Tools)

## Summary

Writing either of the two panel-layout parameters of a Cadimage CI Tools Window through `SetGDLParametersOfElements` fails, in two different ways. One parameter on one element is enough for both.

| parameter | result |
| --- | --- |
| `glazingPanelType` | Archicad stops responding. Force close, write never lands. |
| `glazingPanelN` | Returns `{"success": true}`, Archicad stays responsive, and the element's GDL parameters become permanently unreadable. |

The second is the reason I am filing this. A hang is obvious and costs a restart. A write that reports success and quietly destroys the element it touched can reach a drawing set without anyone noticing.

## Values are not guessed

Both values below were read out of windows configured by hand in the Archicad UI, using `GetGDLParametersOfElements`, then written unchanged to a plain single-fixed window of the same type. Nothing here is an invented enumeration.

## Case 1: `glazingPanelType` hangs

One element, one parameter:

```json
{
  "elementsWithGDLParameters": [
    {
      "elementId": {"guid": "..."},
      "gdlParameters": [
        {"name": "glazingPanelType",
         "value": ["X","X","T","X","X","X","X","X","X","X"]}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`T` is the awning code, `F` fixed, `X` an empty slot, read from a window set to a single awning sash.

The request never returns. Archicad reports `Responding: False`, sits at roughly 110% of one core, and has to be force closed. After restart the value is unchanged, so the write does not land.

## Case 2: `glazingPanelN` returns success and corrupts the element

Same element, same shape of call:

```json
{"name": "glazingPanelN", "value": [0, 2, 2, 2, 0]}
```

Response:

```json
{"executionResults": [{"success": true}]}
```

Archicad stays responsive. The element is destroyed. Reading it back:

```json
{"error": {"code": -2130313215,
           "message": "Failed to get parameters of element with guid DE2D1D11-..."}}
```

The damage is scoped exactly to the element written. Reading all 17 CI Tools Windows in the file in a single batched call:

```
batch read ok = true
unreadable: ['EW02']
readable:   16/17
```

The corrupted element still enumerates through `GetElementsByType`, still reports its width and host wall, and still draws in plan and 3D. Only its GDL parameters are gone.

I hit this before I understood it: an earlier window in the same project was damaged the same way and stayed unreadable across two Archicad restarts, with no error anywhere to explain it. The only repair I found was deleting the element and rebuilding it from a Favorite.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place a Cadimage CI Tools Window in a wall.
2. Read its parameters with `GetGDLParametersOfElements` and note `glazingPanelType` and `glazingPanelN`.
3. Call `SetGDLParametersOfElements` with `glazingPanelN` set to `[0, 2, 2, 2, 0]`.
4. Observe `success: true`.
5. Read the element again. The read fails with -2130313215, and keeps failing.

Substituting `glazingPanelType` at step 3 hangs the application instead.

## Expected

Either the write applies, or it is rejected with an error. A parameter that cannot be set safely should fail loudly rather than report success and leave the element unreadable.

## Notes

- Material parameters on the same object are fine. I write 13 of them (`gs_frame_mat`, `sill_mat`, `mainFrameMat` and similar) with no trouble at all, so this is specific to the two panel-layout parameters and not to CI Tools objects generally.
- Batching is not a factor. Both cases above are a single element in a single call.
- Favorites are a working way around it: an element created from a Favorite carries that Favorite's panel layout, so the layout is reachable as long as it is never written directly.
- Possibly related to #555, which I filed against the same add-on version: `DeleteElements` returns success on an Object element and leaves the element in place. Different command, same shape of problem, a call that reports success without doing what it says.
- I appreciate this may sit on the Cadimage side of the boundary rather than in Tapir. Flagging it here since the crash and the corruption both arrive through `SetGDLParametersOfElements`, and a guard at that level may be the practical fix.

I have a small reproduction file (throwaway copy, contains the corrupted element) and can attach it if useful.
author: kozure-dev

title: `CreateDrawings` terminates Archicad when `navigatorItemId` does not resolve to a placeable view
body:
**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| Archicad | 28, build 6003, language NZE |
| Tapir | 1.5.7 |
| OS | Windows 11 |

**Summary**

`CreateDrawings` does not appear to validate `navigatorItemId`. Any guid that does not resolve to a
placeable viewpoint ends the Archicad process: the HTTP connection is reset part way through the
call, nothing is returned, no dialog appears, and the process is gone. Unsaved work is lost.

A guid that exists nowhere in the project is enough, so the smallest reproducer is a single call
with a made up guid.

**Minimal reproducer**

Against any ordinary layout, with a guid that resolves to nothing:

```json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": {
      "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
      "commandName": "CreateDrawings"
    },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
      "drawingsData": [{
        "navigatorItemId":  {"guid": "DEADBEEF-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"},
        "layoutDatabaseId": {"guid": "<any ordinary layout database>"},
        "name": "crash",
        "position": {"x": 0.05, "y": 0.05}
      }]
    }
  }
}
```

**Isolation, four cases**

| | `navigatorItemId` | `layoutDatabaseId` | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | a view in the View Map | ordinary layout | succeeds |
| B | the id `GetDetailsOfElements` reports for an existing Drawing | ordinary layout | **terminates** |
| C | a view in the View Map | **master layout** | succeeds, drawing verified in place |
| D | a guid that exists nowhere | ordinary layout | **terminates** |

A against B, and A against D, hold the target constant and vary only the source, so the target is
not a factor. **C shows master layout databases are fully supported**, which is worth stating
because our first report guessed otherwise.

B is worth calling out separately as the likely route in: `GetDetailsOfElements` on a Drawing
returns a `navigatorItemId`, and passing that back to `CreateDrawings` is the obvious way to copy a
drawing. That id is the drawing's own navigator item rather than the view it draws, so it does not
resolve as a source, and the call takes the application down.

**A neighbouring case that fails cleanly**

Passing a stale `layoutDatabaseId`, from a layout that had since been deleted, returns a proper
error and leaves Archicad running:

```json
{"error": {"code": -2130313110, "message": "Failed to activate the layout database."}}
```

So the command already refuses one class of unusable input on the target side. The source side
appears to have no equivalent guard.

**Suggestion**

Resolve `navigatorItemId` before use and return an error in the same style as the one above when it
is not a viewpoint that can be placed as a drawing. That would cover the unresolvable case, the
wrong-item-type case, and the copy-a-drawing route in one check.
author: kozure-dev

title: Wish: expose ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_* (create/modify/delete override rules and combinations)
body:
## What's missing

Tapir currently has no commands for Graphic Overrides. `SetViewSettings` can *assign* an existing override combination to a view (by name), but there is no way to create, modify or delete the rules and combinations themselves.

## Why this matters

Graphic Overrides are how an office expresses its graphic standard — poché styles, fire-compartment and code-compliance colouring, thermal, demolition/renovation. Today every office has to author them by hand in the UI, once per template, and there is no way to version them, generate them from project data, or roll them out across projects programmatically. For anyone maintaining a template as code, this is the single largest remaining gap.

## The API is already there

The Archicad 29 C++ API exposes a complete CRUD for this — 22 functions in the Graphic Overrides group, including:

- `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_CreateOverrideRule` / `CreateOverrideRuleGroup` / `CreateOverrideCombination`
- `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_ChangeOverrideRule` / `ChangeOverrideRuleGroup` / `ChangeOverrideCombination` / `MoveOverrideRule`
- `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_DeleteOverrideRule` / `DeleteOverrideRuleGroup` / `DeleteOverrideCombination`
- plus 7 getters, 2 ordering and 2 enable functions.

`API_OverrideRule` is `{ guid, name, style, criterionXML }`, and the SDK ships an `Override_Test` example documenting the criterion XML format. So the hard part — the criteria model — is already solved and serialisable.

## Suggested commands

Mirroring existing Tapir naming:

- `GetGraphicOverrideCombinations` / `GetGraphicOverrideRules`
- `CreateGraphicOverrideRules` / `CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations`
- `ModifyGraphicOverrideRules` / `DeleteGraphicOverrideRules`

Even read-only getters plus `Create*` would unblock most real workflows.

## Note on the existing workaround

Combinations can be exported/imported as XML from the UI dialog, which does allow transporting them between projects. But it's a manual, per-file gesture — it doesn't help generate rules from model data or drive them from a script.

Happy to test on macOS / Archicad 29 (ES) against a large production template if that's useful.

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes returns zMax = 0 for stairs — 3D extent is unverifiable via the API
body:
## Summary

`Get3DBoundingBoxes` returns a flat box for Stair elements: `zMin = zMax = 0` (the footprint is correct). The stair's 3D extent therefore cannot be verified through the API at all — which matters because stairs are also the element class where input parameters and solver output can legitimately diverge (#425), so callers need an independent read-back more than anywhere else.

Split out of #425 on @tlorantfy's suggestion.

## Repro (AC28 Win, 1.5.8 base build)

```json
CreateStairs {"stairsData": [{"baseLinePoints": [{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":0,"y":5}], "zCoordinate": 0.0, "totalHeight": 3.25}]}
Get3DBoundingBoxes {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "<created>"}}]}
```

Result: `boundingBox3D.zMin = 0, zMax = 0` although the created stair spans 3.25 m vertically (visible in 3D). Walls/slabs/beams/roofs return correct z extents through the same call.

## Expected

`zMax − zMin ≈ totalHeight` (plus structure thickness), like every other element type.
