title: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection still returns ghost GUIDs: the #512 guard was not applied to it (Interior Elevation, 1.5.8)
body:
### Summary

The ghost-GUID guard added in #512 was applied to `CreateAssociativeDimensions` and `CreateWallThicknessDimensions`, but not to `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`. That command still returns a success response with an element GUID when nothing is created.

This also answers the question left open when #509 was closed:

> Built against AC29; the live check on a real section is on the PR's test plan. @weltmaister @sceptic420 - a try on your side once it is merged would be welcome, particularly whether the interior-elevation sub-views behave the same as plain sections.

They do not. `GetSectionElements` (#535) works perfectly on an interior-elevation sub-view - it is what makes the whole flow reachable, thank you - but the dimension command it feeds does not create anything there.

### Environment

- macOS, Archicad 28, Tapir add-on **1.5.8**
- Solo project, not Teamwork
- Interior Elevation sub-view of a composite marker, live interior-design project

### The gap in the source

In `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp` under 1.5.8, both patched commands carry the post-create check and a comment referring to #510:

```cpp
// Same ghost-guid failure mode as CreateAssociativeDimensions (#510): with a
// section/elevation window active the create reports success although nothing
// was created in any database. Verify before reporting the id.
API_Element createdElement = {};
```

`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSectionCommand::Execute` has no such check - it pushes the GUID straight after `ACAPI_Element_Create` returns `NoError`:

```cpp
err = ACAPI_Element_Create (&element, &memo);
if (err != NoError) {
    elements.Push (CreateErrorResponse (err, "Failed to create associative section dimension."));
    continue;
}

elements.Push (CreateElementIdObjectState (element.header.guid));
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Resolve the Interior Elevation database with `GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId`.
2. `GetSectionElements` on that database; pick an entry whose `ownerElementType` is `Wall`.
3. `GetElementsByType { "elementType": "Dimension", "databases": [<that database>] }` -> **3 dimensions**.
4. Call:

```json
{
  "dimensionsData": [{
    "sectionElementId": { "guid": "<wall section element>" },
    "referencePoint": { "x": 2.0, "y": 2.5 },
    "preset": "WallCompositeFaces"
  }]
}
```

5. Response: success, with an element id - e.g. `7C2FF40B-2748-A448-8482-6BFB71E4906A`.
6. Repeat step 3 -> **still 3**.
7. `GetDetailsOfElements` on the returned GUID -> **`Failed to get the details of element`**.

### The guard demonstrably works on the sibling command

Same session, same Interior Elevation, the patched command refuses honestly:

```
CreateWallThicknessDimensions -> { "error": { "code": -2130313215,
                                   "message": "Failed to create wall thickness dimension." } }
```

So #512 is doing its job where it was applied. Only the unpatched command still hands back a GUID for an element that does not exist.

### Ruled out by test, not by assumption

- **Not the MCP wrapper.** Reproduced through the raw JSON API (plain HTTP POST to `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`, no wrapper, no `archicad` package) and independently through an MCP client. Different GUIDs each run, same outcome.
- **Not the active window.** Re-run with the active window explicitly switched to the target Interior Elevation via `ChangeWindow` first. Same result. (`ChangeWindow` into an Interior Elevation works correctly under 1.5.8, for what it is worth.)
- **Not a general restriction on writing into an Interior Elevation.** In the same database and session, `CreateLabels` returns a GUID that `GetDetailsOfElements` resolves with real data, and the label is visible and deletable.
- **Not a hidden or locked layer** for the dimensions already in that view: layer index 215 returns `isHidden: false`, `isLocked: false` from `GetLayers`. I could not read the Dimension tool's own default layer - there is no command for a tool default - so I make no claim about where the element would have been placed.

### Suggested fix

Apply the same post-create verification from #512 to `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSectionCommand::Execute`. That would turn this into an honest error, which is all a caller needs.

Whether the dimension itself can be made to work in an interior-elevation sub-view is the larger question, and the one #509 anticipated. Happy to run anything against a real Archicad 28 project - the repro is set up here, on a project with 54 interior elevation views.
author: gustavodazarq-blip

title: The #539 navigator fields cannot reach generated clients while GetNavigatorItemTree has no response schema
body:
### Context

When closing #538 via #539, you noted:

> Tapir's `GetNavigatorItemTree` has never had a response schema (it does not override `GetRawResponseSchema`), so these fields are undocumented in the command reference. Writing one needs a self-referential `$ref` for the children recursion, which I would rather do as its own change than fold into a field addition.

This is not a new finding - it is a report of what that missing schema costs downstream, which may bear on how it is prioritised.

### The consequence

Generators that build typed clients from the command reference cannot emit a binding for a command with no documented result, so they drop the command:

- `multiconn_archicad` v0.6.8 has a `GetNavigatorItemTreeParameters` model and **no `GetNavigatorItemTreeResult`**.
- `tapir-archicad-MCP` v0.5.3 therefore excludes Tapir's version outright, in `scripts/generator_config.py`:

```python
"GetNavigatorItemTree",  # result model missing from tapir documentation
```

and falls back to the official Archicad JSON API command of the same name.

### Why this bears on #539 specifically

The official `NavigatorItem` type carries only `navigatorItemId`, `prefix`, `name`, `type`, `sourceNavigatorItemId` and children. It has no `uiId`, `customUiId`, `customName` or `isIndependent`.

So the four fields added in #539 and shipped in 1.5.8 are implemented in the add-on but **cannot be reached through a generated client**, because the only command that carries them is the one being dropped. The audit use case from #538 - finding views whose ID or name has been hand-overridden - is still not reachable that way.

### Verified

Against a live Archicad 28 project, add-on 1.5.8, with multiconn v0.6.8 and wrapper v0.5.3 regenerated from the 1.5.8 documentation:

- `grep` for `GetNavigatorItemTreeResult` in multiconn v0.6.8: no match. `GetNavigatorItemTreeParameters` is present.
- The generated MCP tool `navigator_get_navigator_item_tree` resolves to the official command; calling it on the Project Map returns items with `prefix`, `name`, `type` and `navigatorItemId` only - no `uiId`, `customUiId`, `customName` or `isIndependent` on any node.

### Suggestion

Nothing new in substance - only that the self-referential response schema you already planned is what unblocks #539 in practice, not just in the documentation.

Happy to verify against a build. The project here has 54 interior elevation views under a naming standard, with a mix of inherited and hand-overridden IDs, which exercises the custom-ID/custom-name distinction well.
author: gustavodazarq-blip

title: GetDetailsOfElements returns 'Not yet supported element type' for roofs (no RoofDetails)
body:
### Summary

`GetDetailsOfElements` returns `details.error = "Not yet supported element type"` for **Roof** elements, so roof geometry cannot be read through Tapir at all. Observed on Archicad 27.

### What's missing

- In `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`, the `GetDetailsOfElements` switch has no `case API_RoofID`; roofs fall into the `default` branch, which adds `"error": "Not yet supported element type"`.
- In `docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js`, the `TypeSpecificDetails` `oneOf` has no `RoofDetails` entry (it ends with `NotYetSupportedElementTypeDetails`).

So there is currently no way to read:

- a **single-plane roof**'s plan outline (`u.planeRoof.poly`) + pivot line (`baseLine`) + pitch (`angle`), nor
- a **multi-plane roof**'s pivot polygon (`u.polyRoof.pivotPolygon`) + per-plane `levels` + `eavesOverhang`.

### Related write-side gap

`ModifyRoofs` only accepts multi-plane roofs (it returns "Only multi-plane roofs are supported." for single-plane roofs) and rewrites the pivot polygon, not the plan outline. A geometry-only single-plane modify path (mirroring the existing `ModifySlabs` polygon-only path) would also be useful.

### Note

This was believed to be covered in #145 ("slab/roof outline polygons"), which was closed as completed. The closing comment only lists typed variants for Wall/Beam/Column/Slab/Polyline, and there is no roof read case in the code. Opening this as a focused follow-up.
author: cgpp5

title: SetStories cannot create stories below the existing structure — negative story indices are unreachable (APIStory_InsBelow is never used)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 28 (Win), Tapir release 1.5.8. The relevant code path in `ProjectCommands.cpp` is unchanged on current `main`.

### What happens

On a fresh project (single story at index 0), sending the full desired story list bottom-up:

```json
{ "stories": [
  { "dispOnSections": true, "level": -5.95, "name": "Basement 2" },
  { "dispOnSections": true, "level": -3.10, "name": "Basement 1" },
  { "dispOnSections": true, "level":  0.00, "name": "Ground floor" }
] }
```

creates the right levels and names, but the indices come out as **0 / 1 / 2** — the deepest basement becomes story 0 and the ground floor story 2. The common convention (ground floor at ±0.00 = index 0, basements −1, −2, …) is unreachable: `GetStories` afterwards reports `firstStory: 0`. In the Story Settings dialog the same structure is trivially created via "Insert Below".

### Root cause

`SetStoriesCommand::Execute` grows the structure exclusively with

```cpp
storyCmd.action = APIStory_InsAbove;
storyCmd.index  = storyInfo.lastStory;
```

so every new story lands on top. `APIStory_InsBelow` exists in the API right next to `InsAbove` but is never called. The input schema (`StorySettings`) also has no `index` field, so the request cannot even express where a story belongs — matching is purely positional.

### Suggested fix

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

1. **Match by level instead of position when growing:** if the requested list contains levels below the current `firstStory` level, insert those with `APIStory_InsBelow` at `firstStory` (mirror of the existing `InsAbove` branch). This keeps the current schema and makes the positional diff behave intuitively.
2. **Add an optional `index` to `StorySettings`** and honor it, so a client can pin the numbering explicitly (`GetStories` already reports `index`, so the round-trip would become symmetric).

### Workaround (for anyone hitting this now)

Create the story structure once in the Story Settings dialog (or start from a template that has the basements), then use `SetStories` only to set levels/names positionally.

Happy to submit a PR for option 1 if you'd take it.
author: weltmaister

title: SetStories with pinned index: levels sent in the same call land shifted when growing from a single story (follow-up to #571)
body:
**Environment:** AC28 GER (Win), current main build including #571 (2026-08-20).

First: #571 works — the pinned `index` immediately produced the right structure in every test. This is a follow-up about the **levels** sent in the same call.

### Repro

Fresh project reduced to **one** story (level −5.95). One `SetStories` call:

```json
{ "stories": [
  { "index": -2, "dispOnSections": true, "level": -5.95, "name": "B2" },
  { "index": -1, "dispOnSections": true, "level": -3.10, "name": "B1" },
  { "index":  0, "dispOnSections": true, "level":  0.00, "name": "GF" },
  { "index":  1, "dispOnSections": true, "level":  3.10, "name": "UF" }
] }
```

**Observed:** indices/names correct (`firstStory:-2 … lastStory:1`), but the levels came out as **−11.90 / −9.05 / −5.95 / −5.95** instead of −5.95/−3.10/0.00/3.10.

### Mechanism (from reading the merged code)

- The grow loops fill the new stories' `height` from the requested list, but the **anchor story keeps its current level** (−5.95) until the later per-story pass — so every inserted story's absolute level is shifted by the anchor's yet-uncorrected offset (here −5.95 vs. the requested 0.00 for that story).
- The subsequent level-correction pass uses `APIStory_SetElevation`, which **moves all stories above along with the changed one**, and the pass is capped at `maxRecursion = 3` — with every level needing a shift, it does not converge within the cap. The call still returns success.

### Workaround (verified)

Two-pass: first create the structure with `index` (levels may be anything), then set the levels in a **second** pass — full list per call, one target level per call, top-down. After that, `GetStories` reported all levels and heights correct.

### Suggested fix directions

- After the grow/delete phase, set the **anchor story's elevation first** (or apply levels top-down within the same call), so the inserted heights land on the right absolute base; or
- raise/replace the 3-iteration convergence cap and verify the final levels against the request before returning success — a shifted result should be a per-call error, not silent success.

Happy to re-test any revision live, as with #571.
author: weltmaister

title: ApplyFavoritesToElements relocates Stair elements (geometry not preserved)
body:
**Tapir version:** 1.5.7 · **Archicad:** 28 (Windows)

The docs for `ApplyFavoritesToElements` say: *"Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions …) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves or resizes the target element."*

For **Stair** elements this does not hold: applying a stair favorite to placed stairs reports `success: true` per element, but the stairs are **moved to entirely different positions** in the project (they appear scattered; baselines no longer match where they were created).

### Repro

1. Create a few stairs via `CreateStairs` at known baselines.
2. Create any stair favorite (e.g. via `CreateFavoritesFromElements` from one of them, or use a template favorite such as the German template's "Treppe Ortbeton").
3. `ApplyFavoritesToElements` with that favorite on the placed stairs.
4. All calls succeed; the stairs are no longer at their original baselines.

### Where it probably comes from

`ApplyFavoritesToElementsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/FavoritesCommands.cpp`) calls

```cpp
API_Element mask = {};
ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SETFULL (mask);
err = ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters (targetGuids, &favorite.element, favorite.memo.GetPtr (), &mask);
```

i.e. a **full** mask together with the favorite's **memo**. The "never touches geometry" guarantee rests on `ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters` semantics, but for a Stair the memo is where the geometry lives — `memo.stairBaseLine` (coords / pends / polygon), the same handle `CreateStairsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` fills to place the stair. Passing the favorite's baseline into the target element would explain exactly the observed relocation, and would also mean the guarantee is unreliable for the other memo-carrying hierarchical types (Curtain Wall, Railing) rather than for Stairs specifically.

If that is the mechanism, the fix would be to withhold the geometry-carrying memo fields (or the memo entirely) for these types rather than to weaken the mask.

### Related observation

`ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` with a stair favorite also has no effect on subsequently created stairs' structure/finishes — presumably because the element defaults used by `CreateStairs` don't include the hierarchical sub-element settings. Together these two make stair structure effectively uncontrollable through the API; #580 adds a `finishVisible` escape hatch for the one case we needed, but it is not a general answer.
author: Liquidmasl

title: ApplyFavoritesToElements on Windows fails: "The Favorite's element type does not match the target element's type"
body:
**Tapir version:** 1.5.7 · **Archicad:** 28 (Windows)

Applying a **Window** favorite to a placed **Window** element always fails with:

```json
{ "error": { "code": -2130313115,
  "message": "The Favorite's element type does not match the target element's type." } }
```

### Repro

1. A project with placed windows and at least one Window favorite (`GetFavoritesByType {"elementType": "Window"}` lists it; the favorite is a regular `WindDefault` favorite created in the Archicad UI).
2. `ApplyFavoritesToElements` with `{"elementId": <window's id>, "favorite": "<that favorite>"}`.
3. Every element fails with the type-mismatch error above — including applying a favorite that was created *from* a window of the same library part.

### Notes

The check is in `ApplyFavoritesToElementsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/FavoritesCommands.cpp`) and compares `header.type` only:

```cpp
const bool typeMatches = favorite.element.header.type == targetElement.header.type;
```

So whatever `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` returns for these favorites, it is not `API_WindowID`. Two things that may narrow it down:

* The same check passes for other types — Stairs go through it fine (see the sibling report about stair geometry, #576) — so it is not a blanket failure of the comparison.
* #397 documents that windows placed with dual-use library parts report `header.variationID = APIVarId_CornerWindow` even when placed as regular windows, and that `CreateFavoritesFromElements` stores them accordingly. If the stored variation also affects what `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` fills in for a name-only lookup, the two issues may share a root cause. Note that `GetFavoritesByType` passes `nullptr` for the variation on AC26+, which is presumably why such a favorite still shows up under `"elementType": "Window"`.

Worth checking as part of that: `API_Favorite favorite;` is left uninitialized before `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` in both `ApplyFavoritesToElements` and `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` — if the call treats any part of `favorite.element.header` as an input key for the lookup, the behaviour would depend on stack contents.

### Workaround we use

Delete the window and re-create it via `CreateWindows` with `favoriteName` plus the old `GetDetailsOfElements` values (ownerWallId / centerOffset / sillHeight / width / height / reflected / refSide / oSide) — that path works and preserves geometry (187/187 windows in our test project).
author: Liquidmasl

title: CreateStairs rejects multi-segment baselines that turn clockwise (-2130313215)
body:
**Tapir version:** 1.5.7 (includes the #444/#445 multi-segment fix) · **Archicad:** 28 (Windows)

Multi-segment stair baselines whose corners turn **clockwise** (right turns) consistently fail with `-2130313215 "Failed to create new Stair"`, while the **mirrored or reversed** polyline of the exact same geometry (turning counter-clockwise) creates fine.

### Repro (empty project, story at 0.00)

```json
// FAILS — L-shape turning right (clockwise)
{ "stairsData": [ { "baseLinePoints": [ {"x": 30, "y": 30}, {"x": 36, "y": 30}, {"x": 36, "y": 24} ],
                    "zCoordinate": 0.0, "totalHeight": 3.0 } ] }

// WORKS — same L mirrored, turning left (counter-clockwise)
{ "stairsData": [ { "baseLinePoints": [ {"x": 30, "y": 40}, {"x": 36, "y": 40}, {"x": 36, "y": 46} ],
                    "zCoordinate": 0.0, "totalHeight": 3.0 } ] }
```

Also reproduced with real U-shaped walklines from a Revit conversion: the clockwise ones fail in every parameter combination we tried (with and without `flightWidth` / `stepNum` / `riserHeight` / `treadDepth`), while their reversed polylines create fine.

### Context

This is a follow-up to #444: since that fix, `CreateStairsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` deliberately leaves `memo.stairBaseLine.edgeData` / `vertexData` null so that `ACAPI_Element_Create` derives them from the baseline geometry. The turn-direction dependency presumably lives in that derivation — the default winder/turning rules appear to solve only one direction. So the straightforward workaround (reverse the polyline) is available to callers, but it silently changes the stair's up direction, which is not always acceptable.

Happy to provide more failing/working polylines, including the real U-shaped ones, if that helps.
author: Liquidmasl

title: CreateStairs: apply the resolved z offset instead of dropping it
body:
`CreateStairsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` calls `ResolveFloorIndexAndOffset (parameters, "floorIndex", zCoordinate, stories)` but only assigns `floorIndexAndOffset.first` (the floor index). The offset (`.second`) is dropped, so **every created stair sits exactly on its home story level**, regardless of `zCoordinate`.

Any stair whose base is not exactly on a story plane is affected — an exterior stair starting 1.9 m above the story, or an interior flight starting a few cm below the finished-floor level.

The sibling commands all apply their offset — `CreateSlabs` → `element.slab.level`, `CreateRoofs` → `element.roof.shellBase.level`, `CreateBeams` → `element.beam.level`, `CreateColumns` → `element.column.bottomOffset`. Stairs now do the same via `element.stair.basePlane.basePoint.z`.

### Repro (Archicad 28, any project with a story at 0.00)

```json
{ "stairsData": [ {
  "baseLinePoints": [ {"x": 0, "y": 0}, {"x": 6, "y": 0} ],
  "zCoordinate": 1.0,
  "totalHeight": 3.0
} ] }
```

Before: the stair base is at 0.00. After: at 1.00.

Verified on AC 28 / Windows (DevKit 28.3001, VS2022 BuildTools, toolset v142) with a collision probe against a slab placed at 0.2–0.5 m — a bounding-box check cannot show this, since stair bounding boxes come back z-degenerate (#563). Also exercised across a Revit→Archicad conversion with 12 stairs on 8 stories.


---

Note for whoever merges: #580 (`finishVisible`) touches the same function a few lines below this one-line change. They are independent, but whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase — happy to do it.
author: Liquidmasl

title: CreateStairs: optional finishVisible for bare (structure-only) stairs
body:
A created stair always carries the default tread/riser finishes; there is no way to request a bare (e.g. monolithic cast-in-place) stair through the JSON API.

Changing the stair *tool default* beforehand does not help either, because the element defaults fetched for the create do not carry the hierarchical sub-element settings — the same reason `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` with a stair favorite has no effect on subsequently created stairs (#576).

This adds an optional boolean `finishVisible` to the `CreateStairs` input schema. When `false`, `element.stair.finishVisible` and the `tread[role].visible` / `riser[role].visible` flags are cleared for both part roles, so only the stair structure is modeled. Omitted → unchanged behavior.

The second commit adds the matching `FinishVisible` input to the Create Stairs Grasshopper component. It is an optional `Field` entry, so existing definitions keep working.

Verified on Archicad 28 / Windows (DevKit 28.3001, VS2022 BuildTools, toolset v142), across a Revit→Archicad conversion with 12 stairs including U-shaped winder flights. The other DevKit versions are covered only by this PR's build checks — happy to guard the code if AC25/26 lack `API_StairPartRoleNum` or the `finishVisible` field.


---

Note for whoever merges: #579 (the `CreateStairs` z-offset bug fix) touches the same function a few lines above this change. They are independent, but whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase — happy to do it.
author: Liquidmasl

title: ModifyWindows / ModifyDoors: expose reveal and revealDepthOffset
body:
The frame plane position across the wall thickness (`API_WindowType.reveal` + `revealDepthOffset`) is not reachable through the JSON API at all: windows and doors created via `CreateWindows`/`CreateDoors` always sit at the wall reference plane, and none of the ~900 GDL parameters of the library part move it (`refSide`/`oSide` only mirror).

This exposes the two fields on `ModifyWindows` and `ModifyDoors` through the shared `ApplyWindowOrDoorDetails` helper, so they follow the same optional-field pattern as `refSide`/`oSide` next to them.

Behaviour is exactly linear — one metre of `revealDepthOffset` moves the frame one metre along the wall normal, sign depending on the wall's reference side — and width, height, sill height and elevation are untouched (verified by measuring floor-plan polygons).

The second commit adds the matching `Reveal` and `RevealDepthOffsets` inputs to the Modify Windows and Modify Doors Grasshopper components. Optional `Field` entries, so existing definitions keep working.

Verified on Archicad 28 / Windows (DevKit 28.3001, VS2022 BuildTools, toolset v142), across a Revit→Archicad conversion with 187 windows and 220 doors. The other DevKit versions are covered only by this PR's build checks.

author: JBENEITEZ

title: GetDetailsOfElements terminates Archicad 29 on one specific element of the stock Hillside House sample
body:
## Summary

`GetDetailsOfElements` **terminates Archicad** when asked about one specific
element in the unmodified **AC29 Hillside House GRAPHISOFT sample**. The socket
resets and the process exits; Archicad's own Bug Reporter appears.

The same command, in the same session, returns a clean per-element error for a
guid that matches nothing at all. So the error path exists and works - this
element takes a different path, and that one is fatal.

Because the sample project ships identically to everyone, the guid below should
be the same in your copy.

```
8AA90DC1-8FFE-9542-92CD-4662EAFC5C20
```

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Archicad | 29 build 3000 (USA) |
| Tapir | 1.5.8 |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 |
| Project | `AC29_Hillside-House_GRAPHISOFT-Sample.pla`, unmodified stock sample |
| Elements in model | 6,725 |

## Reproduction

Standard library only, no dependencies.

```python
import json, urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:19723"
CULPRIT = "8AA90DC1-8FFE-9542-92CD-4662EAFC5C20"

def post(command, parameters):
    body = json.dumps({"command": command, "parameters": parameters}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body,
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read().decode())

post("API.ExecuteAddOnCommand", {
    "addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
                       "commandName": "GetDetailsOfElements"},
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
        "elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": CULPRIT}}]},
})
```

1. Open the AC29 Hillside House sample.
2. Run the above.
3. Archicad terminates.

Confirmed on a **freshly copied** `.pla`, so accumulated recovery state is not
involved.

## Three explanations ruled out by measurement

**1. Not request size.** From one bisection run, same session, same project:

| Elements in request | Result |
|---|---|
| **3,362** | succeeded |
| 1,681 | **terminated Archicad** |
| 840 | **terminated Archicad** |
| 52 | **terminated Archicad** |
| 6 | **terminated Archicad** |
| **1** | **terminated Archicad** |

A 3,362-element request succeeded while a 1-element request killed the
application. Any batch containing this element dies regardless of size; any
batch without it survives regardless of size.

**2. Not element type in general.** One element of each of the **31 element
types present in the model** was sent as its own single-element request. All 31
returned normally.

**3. Not malformed input.** An invented guid, in the same session, is handled
cleanly:

```json
{"detailsOfElements": [
  {"error": {"code": -2130313115,
             "message": "Failed to get the details of element"}}]}
```

That is the correct behaviour, and it shows the per-element error path works.
The real element does not reach it.

## The likely mechanism

The culprit is returned by `GetAllElements` (scoped to the story databases) but
by **no** `GetElementsByType` query across **62 types** tried - the full
`ElementType` enum. Five other elements in the model share that property, and
they were the other finalists of the bisection:

```
8AA90DC1-8FFE-9542-92CD-4662EAFC5C20   <- confirmed fatal on its own
9DA46CAE-2D15-4C49-9281-B293C552A7D3
986A50A4-906E-8143-9B49-2BD4729ABCA3
C68D87E3-ED5B-A146-B409-7A0B7B2D874D
1298147A-C1B2-9F4D-9E25-DE86669E884A
E7C91731-6CCE-C241-9EC7-6CD229DE5615
```

An element that `GetAllElements` hands out but that no type query claims looks
like one whose type has no branch in the detail dispatch. Issue #569 shows the
graceful form of that - `GetDetailsOfElements` returning "Not yet supported
element type" for roofs. This path appears to fall through into something fatal
instead.

I did not test the other five individually; each test costs an Archicad restart.
They are the obvious next place to look.

## Suggested fix

Whatever the element turns out to be, the per-element error path already exists
and is already correct - the invented-guid case proves it. Routing the unhandled
type into that same path, rather than whatever it currently does, would turn a
process termination into `{"error": ...}` for that one element and leave the
rest of the batch usable.

## Impact

One unlucky element makes `GetDetailsOfElements` unusable across an entire
project, and the failure mode is data loss rather than an error: Archicad exits,
taking unsaved work with it. Callers cannot defend against it - catching the
exception does not help once the application is gone, and there is nothing left
to retry against.

## Also reported to Graphisoft

Submitted via Archicad's Bug Reporter as **`AC29-2026-08-24-14-57-17-1929`**
(detailed report, 2026-08-24), in case the fault sits on the Archicad side of
the add-on boundary.

## Method

Found by bisection over all 6,725 elements, with state persisted before each
request so that a probe left unanswered identified the request that killed the
process. Five Archicad restarts, 43 probes.
author: 67Fresh

title: A read-only view/layout standards audit built on Tapir, looking for projects to break it
body:
I built a tool on top of Tapir that answers a question Archicad can't:
**which views in this project carry custom settings instead of a named
combination?**

`GetViewSettings` returns an empty string for `layerCombination`,
`penSetName`, `modelViewOptions`, `dimensionStyle` or
`graphicOverrideCombination` when a view has custom settings rather than a
named one. That empty string is the mechanism behind office standards
quietly failing to propagate. Those views don't follow when the standard
changes, and there's no way to list them from inside Archicad.

So it lists them. It also reports duplicate sheet numbers, sheets with no
number, layouts sitting outside any subset, and layouts with no drawings on
them (that last one comes free from the Layout Book tree, since a
LayoutItem's children *are* its drawings, so no element query is needed).

On the stock Hillside House sample: 172 views, 38 layouts, 4 views on custom
layer combinations, 97.7% consistency.

**What I'm asking for.** It has only ever run against Hillside House and the
generic template. That's a terrible sample. I'd like a handful of people to
run it on real projects and tell me where it's wrong: miscounts, crashes,
things it claims that aren't true, structures it doesn't understand.

It's a single .exe, needs no Python, and:

- reads only, never writes to the project
- makes no network calls at all (127.0.0.1 only)
- writes two files: a full HTML report, and a counts-only summary with no
  project, view or sheet names in it, so you can share results without
  disclosing anything about the job

If you'd like to try it, reply here and I'll send it over. Happy to send the
source instead if you'd rather read it before running it.

A few things I learned building on Tapir that might be useful to others here:

- `GetDocumentRevisions` returned **zero** on a project with 38 layouts. A
  layout only has a revision once it's been issued, so the Layout Book tree
  has to be the source of truth for layouts, not revisions.
- `prefix` is empty on layouts; **`uiId`** carries the layout number.
- Neither layout names nor numbers are unique. Hillside House has 38 layouts,
  26 distinct names, 34 distinct numbers.
- `GetNavigatorItemTree` has no declared output schema. The real shape is
  `{"navigatorItemTree": {...}}` with each child wrapped in
  `{"navigatorItem": ...}`, and there's no `rootItem`.

Thanks for Tapir. None of this would exist without it.

title: Add possibleEnumValues to an existing property (and read them back)
body:
### Context

We create a singleEnum property via `CreatePropertyDefinitions`. Later we want
to add a value to its option list in projects that already have the property.

### Problem

`UpdatePropertyDefinitions` accepts only `propertyId` and `expressions`, and
returns "property is not expression-based" for a singleEnum.

`DeletePropertyDefinitions` + recreate works mechanically but destroys every
element's stored value, so it isn't usable.

We can't find any command that modifies `possibleEnumValues` on an existing
property.

### Requests

1. A way to add values to `possibleEnumValues` on an existing property,
   ideally additively so existing values and element assignments survive.
2. A command that returns a property's current value descriptor including
   `possibleEnumValues`. `GetAllPropertyNames` returns names only, so we
   can't currently detect that a project's option list has drifted from our
   definition.

### Concrete case

We ship a classification/property definition that includes a `LYNQr SCHEDULE`
singleEnum. When we add a new value (e.g. `SKYLIGHT SCHEDULE`), projects
provisioned before that addition can never receive it, because our diff sees
the property already exists and there is no command to extend its option
list. Every such project needs a manual edit in Property Manager, per project,
forever.

Tapir 1.5.8, Archicad 29.

author: lpereira-jdva

title: Read and extend a property's possibleEnumValues (#589)
body:
Fixes #589. Both halves of it — @sprtic1 asked in the thread whether the read
side was in scope, and it is: without it you cannot tell which projects have
drifted, so the write alone would still mean opening Property Manager in each
one to find out where to write.

## Read

`GetAllProperties` now reports `possibleEnumValues` for enumeration properties,
in the same `enumValue` shape `CreatePropertyDefinitions` already accepts, plus
the value's `enumValueId` so a caller can tell two identically-named values
apart.

## Write

`UpdatePropertyDefinitions` accepts `possibleEnumValues` alongside (or instead
of) `expressions`. It is **additive**:

- a value already on the property is matched by `nonLocalizedValue`, or by
  `displayValue` when it has none, and left completely untouched;
- values on the property that the call does not mention are kept;
- only genuinely new values are appended, with a fresh identifier.

That matters for the reason the triage comment flagged: an element's stored
value refers to an enum value **by its `keyVariant` guid**. Regenerating the
existing values' guids would detach every stored value in the project, which is
the same damage as delete-and-recreate. So the existing entries are carried
across untouched rather than rebuilt.

`expressions` keeps its old behaviour and still requires an expression-based
property; `possibleEnumValues` requires an enumeration. Sending neither is now
an error that names both, rather than the old blanket
`property is not expression-based`.

The `enumValue` shape is now a single `PossibleEnumValues` definition in
`CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`, referenced from `PropertyDefinition`,
`PropertyDetails` and the update input, instead of a copy per command.

## Status: built, **not** live-verified

Compiles on AC29. I could not run it, and I want to be precise about why rather
than imply it is tested:

The scratch project has 1802 properties and **zero** enumeration properties, so
there was nothing to read or extend, and I could not create one to test
against: `CreatePropertyDefinitions` refuses a `singleEnum` in that project with
`failed to create the property` from `ACAPI_Property_CreatePropertyDefinition`
itself, after the schema validation passes. That is the existing create command,
untouched by this branch, but it blocked the fixture.

So the two things a maintainer with a real project should check are exactly the
two claims above:

1. after adding a value, an element that had one of the **old** values still
   reports it — this is the one that matters, and the one the triage comment
   said needed a seat;
2. `GetAllProperties` lists the full option list, and the identifiers of the
   pre-existing values are unchanged across the update.

`archicad-addon/Examples/add_enum_values_to_property.py` does both checks and
prints the verdict; it needs an existing `Tapir Example / Schedule` singleEnum
property to run against.

No new command, so no `AddOnMain.cpp` registration and no version bump.

author: tlorantfy

title: Run bot jobs using Fabel 5
body:
All three Claude jobs now run on **`claude-fable-5`**, with the turn and timeout
caps raised to match.

## Why the caps went up

Turn exhaustion was the actual failure mode, twice — not wall-clock:

- the fix job died on `Reached maximum number of turns (60)` after 7 minutes;
- the review on #554 hit `41 turns, exceeding the configured maximum of 40`
  **after finishing the work**, so the run failed and the review was lost.

| job | turns | timeout |
|---|---|---|
| triage | 40 → **80** | 20 → **45 min** |
| fix | 60 → **120** | 30 → **60 min** |
| review | 60 → **120** | 20 → **45 min** |

The timeouts rise with the turns because Fable 5 spends much longer inside a
single request than Opus does — a job cap that was generous for 40 Opus turns is
not for 120 Fable ones.

## Two things to know about Fable 5

- **It requires 30-day data retention** and is not available under zero data
  retention. If the org is set below that, every request fails with a 400 that
  has nothing to do with the request itself.
- Whether a **Pro/Max subscription token** can reach Fable 5 is not something I
  can verify from here. If it cannot, the jobs will fail at authentication —
  reverting is one line per job, back to `claude-opus-5`.

Either failure shows up on the first run after merge, which is the moment to
watch.

author: tlorantfy

title: Drop an include nothing uses
body:
A deliberately small cleanup, and I want to be straight about why it is small
rather than pad it.

## What is in it

`IFCCommands.cpp` included `ACAPI/IFCAssignments.hpp` but never named
`Assignments`. That file reads IFC objects and properties; it does not touch the
assignment tree. The stray include has already misled a reader once — the triage
on #590 cited it as a hint that an IFC write path might live there.

Built against **AC29 and AC25**, so both sides of the `ServerMainVers_2800`
guard.

## What I deliberately did not do

**The biggest cleanup in the add-on collides with every open PR.** Manual
`BMKillHandle` cleanup repeated on every early return:

| file | occurrences | touched by |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectCommands.cpp` | 21 | #574 |
| `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp` | 13 | #463, #587 |

Both are the same pattern — a handle freed by hand at each of a dozen exits,
which is a leak waiting for the next `return` someone adds. `GS::OnExit` is
already used elsewhere in the codebase (`CalculateStairBounds`) and would remove
the whole class. But rewriting the exits of `SetStories` while #574 rewrites its
body would hand a conflict to a branch that is mid-review, and the same for
`ExtendedElementCommands.cpp` against #463 and #587.

That is worth doing **after those land**, not now.

**Things that look like cleanup and are not:**

- `ACAPI/IFCAttribute.hpp` in the same file looks equally unused by a token
  search. It is not: `GetAttributes` returns `std::vector<Attribute>` and
  iterating it needs the complete type.
- `CollectCutFillPolygons` in `ElementCommands.cpp` reads as dead — it is passed
  as a callback to `ACAPI_Element_ShapePrimsExt`, under a version guard.
- The `ACAPI/MEP*.hpp` includes in `MEPCommands.cpp` (13 of them) all resolve to
  types spelled differently from their header names.

Each of those would have compiled fine on AC29 and broken something else.

title: Fix what the review found on #596
body:
The review on #596 was right on every count, and #596 was auto-merged seven
minutes after it said "Not ready to merge" — so this fixes the findings on
`main`.

## The one that mattered

**Matching was one-sided**, which defeated the point of the change. A value
already on the property as `{displayValue: "Door"}` with no
`nonLocalizedValue`, sent again with one added, was looked up by
`nonLocalizedValue` only, missed, and appended — leaving two options both
reading "Door" in the UI. Both keys are checked now, so *values already there
are left untouched* holds in both directions.

## The rest

- **`enumValueId` shape** — it is a `oneOf` over `displayValue` /
  `nonLocalizedValue`, and the read side emitted `{"type":"guid","guid":...}`,
  which validates as neither. A value read from `GetAllProperties` could not be
  fed back into a write command. The identifier is now its own `guid` field.
- **Input accepted an identifier it ignored** — the update took
  `PossibleEnumValues`, which carries `enumValueId`, and always assigned a fresh
  guid. It now takes a new `EnumValuesToAdd` with no identifier fields, so there
  is nothing to silently drop.
- **Registered description** in `AddOnMain.cpp` still described the old
  expressions-only command; the generated docs come from it.
- **Indentation** of the moved `PossibleEnumValues` block.
- **The example** printed a hint that `test_examples.py` would have pinned as a
  golden looking like a passing run. It says `SKIPPED:` now.

## Not done, deliberately

`GetAllPropertiesComponent` gains no enum-values output. It exposes ids and
names only, and already omits seven other `PropertyDetails` fields
(`propertyType`, `propertyValueType`, `isExpressionBased`, …), so surfacing
exactly one of them is arbitrary. Exposing that response properly in Grasshopper
is its own change.

## Still unverified, and now I know why

The behaviour claims — existing values keep their guid, elements keep their
stored value — are still untested. `CreatePropertyDefinitions` **cannot create
any property** in the scratch project: a `singleEnum` fails with
`-2130313112` and a plain `string` property with `-2130313104`, both from
`ACAPI_Property_CreatePropertyDefinition` after schema validation passes, with
the property group created successfully first. That is unrelated to this branch
and looks like its own bug, but it is what blocks the fixture.

Built on AC29.

title: Take slab outlines and voids as curves (#582)
body:
Fixes #582. @JBENEITEZ was right on both counts: the input called Vertices was a
point list, so an outline could only ever be straight edges, and arcs and voids
existed only as JSON you had to hand-write into `AdditionalSettings`.

## What the component takes now

- **Outlines** — one closed curve per slab. Line and arc segments are carried
  across as they are, so an arc drawn in Rhino stays an arc in Archicad instead
  of being flattened into chords. Anything else is approximated with a polyline.
- **Holes** — a second curve input, one branch of closed curves per slab. A slab
  with no voids gets an empty branch.

Both are new field kinds on `CreateElementsComponentBase`, so any other creation
command with a polygon can use them without repeating the conversion.

## ⚠️ Breaking

The first input changes from a **point tree** to a **curve list**. An existing
definition feeding points into `Vertices` needs a `PolyLine` component between
the points and this one. Renaming it to `Outlines` makes that visible on the
canvas rather than silently mismatched.

## What needs checking in Rhino — I could not

Built for net48, net7.0 and net7.0-windows, but there is no Rhino or Grasshopper
on this machine, so **none of it has been run**. Three things are worth checking
first, and all three are isolated to one method:

1. **Arc direction.** `arcAngle` is documented as positive when the arc bulges
   to the right of the straight segment from `begIndex` to `endIndex`. A Rhino
   arc whose plane normal points up turns counter-clockwise, which bulges left,
   so its angle is negated. If arcs come out mirrored, that negation is the one
   line to flip.
2. **Node indices.** `begIndex`/`endIndex` are written 0-based within the
   contour, and the closing segment's `endIndex` is folded back to 0, because
   the add-on appends the first node itself (`AddPolyToMemo`). A slab whose last
   segment is an arc is the case that exercises it.
3. **Hole orientation.** Nothing reverses a hole curve, on the assumption
   Archicad does not care. If voids come out solid, that is where to look.

A slab with a straight-edged outline and no voids exercises none of the three,
so it is worth testing an outline with at least one arc, one with a circular
void, and one whose closing segment is an arc.

title: Feature request: batch input for GetZoneBoundaries (severe performance issue on larger projects)
body:
## Problem
I'm building a tool that automatically groups Zones into apartments by detecting open (wall-less) boundaries between rooms.
GetZoneBoundaries provides exactly the information I need through connectedElementId / neighbouringZoneElementId. However, it currently accepts only a single zoneElementId per call, and its performance degrades severely as project size increases.
For a given Zone, I need to identify which other Zone(s) it is directly adjacent to across a boundary with no separating element, including the identity of the neighbouring Zone. GetZoneBoundaries exposes this information per boundary segment through connectedElementId and neighbouringZoneElementId.
## Performance
We measured the following execution times for individual GetZoneBoundaries calls:
| Project size (zones) | Time per call |
|---|---|
| ~15 | < 1 s |
| ~43 | ~3 s |
| ~50 | ~2.7–2.9 s |
| ~225 | ~37–39 s |
| ~400 | ~55–60 s |
The particularly surprising finding is that the cost appears to depend on the total number of Zones in the project, rather than on the Zone being queried or the number of Zones relevant to the query.
We tested this directly by querying the exact same 41 Zones on the exact same floor, with everything else unchanged:
- ~4.3 s/call when the project contained only that floor (41 Zones total)
- ~55–60 s/call after adding three additional floors elsewhere in the same project (increasing the total project Zone count)
The query still targeted only the same 41 Zones on the original floor.
This suggests that limiting the query scope to a subset of Zones (for example, using OnActualFloor) does not avoid the performance cost on larger multi-floor projects. Each individual call remains expensive, apparently due to processing related to the overall project size.
With projects containing several hundred Zones, querying every Zone individually can therefore take hours.
## Feature request
Would it be possible to extend GetZoneBoundaries so that it accepts a list/array of zoneElementIds and returns the boundary results for all requested Zones in a single call?
This would allow clients to batch the requests and potentially avoid paying the current per-call overhead hundreds of times.
## Question
If a batch-capable alternative to GetZoneBoundaries already exists somewhere in the Archicad JSON API or Tapir that can provide the same neighbouring-zone information (connectedElementId / neighbouringZoneElementId), we'd be very interested in using it.
Based on our research so far, however, GetZoneBoundaries appears to be the only mechanism that exposes this specific neighbouring-Zone relationship.
Any guidance on an existing alternative, or consideration of adding batch support to GetZoneBoundaries, would be greatly appreciated.

title: Add Discord issue bot and monthly release automation
body:
Two pieces of project automation, both running entirely on GitHub Actions (no hosted server needed).

## Discord issue bot

Watches the project's Discord channels for messages that read like a **bug report** or a **feature request**, files each one as a GitHub issue, and replies to the Discord message with the created issue's number and link.

- `tools/discord-issue-bot/discord_issue_bot.py` — one-shot poller: fetches recent messages of the configured channels over the Discord REST API, asks Claude (through the Claude Code CLI on the Pro/Max subscription) whether each is an actionable Tapir bug report or feature request (casual chat, questions and help requests are ignored), creates a labelled issue (`bug`/`enhancement` + `discord`) with a summary, the quoted message and a link back, then adds a ✅ reaction and replies with the issue number.
- `.github/workflows/discord_issue_bot.yml` — runs it every 30 minutes; manual dispatch has a **dry run** option that only logs classifications.
- Duplicate-safe twice over: messages carrying the bot's own ✅ reaction are skipped, and issue bodies embed the Discord message ID, which is searched (and author-verified) before creating a new issue. Confidence threshold, minimum message length, a per-run issue cap and a daily cap across runs guard against noise and floods; borderline classifications are collected on a rolling "Borderline Discord reports" issue.
- Setup (bot token, channel IDs, Claude Code OAuth token) is documented in `tools/discord-issue-bot/README.md`. Until the secrets are configured, runs exit quietly, so merging first is harmless.

## Monthly release workflow

`.github/workflows/monthly_release.yml` automates the [wiki Release process](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/wiki/Release-process) on the 1st of every month (or manual dispatch):

1. Skips when there are no commits since the last release tag.
2. Checks the generated docs were updated since the last release whenever the Add-On sources changed (regenerating needs Archicad, so a stale `docs/archicad-addon` fails the run with instructions; a manual run can override with `skip_docs_check`).
3. Tags HEAD with the current version from `tools/package_info.json` (the sources already carry it, per the project convention).
4. Dispatches the two existing release pipelines on the tag and waits for all artifacts. They must be dispatched explicitly because a tag pushed with the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger on-push workflows — hence the added `workflow_dispatch:` trigger on `archicad_addon.yml` and `grasshopper_plugin.yml`.
5. Publishes the draft release with auto-generated notes once every artifact is built. A build failure stops the run before publishing and before any version change; the tag stays for investigation.
6. Increments the patch version via `tools/update_version.py` and commits "Update version after release".

The yak deploy step is additionally guarded with `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')` so a manual dispatch on a branch can never publish an untagged build to the Rhino package manager, plus `updateOnlyUnreleased` on the draft-release steps so a stray dispatch on a shipped tag cannot mutate the published release.

## Verification

- Both scripts/workflows YAML-validated; the bot ships with an offline unit test suite (`tools/discord-issue-bot/test_discord_issue_bot.py`, 33 tests against stubs — no Discord/GitHub/Claude access needed) covering the classifier normalization, sanitizers, dedupe/borderline lookups, retry behavior, pagination and config validation.
- The version bump step was rehearsed on a copy of the real files: 1.5.9 → 1.5.10 propagates byte-identically into `AddOnVersion.hpp`, the `.csproj`, `TapirGrasshopperPluginInfo.cs` and the yak `manifest.yml`.
- Not exercisable in CI from this PR: a live Discord run (needs the secrets) and a full release cycle (needs a tag). Recommended first steps after merge: run *Discord Issue Bot* manually with **dry run** checked, regenerate the Add-On docs (the docs check will otherwise stop the first scheduled release — see the open review thread), and note that if `main` has branch protection blocking direct pushes, the release workflow's final version-bump commit needs an exception for `github-actions[bot]`.

title: The most expensive failure class: parameters and payloads that are accepted and silently ignored
body:
**Environment:** AC28 (Win, GER), builds from release 1.5.8 up to current main, live as-built modelling on a real ~300-element model plus scratch-project verification.

This is a meta-issue with collected evidence: the costliest failures in automation practice are not rejected calls but **accepted calls that do nothing** — `succeeded: true`, no item error, and the model is unchanged or only partially changed. The client then debugs the wrong end (its own payload, geometry, permissions).

### Collected cases (each live-verified)

| Command | Field / situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateSlabs` / `ModifySlabs` | `holes` in 4 of 5 plausible shapes (bare coordinate array, `{"polygons":[…]}`, nested arrays, `[{"coordinates":[…]}]`) | accepted, discarded — only `holes:[{polygonCoordinates:[…]}]` works |
| `ModifySlabs` | hole polygon outside the slab outline | accepted, silently dropped (`success:true`, hole missing on readback) |
| `ModifySlabs` | `polygonOutline` sent without `holes` | accepted — and the **existing holes are deleted** (the modify replaces the whole polygon memo) |
| `CreateRoofs` | `thickness` | accepted, tool default applies (back-computed 0.345 from two calibration roofs at two angles) |
| `CreateStairs` | `stepNum`, `treadDepth`, `riserHeight` | accepted, ignored (#425) |
| `ModifyRoofs` | `level` (builds ≤ late Aug) | `succeeded:true`, bounding box unchanged — current main at least returns an honest per-item error for single-plane roofs, which is the right direction |
| `DeleteAttributes` | delete a composite (`attributesToDelete`, correct shape) | `succeeded:true`, attribute still there — had to be removed by hand |
| GDL parameters | `ac_*` prefix | `success:true`, no effect (only `gs_*` are writable) |
| `CreateOpenings` | one call with several items | `elements: []`, no error, nothing created (one-per-call works) |
| `SetClassificationsOfElements` | `classificationItemId` without `classificationSystemId` | `succeeded:false` with an **empty** error message |

### Suggestions, in descending payoff

1. **Strict schema validation on nested objects** (`additionalProperties: false` everywhere, not only at the top level). A mis-shaped `holes` entry should return `4002`, not silence.
2. **Effectiveness feedback per item**: name the fields that were actually applied — or the ones ignored. A field the add-on cannot apply (`thickness` on roofs) belongs in a `warnings[]` array on the response.
3. **Call level must not report clean success when items failed** — at minimum an aggregated `itemsFailed: n` next to `succeeded`.

Items 1 and 3 alone would have saved the majority of the time lost in the live sessions. Some of this already moved in the right direction on current main (the `ModifyRoofs` per-item error) — this issue is the collected rest, so it can be triaged as one class instead of ten single reports.
author: weltmaister

title: Feature request: fields[] filter on GetDetailsOfElements — batch reads can hang minutes on payload-heavy elements
body:
**Environment:** AC28 (Win, GER), Tapir 1.5.9-era builds, real ~300-element model and scratch projects.

### The measurement

On one instance, a single `GetDetailsOfElements` with **10** elements hung for **more than 9 minutes** (300 s client timeout, call never returned), while **30 single-element calls** completed in **576 ms total**. `Get3DBoundingBoxes` with 40 and even with 5 elements timed out the same way. On other builds/instances (AC26/1.5.3, AC28/1.5.4-dev) batches of 25–45 were stable — so it is instance/model-dependent, and clients now have to probe batch-vs-single at session start.

A related extreme: `GetElementsByType {elementType:"Stair"}` blocked reproducibly (>200 s) in a model with 4 stairs, while Wall (224), Slab, Door (61), Zone (47) answered in milliseconds — and `SetDetailsOfElements`/`GetPropertyValuesOfElements` on a **single** stair hung too. The HTTP server itself stayed responsive (an unknown command returned "not found" instantly), so Archicad-side work is the bottleneck.

### The request

A **`fields[]` (or exclude-) filter on `GetDetailsOfElements`**, so a client can deselect expensive payload parts — the prime suspect here is `floorPlanPolygons`, which is always computed and returned since #437 even when the caller only needs a thickness or a layer index. The attribute detail reads already have this kind of opt-in granularity; this would bring element reads in line.

Benefits: verification loops (read-back after every mutation, which the silently-ignored failure class makes mandatory) stop paying for polygon extraction they never use, and batch reads would likely become viable again on the affected instances.

Happy to benchmark any build on AC26/AC28 with the 1-vs-10-vs-30 matrix above.

title: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection: allow one continuous chain across multiple section elements
body:
### Use case

I am dimensioning building sections for German working drawings (Ausführungsplanung, 1:50). The main vertical chain on a section runs as one continuous dimension chain across all slabs from the foundation to the roof: slab thickness, clear storey height, slab thickness, and so on, all in a single chain at the left or right edge of the section.

With the current `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` (1.5.8) this is not possible: each `dimensionsData` item accepts exactly one `sectionElementId` plus one `preset`, so every slab produces its own tiny two-point chain. A stack of isolated per-element chains is not usable on a real drawing, the essential dimensions (the clear heights between the slabs) are missing entirely.

### Suggestion

Either of these would solve it:

1. Accept an array of `sectionElementIds` per chain and merge the generated preset points into one chain, or
2. Expose explicit `witnessPoints` for section databases, analogous to what `CreateAssociativeDimensions` already offers on the floor plan.

### Technical note

From reading the sources: `BuildSectionAssociativeDimensionPoints` already produces a `GS::Array<AssociativeDimensionPoint>` that `PopulateAssociativeDimensionMemo` consumes independently of the source element. Merging points from several section elements into one chain therefore looks feasible without touching the dimension creation itself, the limitation appears to be only in the input schema and the per-item loop.

### Related

Support for elevation dimensions in sections (`dimAppear = APIApp_Elev`, currently hardcoded to `APIApp_Normal`) would complete automated section annotation, spot levels are the second half of every section markup. Happy to open a separate issue for that if preferred.
